## Game passes: kits add their own GPU passes (TopGun Tom request 1, 2026-10-30)

Chris (2026-10-30): TopGun Tom's work comes first; its request 1, `game-gpu-passes` (CORE_REQUESTS 2026-10-29), is the key unlock for that game. Built ahead of its filed stage (Stage 8) on that instruction, as a first slice. docs/GAME_PASSES.md.

- **One system, the existing graph.** A game pass is a `PassDesc` in the same `RenderGraph` as the engine passes and evani-fx effects (owner `game`), ordered by the same read/write rules and the same `order` tie-break; a game target is a graph target of the new kind `TargetKind::Game` (feature `game-passes`), which the renderer's game-pass code allocates, as the particle system allocates its `Buffer` target. Compute passes use the existing `PassKind::Compute` (`game-passes` turns on `compute`). No parallel scheduler.
- **Why not `PostEffect`.** The effect interface stays as it is (one sampled input plus depth, fixed target formats, a hand-filled 64-word uniform, `&'static` WGSL): it fits engine effects. Games need several inputs per draw, compute, 3D textures, fixed LUT sizes, history copies and their own formats, so game passes get their own small GPU module (`gpu/frame/game_pass.rs`) with one bind group layout per pass, built from the pass's declared inputs.
- **The kit writes only `pass_main`.** The engine composes the module: a fixed header (`EngineFrame`: inverse view-projection, view-projection, camera and time, sun, tier index, output size, frame number, history parity, ambient, background; `samp`, `samp_wrap`, `data`), one binding per input, a `param_<name>()` accessor per parameter, and the full-screen vertex stage or the compute entry point (8x8x1 for 2D, 4x4x4 for volumes, bounds-checked, `textureStore` of the returned value). So bindings never drift from the layout, and a kit can't forget the bounds check.
- **Live by construction.** Every pass parameter is a registered param `kit.<id>.<pass>.<name>` (plus bool `.on`), marked `gpu`, packed into a 16-`vec4` uniform (f32s share a `vec4`, vec3s start on one); the live tools, sweeps and bakes see them with no extra code.
- **Reading your own output.** A full-screen pass that lists its output as an input (heat haze reading `hdr` while drawing into it) reads a copy taken just before its draw; engine colour targets gain `COPY_SRC` only with the feature.
- **Tier behaviour.** `min_tier` (off below, catalog order) and per-tier scales of screen-sized game targets; a pass reading a game target whose writers are all off goes off too, so a gated writer never leaves a reader sampling stale texels. The active tier index is in the frame uniform for passes that pick their own step counts.
- **Errors become tools.** `add` / `add_target` refuse a bad declaration at build with a `fix:` line (17 cases tested by name); `game_pass::check` (feature `game-passes-check`, kit tests) compiles the graph and validates each composed module with naga; `cargo xtask check` reports an ERROR for a kit that uses `game_pass::` without that test or without the feature in its dev-dependencies (tools/evani-guide/src/game_passes.rs). In the browser a pipeline that still fails is logged once and skipped.
- **Dependency.** naga `=30.0.1` (already the dev-dependency pin) becomes an optional dependency of evani-render behind `game-passes-check`, so kit tests can validate game-pass WGSL; kits list it only under `[dev-dependencies]`, so it never reaches a download.
- **Zero bytes for everyone else.** Every engine change is behind `game-passes` and written on existing lines (same line count, code after the existing tokens), so panic locations and the compiled code of games without it are unchanged; the example passes are behind the example kit's own `game-pass-demo` feature, never in an `evani.toml` (the sandbox `game-pass-proof` hook follows later).
- **Left for later** (docs/GAME_PASSES.md "Not in this first slice"): geometry passes with their own vertex shaders and depth testing (terrain), engine shaders reading game targets (the `atmosphere` and `volumetric-clouds` rows), CPU texture uploads, MRT outputs, and live WGSL swaps of a pass.

## Ground textures: texture layers for the kit material hooks (TopGun W3, 2026-10-30)

- **What.** evani-render feature `kit-textures` (implies `kit-material`): two texture-array sets (0 ground, 1 hero; up to 16 layers; `ah` = albedo sRGB + height, `nra` = normal XY + roughness + AO), a game-written RGBA8 macro array with engine mips, a wrap sampler (anisotropy by tier) and a clamp sampler, and per-layer ready words, bound at group 1 bindings 16 to 23 next to `kit_data` in the forward, shadow, AO-depth and cascade passes (one layout, so one kit WGSL compiles everywhere; `KIT_SHADOW_PASS` tells them apart). docs/GROUND_TEXTURES.md.
- **Owner's picks (2026-10-30, via the orchestrator): biplanar mapping, hex-tiling and texture arrays; not height-based layer blending, not painted splat or weight maps.** The engine builds none of the blending: layer choice and weights stay in the kit's code (TopGun's height blends live game-side). The proof kit uses world-XZ on flat ground, biplanar on steep faces and hex-tiling on the near band only. Ideas from Inigo Quilez (biplanar) and Mikkelsen 2022 (hex-tiling) and MDN's WebGPU limits; no code copied (licences unknown or CC-BY-SA).
- **Arrays, not an atlas**: hardware wrap, per-layer mips, correct anisotropy, dynamic layer index; 5 sampled textures and 2 samplers added to the fragment stage (about 8 and 5 of WebGPU's default 16 in the forward pass).
- **Files**: plain KTX2 per layer, map, tier size and device format (`<path>_ah.<size>.<astc|bc7|rgba>.ktx2`; `rgba` at half size), no supercompression (the server compresses on the wire, as for models). Loads start only once the tier has settled. Sets come from `kit-textures.json` (the same file the check reads) or code; code wins per set.
- **Macro `write_rect`**: per-frame safe; covered pending writes are dropped; mips are rebuilt on the GPU over the rect's parent texels only (a scissored 2 x 2 bilinear pass per level).
- **Converter** `cargo xtask convert-textures` (tools/evani-convert/src/groundtex.rs): our own Kaiser-windowed sinc mips (wrap addressing, albedo in linear light), renormalised normals with Toksvig roughness, AH/NRA packing, our own RGBA KTX2 writer, ASTC/BC7 by the pinned `ktx` tool fed our levels. Photo inputs decode through the pinned sharp tree. No new dependency.
- **Errors become tools**: `cargo xtask check` (evani-guide `groundtex.rs`) errors on a set missing a tier, a tier's file missing in a shipped format, a file the engine would refuse, a tier over its download budget, kit WGSL over the 60 KB shader cap, and a manifest without the feature; the runtime reports a forward module over 60 KB in the ErrorLog.
- **Count-neutral hooks**: every hook in a shared file (lib.rs, kit_material.rs, gpu/kit_material.rs, gpu/pipelines.rs, gpu/mod.rs, gpu/frame.rs) is appended to an existing line or swaps a `cfg` on its line, new code is in new files, so games without the feature keep their panic locations and bytes.
- **Proof**: `examples/ground-textures`, a game outside the engine workspace (as TopGun Tom is) with three original procedural layers (rock, field, paving).

## Ground textures W3c + W3d: streaming and the app-dir converter (TopGun W3, 2026-10-30)

- **W3c streaming: two waves, one swap per set.** A set's optional `boot` size loads first for every wanted layer (bound as each pair lands), then the tier size into a second pair of arrays; the set swaps to them in one go once every wanted layer is in, and the boot arrays are freed. Picked over per-layer LOD clamping (bind one full-size array and clamp each layer's mip until its top levels arrive): WGSL samplers can't clamp per array layer, so that needed a per-layer gradient scale in every kit sample call, a contract TopGun's code would have to follow everywhere. Picked over filling a full-size array's top mips by upsampling the boot file: BC7 / ASTC can't be render targets. Cost of the pick: the tier wave downloads whole files (the boot's levels again, 0.4 % for 64 px under 1024 px) and the boot arrays live alongside until the swap (1/16 of the memory or less). The rules are a pure CPU plan (`kit_textures::SetStream`), tested natively; the GPU side only runs it.
- **`kit_tex_ready` fades**: 0 to 1 over `fade_s` (default 0.5 s) of render time once a layer shows; same WGSL contract (it was 0 or 1). Render-only, so wall-clock time is fine (the simulation never reads it).
- **Per-layer wants and a hold**: `want(set, layers)` (a mission fetches the 8 to 10 of 16 layers it uses), `hold_full` (boot sizes only, e.g. until take-off; sets without a boot size load as usual), `boot_done` (tier settled and every wanted layer shows), `stage` per layer, `loaded_bytes`.
- **Tier settings stay in the game's manifest** (`size`, `anisotropy`, and new `macro` per tier), not the engine's `assets/tiers/*.json`: those are shared by every game and compiled into each download, so a game's texture sizes there would change every game's bytes. The game reads `macro_size_for(tier)`; the engine never resizes the macro it writes.
- **No Cache Storage layer**: the browser HTTP cache already keeps the files (as for models); the spec's "second launch downloads nothing" needs long cache headers on the host, not engine code.
- **W3d converter for games outside the engine**: `cargo xtask convert-textures --app-dir <app>` (layer list from the app or its game folder, output to `<app>/assets`); `"source": {"folder": ...}` finds Poly Haven and ambientCG map names (largest file per map, OpenGL normals over DirectX ones, which are flipped, `_arm` packs for AO and roughness); a per-layer stamp (settings, sizes, formats, input file sizes and times, converter version) skips unchanged layers (`--force` redoes them); boot sizes are written. Supercompression stays off (DECISIONS above: the server compresses on the wire).
- **Errors become tools**: the check now errors on missing boot files, a start download over `boot_budget_mb` (default 4 MB, TopGun's blocking budget), and kit textures over half a tier's `max_texture_memory` (models share the rest).
- **Zero bytes for everyone else**: every change is in files compiled only with `kit-textures` (`kit_textures.rs`, `gpu/kit_textures.rs`) or in native tools; no shared runtime file changed. Proof (rustc 1.99.1, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=65e8497`): ship builds of sandbox (a `kit-material` game) and 2d-platformer against Join 19 (e5609525): every downloaded file the same (sandbox 28 of 28, 2d-platformer 4 of 4); only `build-facts.json`, the statement beside the download, differs in its commit label. Checks on the branch: `cargo xtask check` and `check --full` clean; `check --app-dir examples/ground-textures/apps/ground-textures` clean (its known geocheck warning). Shots: `.evani/shots/w3/` (boot vs full, a 3 Mbit/s line at 5, 9 and 28 s, `want=rock`); the netlogs show the boot files first and no paving fetch under `want=rock`.
- **No new dependency.**

## Incremental mesh upload (2026-10-30, TopGun Tom request)

- **Problem.** Every add or replace in the `MeshLibrary` rebuilt and re-uploaded the vertex and index buffers of every mesh; streaming terrain, rock and vegetation chunk LODs paid the whole library each time.
- **Layout.** One shared vertex buffer and one shared index buffer stay (one `set_vertex_buffer`/`set_index_buffer` per pass, no bind group or shader change). `mesh::MeshStore` (CPU, no GPU types) places each mesh in both with a first-fit, lowest-offset free list that coalesces neighbours, so the same sequence of changes always gives the same layout and the same writes. Built-ins are placed first and never move.
- **Change rules.** Add: write that mesh's two ranges. Replace not bigger in both buffers: write in place and free the tail. Replace bigger: free the old block, take a new one, write it. Remove: free both ranges and the slot. A mesh with no triangles or an index past its vertices owns no range and draws nothing. `MeshLibrary` keeps a revision per slot, so the renderer and the cull bounds find the changed slots without a change log (and several consumers can follow one library).
- **Growth policy.** First sync sizes each buffer to a power of two over the built-ins plus the library's meshes, at least 4096 vertices (96 KiB) and 16384 indices (64 KiB), so a game that builds its meshes once never grows. When a block does not fit, the buffer doubles (or grows to what the mesh needs if that is more) with one `copy_buffer_to_buffer` of the old contents, submitted before the writes of that frame. Buffers never shrink; fragmentation is absorbed by the free list and by doubling, not by moving meshes (ids and ranges of live meshes are stable). Cost of the simplest policy: a free list that has room only in pieces smaller than a new mesh grows the buffer, using at most about twice the live bytes plus the largest hole.
- **Cost.** A frame with no library change: one revision compare, no allocation. No new dependency.
- **Measured** (`cargo test -p evani-render --features meshes mesh::store -- --nocapture`): with 40 meshes of 60 vertices and 40 triangles in the library, one add uploaded 111,168 B before and 1,920 B after (58x less); a same-size replace of a 60-vertex mesh in a library of 5 uploaded 48,048 B before and 3,120 B after. The tests assert the drop and print the figures. A growth copy uploads nothing from the CPU: over 60 adds with two doublings the CPU wrote exactly the meshes' own bytes once.


## Join 16 request: kit_data 4 MB -> 32 MiB (TopGun Tom, 2026-10-30)

- **Request.** TopGun Tom (a jet game on Evani.Dev) needs 16 to 32 MB of `kit_data`: its land map uses 3.2 MB of the 4 MB cap and the village, field-parcel, building and tree tables need more. It blocked their look-match.
- **How it worked.** `kit_data` is one read-only storage buffer (not a uniform) at group 1 binding 15, only with the `kit-material` feature. It started at 16 records and doubled; `MAX_DATA` = 2^18 records (4 MB) was a soft cap that only truncated the upload and logged a note. It was not a hardware limit: the device is created with the full limits of the adapter (`required_limits: adapter.limits()`), and WebGPU guarantees a storage binding of at least 128 MiB.
- **Pick: raise the cap, no second buffer.** `MAX_DATA` = 2^21 records = 32 MiB, in the one buffer, same binding, same WGSL, same API. A second buffer would add a binding, a bind group and a WGSL name for no gain at this size. 32 MiB is a quarter of the guaranteed minimum, so it binds on every adapter, phones included; the per-device cap is also clamped to `max_storage_buffer_binding_size` and `max_buffer_size` (`device_max_records`) in case an adapter reports less.
- **Pay only for what is used.** The default allocation is unchanged (16 records, 256 B). Growth is the old powers of two up to 4 MB (so every existing game allocates exactly what it did), then whole MiB steps (a 5 MiB table takes 5 MiB, not 8) up to the cap. Games without `kit-material` compile none of this; the download does not change.
- **Errors.** Over the cap, the renderer still keeps the first records (backward compatible) but now logs an `error` (was a `note`) naming the count, the cap and the fix. New `KitMaterial::set_data` returns `KitDataError` and keeps the old data, so a kit finds out at once.
- **Tests (errors become tools).** In `kit_material.rs`: write and read back at `MAX_DATA - 3` and exactly `MAX_DATA` records; the over-cap `set_data` error and its message; the upload plan (`plan_upload`, the code the GPU path uses, so the test covers the real sizing); allocation steps; small-device caps.
- **Known cost.** A data change re-uploads the whole buffer, so at 32 MiB a table should be written once. A partial upload is still the suggested follow-up (see the sky note above).
- **No new dependencies.**

## Join 22: main-line check fixes (2026-10-31)

The game-passes join (b5a36275, a fast-forward with no join number) went in with its checks not all clean. This join proves the main line and fixes what was wrong. Nothing in a download changed.

- **`check --full` on b5a36275: clean** (exit 0, 100 min, all eight games' tests and ship builds). `--full` has no clippy step (see the 2026-10-16 note on quick mode), so lint errors do not show in it; that is how the first two below got through two joins.
- **Clippy, three errors, all real, none from game passes.** `tools/evani-convert/src/groundtex.rs` needless_range_loop (ground textures, Join 19, b2592bfe); `crates/evani-render/src/kit_material.rs` test int_plus_one (kit_data 32 MiB, Join 16, 68e4d6c2); `crates/evani-render/src/gpu/kit_material.rs` useless `u64::from` on the web target (same commit, Join 16; only a wasm32 clippy sees it). Fixed in place, each on its own line so no later line number moves. Found by `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --keep-going` and `-p evani-render --lib --all-features` natively and for wasm32, plus the kits for wasm32. The mesh-slots and game-pass code had no lint errors.
- **`msdf.rs` re-export.** `pub(crate) use evf_err` is used only by the web code (`gpu/msdf.rs`); a native build with `msdf` saw it as unused (since S3-13a, 2026-10-17, not from any join). Now `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]` on the same line.
- **The two `base-building-rts` test failures were not a regression.** `modules_match_features` and `finds_one_toggle_per_compiled_effect` compare `cfg!(feature = "bloom")` with the effects the world really has. `check --quick` ran every chosen crate in one `cargo test -p a -p b ...`, so cargo built `evani-fx` once with the union of the features: `evani-bench` and `evani-live` (dev-dependency) turn on bloom and vignette. The tests are as old as the kit (2026-10-20), `quick.rs` as old as 2026-10-16, `evani-live`'s dev-dependency 2026-10-14 and the bench's features 2026-10-15; no join since Join 14 touched them. They pass in `--full` (the app alone) and failed in quick whenever a render change pulled in the bench or the live tools. Reproduced by running quick over everything since Join 14 (56 files, 31 crates).
- **Fix in the tool, not the tests.** `check --quick` now runs `cargo test` as one command for the libraries and tools and one command per game app together with its kits (`quick::test_batches`, unit-tested), the pairs `--full` tests. Per-app alone is not enough: the model-view kit's tests need the `models` module its app turns on, so a kit tested without its app failed (found while trying that). Re-run: quick over the same 56 files is clean (31 crates, clippy ok, tests ok).
- **Byte proof.** Ship builds of all eight games at Join 21 (82525157) and at the fixed head (b5a36275 + this join), same rustc 1.99.1, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=8252515`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1`, `--no-diff`: all 16 files (js and wasm) have the same SHA-256 and size, and the same hashed file names. So game passes, ground textures, mesh slots and these fixes add nothing to a game that does not list them.
- **Suggested, not done:** a clippy step in `check --full` (about 40-60 s when warm) would have caught the lint errors at join time. It changes the documented split of the two gates, so it waits for Chris.

## `[modules] materials`: a game lists its material families (2026-10-22)

- **Why.** The material families (`evani-material-layers`, `-nature`, `-proc`, and evani-render's character pass) were optional crates and features, but `evani.toml` had no way to switch them on, so a ship build (always `--no-default-features`) carried none. The material-view game is the first game that needs them.
- **What.** `[modules] materials = ["layers", "characters", "nature", "playground"]` (any subset, duplicates fold, an unknown family is an error). Each entry turns on the app feature `material-<family>`; the game's `Cargo.toml` says what that feature pulls in. Both readers know it (xtask's `Manifest` and evani-guide's `Modules`); `build --ship` reports each family's size like any other module (`without_each`), the size base drops them all, and the published build facts list them.
- **Bytes.** Nothing changes for a game that does not list it: no existing game does, so their features and ship builds are as before.

## material-view: a game for viewing and tuning materials, the home of Evani.Materials (2026-10-22)

- **Why.** Chris: "rather than making a new tab, maybe we should just view this in the Evani Dev. That's what it's for. So we just build a game to view materials." Research: `.vibedeck/research/2026-10-22-material-viewer-look-dev-scenes-for-a-phone-and-de.md`; the approach picked was Filament's gltf_viewer and material sandbox (Google, Apache-2.0).
- **Borrowed from Filament (ideas only, no code copied, so no notice entry).** (1) The tuning panel is generated from the registered parameter list (`library::panel_rows`, `apps/material-view/src/panel.rs`), so a live edit moves the sliders and a slider move is a live edit under the same `material.*` names the Look Lab and AI use. (2) The quality switches sit in one Quality section (tier chips, the family's quality params, a frame-time readout). (3) A small fixed set of lights (`data/lights.json`: Studio, Overcast, Sunset, Night lamp) plus a sun drag and a turntable, under the procedural sky; no HDR download.
- **What.** `apps/material-view` and `kits/evani-kit-material-view`. Six scenes (shader ball, cushion, head, ground patch, pool, lamp corner), each drawn only by its family's scene module, compiled in only when evani.toml lists the family. The data (scenes, families and presets, the param grouping keywords, lights, and the 24 world rooms from `.vibedeck/plans/world-kit-materials.md`) is JSON in the kit. Compare copies the view with the saved values (A) into an overlay canvas clipped at `kit.material_view.split`; where a browser cannot read the WebGPU canvas back it falls back to holding a button to see A.
- **Bytes.** No new dependencies. Existing games are untouched (their ship builds keep the same SHA-1, the join-5 byte proof).

## material-view: art styles, test shapes and streamed models (2026-10-23)

- **What.** A new family `styles` (app feature `material-styles`, listed first in `[modules] materials`): the scene shows the open art style's starter materials on a chosen test shape (sphere, monkey, cube, long box, prism, cylinder, ring, teapot), one row when the view is wide, two columns when it is tall, with a glowing disc under the selected one. The styles and their draft presets are kit data (`kits/evani-kit-material-view/data/styles.json`), tuned live through `kit.material_view.style.*`; a style that isn't made yet draws only the ground and the page says so.
- **`model-replace` (evani-render, opt-in).** `Models::replace_glb(id, bytes)` swaps an in-memory model's bytes in place (the old version draws until the new one is on the GPU). Why: every roughness, metallic, bump or glow edit rebuilds that place's GLB, and adding a new model per edit would grow the table without end. The colour is a live tint, so it needs no rebuild unless the material glows. Only material-view turns it on; no shipped game does, so their downloads are unchanged.
- **`/dev-refs/` in the live bridge (dev only).** Reference screenshots for each style live in git-ignored `art-source/style-refs/` on this PC. Only the dev bridge serves them; no build copies them, so a ship or published bundle never holds third-party pictures, and a page served any other way shows "no reference pictures".
- **Model sources.** Monkey: Khronos glTF Sample Assets IridescenceSuzanne (CC0 1.0, (c) 2022 UX3D, (c) 2021 Pascal Schoen), mesh only, its material stripped. Teapot: the Utah teapot from the University of Utah's own page ("Download OBJ File", the 1987 Frank Crow version), whose terms allow any use including commercial. Both went in through `cargo xtask convert` and stream through the manifest; credits in `apps/material-view/CREDITS.md`.
- **Test head streams.** The character scene's test head moved from `include_bytes!` into `assets/models/char-head*.glb` (through `cargo xtask convert`, which kept its `evani_kind` tags: four tiers, 111 to 454 KB, instead of one 1.1 MB file in the wasm), streamed with `models.handle("char-head")` and a pale ball while it loads, so the viewer's wasm holds no model files (a test checks no `include_bytes!` is left in the app).

## Material catalogue batch 1: design (2026-10-24)

Chris approved batch 1 (106 materials, all 29 recipes) plus the 60 optional vehicle and fantasy / sci-fi materials (166 in all) on 2026-10-24. Full design: `docs/materials/BATCH1_BUILD_PLAN.md` sections 2 to 4. Filed in STAGES.md under Stage 3 (opt-in extension of the shared materials library); no gate box.

- **One new opt-in crate, `evani-material-recipes`.** It holds the material block format, the recipe stage WGSL, 8 condition layers (wet, mud, dust, snow, wear, oxide, growth, blood) and the `material.quality.*` groups. The four existing families (layers, character, nature, proc) are untouched. Each recipe has one backend in `catalog/materials/recipes.json`: the new crate, or an existing family.
- **32-byte material block.** Recipe code, variant, extras mask, condition mask, three sRGB8 colours, ten u8 numbers, an FNV-1a seed byte and 8 default condition amounts. It travels in the glTF material's extras (`extras.evani_recipe`, 64 hex characters) next to plain PBR factors, so a game downloads only the numbers of the materials its models use. Shader code is per cargo feature (`recipe-<name>`, `cond-<layer>`), chosen from `evani.toml` `[materials] recipes` and `conditions`.
- **No tier file changes.** The planned `material_quality` field in `assets/tiers/*.json` is dropped (it would change all 8 games' bytes); the crate keeps its tier table in code, like `material.layers.quality`. Recorded change from CATALOGUE_PLAN section 5.2.
- **Quality and switches.** `material.quality.<group>` (detail, fur, water, glass, skin, foliage, conditions, reflections) take auto, lite, low, medium, high or ultra; turning down only swaps in the light version. Family groups drive the family's own param by name. Every switch is a registered `material.*` or `kit.material_view.*` parameter.
- **Fur stays painted in batch 1.** Real 3D fur shells stay filed under Stage 8 until Chris says otherwise.
- **Branches.** Engine work on `matcat-engine` (worktree `Evani.Dev-matcat-engine`, from m1-foundation at 65e84978, with `material-catalogue` merged); viewer work on `matcat-viewer`, later.
- **Byte proof.** The 8 existing games (2d-platformer, base-building-rts, kart-racer, match-3, model-view, sandbox, tactical-fps, top-down-action-adventure) must stay byte-identical, wasm and js. Baseline built in P0 at 65e84978 with `rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13)`, `cargo 1.99.1`; the stable toolchain was last updated 2026-10-22 23:15 (`~/.rustup/update-hashes`). Files are in `.evani-tmp-matcat/` (not committed). If the toolchain changes, rebuild the baseline before the next proof.

- **P1 material catalogue data and block (2026-10-24).** New opt-in crate `evani-material-recipes` (no game lists it; no new dependency, `serde_json` is already pinned and only the dev feature `catalog` pulls it in). `catalog/materials/recipes.json` and `materials.json` are the master from now on; the CSV is regenerated from them (`tools/materials/import_csv.mjs export`). The 32-byte block is fixed by BATCH1_BUILD_PLAN 2.2; the seed is the low byte of FNV-1a 32 of the id.

- **P2a recipe stage core and patch (2026-10-24).** `evani-material-recipes` gains `shaders/core.wgsl` and `src/shader.rs`: text only, no new dependency (naga `=30.0.1` and the engine crates are dev-dependencies for the tests). The patch rewrites five exact lines of `model_lit_fs` or `model_layered_fs` (frame before the discard, `mat_surface` after `occ`, `mat_extra` before fog), each also holding on the character-patched text (one edit takes `let base` or `var base`); a missing line returns `None`, so the stage draws plain PBR. Edits are confined to the patched function's body. Choices the plan left open: `MatIn` also carries the stage's current `base`, so recipe 0 returns it unchanged; `MatOut`'s post-light inputs are fixed as `emit`, `sheen` (rgb + rim power) and `glint`; the per-frame uniform (binding 13, 64 bytes) is two `vec4<f32>` of global condition amounts, `misc` (quality levels 4 bits each, sim time bits, off bits, reserved) and 128 extras **deny** bits, so an all-zero uniform is a safe default; extras take consecutive global bits in the `STAGE` table order (45 in all, paint included); a recipe with no quality group (glow) uses `detail`. The dispatch and the condition pass are generated from `COMPILED` and `LAYERS`, empty until P3 and P4 add cfg'd rows.

- **P2b recipe stage in evani-render, sandbox proof (2026-10-24).** New evani-render feature `material-recipes = ["look-surface", "dep:evani-material-recipes", "evani-material-recipes/engine"]`, off with `relief`; no new external dependency (evani-core is already in the workspace; the recipe crate gains feature `engine` for its live switches). Choices made:
  - **Same-line wiring only.** gpu/models.rs, model.rs, lib.rs, gpu/mod.rs and gpu/pipelines.rs gain cfg'd additions on existing lines (no line moves, so panic locations and every shipped byte stay put). The 8-game ship proof printed `same` for all 16 files.
  - **Text built natively.** `model::recipes::patched_forward(msaa)` (the forward module through the character patch when `char-materials` is on, then the recipe patch, layered when `material-layers` is on) is what gpu/recipe_material.rs caches per sample count, so the native tests check exactly what the pipelines compile. The recipe template is asked first; if it returns `None` the character template or the engine's own is used and the overlay log gets one note.
  - **Live block edits** go through a world resource, `model::recipes::BlockEdits::set_block(model, material, &Block)`, applied at the next frame (the GPU module is private, so the plan's `set_block` lives there as the public face; a model not yet on the GPU ignores an edit).
  - **Family mirror** runs only when a `material.quality.*` group changes (so start-up changes nothing): `skin` sets `material.character.quality` (-1, 0..3), `detail` sets `material.layers.quality` (auto, cheap, full). The nature family has no quality param, so water, glass and foliage mirror nothing yet.
  - **Extras names** (`shader::EXTRA_NAMES`, 21 rows, held equal to recipes.json by a catalog test) give `material.recipe.<recipe>.<extra>`; registered only for compiled recipes (none in P2b).
  - **Tests moved.** The P2a naga tests now live in `crates/evani-render/tests/recipe_wgsl.rs`; evani-material-recipes dropped its engine dev-dependencies (no dev-dependency cycle).
  - **Core cost.** The recipe core WGSL is stripped at compile time (comments, indentation, blank lines; `shader::wgsl_strip`, `CORE_STRIPPED`), the per-model block list is a plain Vec. Measured with two sandbox release builds through trunk (wasm-opt -Oz, gzip -9): `lit-proof` 292,895 B vs `lit-proof` + `evani-render/material-recipes` 300,417 B, so **+7,522 B (7.3 KiB)**, about 350 B over the plan's 7 KB. Recorded rather than cut further: what remains is the stage WGSL (~2.4 KB gzip), the five patch edits and the spec'd switches, mirror and live edits. A later trim (shorter WGSL identifiers in core.wgsl) can win it back if wanted.
  - **Proof scene** (`recipes-proof`, never in evani.toml): five shapes from the existing layer fixtures, their glTF materials rewritten in code to carry catalogue blocks (leather.saddle_tan, wood.walnut.stock, fit.button.brass, stonework.marble_floor, gem.ruby; a test holds each equal to the catalogue's encoding). No recipe is compiled yet, so they draw their plain colours through the recipe stage's identity.

- **P3 condition layers (2026-10-24).** The eight layers of plan 2.4 (wet, mud, dust, snow, wear, oxide, growth, blood) as `shaders/cond_<layer>.wgsl` in evani-material-recipes, one feature each (`cond-<layer>`, each turning on an internal `conditions` feature), stripped at compile time. They run on every recipe-stage material after its recipe (Bevy's ExtendedMaterial order, ideas only, no code), never as separate materials. No new dependency. Choices made:
  - **Binding 13 grown, not a binding 14.** One change moved `FRAME_BYTES` (64 to 128), the `RecFrame` struct (four more `vec4`: `ka`..`kd`, the layers' look numbers), `frame_words` and the buffer; tests hold the WGSL struct size, the Rust word count and every look number's word against each other. Cheaper than a 14th binding (no layout, bind-group or pipeline change, one buffer write per frame as before).
  - **Contract extended:** `cond_<layer>(b: RecBlock, a: f32, o, i, f, nz)`; the block is passed so wear can show paint's colour B and oxide a metal's colour C.
  - **Live switches** (registered only for compiled layers): `material.cond.enabled`; per layer `material.cond.<layer>.on` (the RDR2-style toggle), `.amount` (global; a material's own default wins if larger) and its look numbers (`wet.puddles`, `wet.puddle_scale`, `mud.ground`, `mud.height`, `mud.color`, `dust.cavity`, `dust.color`, `snow.angle`, `snow.frost`, `wear.edge`, `wear.scratches`, `oxide.strength`, `growth.color`, `growth.scale`, `blood.age`). The plan's `material.cond.*` names were kept over the brief's `material.layer.*`, which would sit next to the layers family's `material.layers.*`.
  - **On/off, quality limit and light version on the CPU:** `conditions::apply` rewrites each block's condition mask byte to its strongest allowed layers (lite 1, low 2, medium 4, high and ultra 8; lite keeps only wet, dust and snow, drawn as tints), only when the rule changes, so the shader never sorts and a layer that is off costs no GPU work. Medium adds normal edits (puddles, mud, snow), High sparkle (snow) and scratches show from Medium.
  - **Fix carried from P2b:** the GPU side took `try_res_mut::<ParamRegistry>` while the frame holds a shared borrow, so it always fell back to defaults: no recipe switch (quality, extras, now conditions) reached the GPU. It now reads with `try_res`; the family quality mirror moved to its own Update system. New check `crates/evani-render/tests/gpu_param_borrow.rs` fails on any GPU module that borrows the registry mutably.
  - **Proof:** `recipes-proof` turns on all eight layers; the five catalogue materials carry a variant with their own amounts (leather wet + mud, walnut dust, brass wear + oxide, marble snow), and a front row of nine test balls shows each layer alone, then all eight. `?q=<level>` sets `material.quality.conditions`. Captures (headless, muted) at Lite, Low and High: `.evani/shots/p3/`.
  - **Sizes** (sandbox `--no-default-features`, trunk release with wasm-opt -Oz, gzip -9; base `lit-proof` 292,893 B): core `+material-recipes` 300,528 B (**+7,635 B**, P2b was +7,522: the grown frame, the mask plumbing and the mirror system, offset by a tighter compile-time strip); all eight layers 305,069 B (**+4,541 B**, within the 5 KB budget). Standalone per-layer WGSL, gzip -9: wet 342, mud 354, dust 317, snow 431, wear 415, oxide 351, growth 363, blood 350 (1,342 together in one stream; the rest of the layer cost is the switches and the mask code). A first measurement showed the mask code reached even with no layer compiled (+9,405 B core); it is now behind `conditions` and `conditions::ACTIVE`, so a game with no layer pays nothing for it.
  - **Core trim:** `wgsl_strip` now also drops spaces beside punctuation (never between two words or two operator characters), about 100 B gzip on the core WGSL. The core stays about 470 B over the 7 KB line; the next mechanical step, shorter WGSL identifiers, would rename the helpers recipe packages call (`rc_*`, `MatIn` fields), so it is left for a decision rather than done here.
  - **Checks:** `cargo xtask check` clean; clippy -D warnings native and wasm32 on evani-render (recipes alone, with layers and character, with skinning, with all layers, with one layer, and without), evani-material-recipes (none, engine, engine with all layers, one layer) and the sandbox (default, recipes-proof); the 8-game ship proof printed `same` for all 16 files (EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=65e8497, rustc 1.99.1).

- **P4 recipes: metal, wood, stone, ceramic (2026-10-24).** The first four recipe-stage recipes, each its own feature (`recipe-<name>`) and `shaders/rc_<name>.wgsl`, stripped at compile time and listed in `shader::COMPILED` (cfg'd) and `ALL_RECIPES` (tests, tools). Written fresh; Voronoi and noise come from the core (Quilez's write-up as the idea, never Blender's GPL file). No new dependency. Choices made:
  - **Core overrun kept (decided before P4):** the readable WGSL names (`rc_*` helpers, `MatIn` fields) stay; P3's ~470 B over the 7 KB core budget is re-weighed in P15 (a line under P15 in the plan says so).
  - **Shared helpers in their own file:** `rc_shared.wgsl` (`rc_out`, `rc_near`, `rc_tuv`, `rc_tw`, `rc_bump`) is appended only when a recipe is compiled, so the core stays as P3 left it and a game with no recipe pays nothing.
  - **Normals without vertex tangents:** each recipe takes a finite difference of its own height function (two extra evaluations, Medium and up, within 25 m) and tilts the normal in a cotangent frame built from the derivatives `mat_frame` already took (`rc_tuv`), or two world tangents for world-space stone (`rc_tw`). No recipe takes a derivative.
  - **Levels:** lite returns the light version (plain metal-rough; two-tone grain, planks keep their layout and tone; flat two-colour noise; one gloss lobe); low draws every pattern, anti-aliased to its average under 1.5 px; medium adds normals (hammered dents, cast pits, engraving grooves, raised late grain, plank and tile bevels, stone grains) and the stone rim and glaze depth; high adds stone glints, the blended two-plane projection and 2-step parallax within 8 m; ultra parallaxes stone everywhere.
  - **Schema rows in Rust** (`src/recipes/<name>.rs`, `BUILT`), held equal to `recipes.json` by a test, so tools know each slot without parsing JSON; plain constants, so nothing reaches a game that doesn't read them. The step list for P5 to P9 is the doc comment of `src/recipes/mod.rs`.
  - **Live switches:** a recipe's engine-level tunables are its extras (`material.recipe.<recipe>.<extra>`, registered by themselves for each compiled recipe, default on, each moving one deny bit of binding 13) and its quality group (`material.quality.detail`); the per-material numbers stay in the block (`BlockEdits::set_block`), as plan 2.6 has it. A sandbox test checks every P4 switch is registered and reaches the GPU words.
  - **Catalogue numbers:** 23 rows got `params` (the 21 batch-1 metal, wood, stone and ceramic rows, plus fit.button.brass and stonework.marble_floor, which the proof shows); 21 are `ready`. The plank deck (no nail heads in the recipe) and the chequered marble floor (stone has no chequer; masonry or the model must give it) stay `planned`. The CSV export is unchanged (it holds no numbers).
  - **Fixes found by looking:** polished stone looked lumpy, so stone grain normals now scale with roughness; tiles are 8 x 8 per uv; the brass button's engraving scale is 20.

Sandbox build pair (`--no-default-features`, trunk release with wasm-opt, all 8 layers on, base 305,072 B): all four recipes **+7,093 B (1,773 B each, within the 2 KB class M budget)**; metal alone +4,941 B, so the first recipe also switches on about 2.5 KB of one-off plumbing (the extras switches, their names and the dispatch, dropped by the optimiser while no recipe is listed). Recorded for P15 with the core overrun.

- **P5 recipes: bark, masonry, plaster, ground (2026-10-24).** Four more recipe-stage recipes on the P4 pattern: one feature each (`recipe-bark`, `recipe-masonry`, `recipe-plaster`, `recipe-ground`), `shaders/rc_<name>.wgsl` stripped at compile time, rows in `shader::COMPILED` (cfg'd) and `ALL_RECIPES`, schema rows in `src/recipes/`. Written fresh (Quilez's cellular-noise write-up and the usual height-field parallax as ideas only; no code taken, no new dependency). Choices made:
  - **World or uv space:** masonry, plaster and ground are world-space (`rc_proj` to Medium, `rc_proj2` blended from High; rows follow world height), so a cube or a slope shows no seam. Bark is uv-space so it follows a trunk: u runs round, v along, furrows run along v, and u is mirrored (triangle wave, period 2) so a trunk's uv seam shows a mirror line, never a cut. A truly periodic noise would need a core change; filed for later.
  - **Patterns:** masonry bond rows from a hash per row (running bond, stack, setts, ashlar) and cellular stones (cobble, flagstone); plaster trowel marks are the contour lines of a noise, cracks the bisectors of a warped cellular noise gated by a slow noise; ground stones are the nearest cells (parabolic domes) over noise soil with a sand ripple and sparkle grains; bark furrows and plates are F2-F1 ridges, peel strips the contour of a slow noise.
  - **Levels:** lite is the flat pattern; low draws everything anti-aliased to its average; medium adds normals (joint bevels and domed stones, trowel ridges, stucco stipple, air holes and cracks, stone, ripple and clod relief, furrow relief) within 25 m; high adds the blended projection, sand flecks in plaster, sparkle in ground and 2-step parallax within 8 m (masonry joints, ground pebbles, bark furrows); ultra parallaxes everywhere.

- **P6 recipes: leather, fur, hide, keratin, and two fixes (2026-10-24).** Four more recipe-stage recipes on the P4 pattern: one feature each (`recipe-leather`, `recipe-fur`, `recipe-hide`, `recipe-keratin`), `shaders/rc_<name>.wgsl` stripped at compile time, cfg'd rows in `shader::COMPILED` and rows in `ALL_RECIPES` / `BUILT` (now 12, in code order), schema files in `src/recipes/`. Written fresh. ShellFurGodot (Arnklit, MIT; read in a read-only clone at `.evani-tmp-matcat/prior/`, nothing run, no code taken, so no THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES) is the idea source for fur only: a coat painted from a base colour to a tip colour, darker at the roots, per-strand and per-lock variation, a pattern layer, a translucent rim. We build fresh and paint (Chris chose "Build fresh" on 2026-10-22). Choices made:
  - **Fur** is uv space (hair flows along the flow angle; pattern space x along the hair, y across). Variants: solid, stripes (bands across the flow), spots and rosettes (cells), patches (fbm threshold), dapple (soft rings). Strands are stretched noise, locks the cells of a second cellular noise (wool is mostly lock shade and lock normals). Points (dark legs, socks, muzzle) come from the thin convex parts of the model (`f.curv`), not a uv mask, so they follow any model without a map. The sheen is a Kajiya-Kay-style term: the hair tangent (from `rc_tuv`) against the view scales the rim written to `o.sheen` for `mat_extra`. No shells; the `shells` extra (default off) is reserved for a later shell pass and, if on, only softens the painted strands. One pass at every level (a text test checks the WGSL has no entry point, binding, texture read or discard, adds none to the stage, and that the Lite branch returns before any strand work); Lite is the painted coat, pattern, points and rim.
  - **Hide** is wrinkles only: ridged noise (plain, wrinkled, slick), domes of a cellular noise (warty), blotches of a second one, wetness as a lower roughness and darker colour, wrap scatter as a rim tint. **Leather**: F2-F1 pebble grain, larger F2-F1 creases, suede's nap as a velvet rim, rawhide's blotches, tooling as a diamond lattice; wear lightens the pebbles. **Keratin**: growth rings are a sawtooth along v (wobbled), bone and antler add fibres and grooves, horn darkens to its tip, shell mottles, edge translucency is a warm rim, nacre a thin-film hue by view angle.
  - **Levels:** lite is the flat painted version (fur keeps its pattern and rim); low adds the strands, grain, rings and blotches anti-aliased; medium adds normals within 25 m (fur lumps and fibres, hide wrinkles, leather grain and creases, keratin rings and grooves), the rims, suede's nap and nacre; high adds a finer second layer (fur strands, hide wrinkles, leather creases, keratin striations); ultra draws as high.
  - **Catalogue numbers:** 30 rows got `params` (all `ready`): the 17 batch-1 rows (horse.coat.bay, horse.coat.grey_dapple, horse.coat.palomino, cattle.coat.black, sheep.wool.white, dog.coat.tan, cat.coat.tabby_brown, bear.coat.brown, wolf.coat.grey, fox.coat.red, trim.fur.sheepskin, frog.green, leather.saddle_tan, leather.suede, antler.bone, beetle.black, teeth.healthy) plus tiger, leopard, cheetah and giraffe (stripes, rosettes, spots, patches), elephant.hide and toad.warty (wrinkled, warty), leather.rawhide and leather.tooled, horn.cattle, bone.fresh, grip.stag, beetle.green and clam.shell, to show the other variants. Left `planned`: deer.coat.brown (batch 1; needs a white belly and tail, a body-region mask no recipe has yet), and every other fur, hide, leather and keratin row, whose numbers wait for the batch that shows them (no new recipe code needed).
  - **Proof:** `?set=p6` (30 shapes: fur, leather and hide on a uv sphere, keratin on a horn cone or a sphere, in four rows), `?set=p6&shape=cube`, `?row=<n>`, and a new `?yaw=<degrees>` that turns every grid shape (brings a seam to the camera). The sphere and the horn are built in code (no new asset). `?q=` now also sets the fur and skin quality groups. The sphere's uv seam faces away from the camera; a uv pattern on any model has its artist's seams, and fur patterns here are not periodic (only bark is).
  - **Fix 1, pottery:** three of the four P4 ceramic rows read as plain white balls. Now: (a) a pooling term (two scales of 3D noise, scaled by the drip number) sways the glaze between thick and thin; thick glaze runs deeper in colour (creamy brown for earthenware and stoneware, cool blue-white for porcelain, enamel and tile); (b) porcelain gets a warm translucent edge (`o.sheen`, medium and up); (c) enamel chips: the dark body shows in irregular flakes, mostly on convex edges (enamel has no crackle, so its crackle amount and scale mean chips); (d) tiles get a per-tile tone and wider grout, and the proof draws the tile on a cube (a real uv square; the ball's uv is a degenerate map). Numbers: tile drip 0.25; porcelain drip 0.6; enamel chips 0.45, scale 10, drip 0.1. Porcelain is still white, as its name says; it now has a soft cool mottle and a warm rim instead of a flat white.

The noises sample a circle (3D value noise on cos/sin of the turn, so any scale fits), the cellular cells wrap at a whole number of cells around (the furrow count is rounded to a whole number, at least 2), and the triangle wave and the sign flip in the normals are gone. Side effect: the oak's cell borders are slightly softer (3D value noise sits nearer the middle; stretched 1.3x in contrast to compensate) and the plate size rounds to a whole number around. The P5 bark pictures change; nothing else does (no shared code touched).

- **P7 recipes: feather and scales (2026-10-24).** Two more recipe-stage recipes on the P4 pattern: `recipe-feather` (code 13) and `recipe-scales` (code 14), `shaders/rc_<name>.wgsl` stripped at compile time, cfg'd rows in `shader::COMPILED`, rows in `ALL_RECIPES` / `BUILT` (now 14), schema files in `src/recipes/`. Written fresh (no outside code; the plan names no research pick for these two). Their `recipes.json` rows and extras were already in the catalogue, so no schema change. Choices made:
  - **Scales** (uv space): cells of the core's hex lattice (`rc_hex`: alternate rows offset by half a cell), cut by a round-to-hex radius (`shape`); overlapping scales are shingled (the two scales one row up lie over this one, so the visible edge is a round arc, with a lighter rim on the free edge), hex tiles have no gaps, plates are square aligned rows, bumps are domes of random height. The pattern kind follows `pattern_scale` and cross-fades: a diamond chain (to 8), blotches (8 to 18), bands across v (18 to 30), speckles (30 up), so the four existing numbers carry four looks without a new slot. Relief is a finite difference of the scale height; the shimmer (extra bit 1) is a hue by view angle that differs scale to scale, with a sheen rim at medium and a one-scale-at-a-time glint at high. The cell count round u is a whole number (scale size is rounded to 1/N), so a ball or trunk shows no seam in the scales; the pattern layer is not periodic.
  - **Feather** (uv space): feathers are the same lattice stretched along v, each an ellipse lying over the next row (only rounded tips show), with a raised shaft, barb stripes slanting away from the shaft towards the tip, a darker overlap edge, and four variants: plain (barring laces the tip edge), barred (bands that follow the tip's curve), speckled, eyed (rings round a point near the tip: outer ring brighter, middle ring the iridescent hue, core the barring colour). Iridescence (extra bit 0) is a thin-film hue by view angle written as a base tint and a sheen rim (medium), plus a glint (high). Edge relief (extra bit 1) is the finite difference of dome, lip and shaft plus an analytic barb ridge slope. Feather size is rounded like the scale size.
  - **Levels:** lite is the flat pattern (scales) or the flat barred colour (feather); low adds the cells and the barbs, anti-aliased (cells and barbs under 1.5 px fade to their average); medium adds the relief normals within 25 m, the shimmer and iridescence with their sheen; high adds per-scale ridges and the glint (scales), a finer second barb layer and the glint (feather); ultra draws as high.
  - **Catalogue numbers:** 33 rows got `params` (all `ready`): the 4 batch-1 rows (snake.rattle, trout.skin, crow.feather, eagle.feather.brown) plus rows that show every variant: fish and snakes (salmon, carp, sardine, koi, python, black, green, leather.snake), lizards (iguana, chameleon, gecko, tortoise), plates (alligator.belly, sturgeon), bumps (alligator.back, crocodile, beaded lizard, horned lizard) and plumage (owl barred, pigeon, dove, peacock, swan, quail, hummingbird, turkey, woodpecker, bluejay, sparrow). Left `planned`, with the reason: snake.garter and snake.banded (a stripe along the body and a three-colour ring need a stripe mode and a fourth colour; the recipe has one pattern colour and bands across v only), mackerel (wavy lines), and every row whose look is a body-region mask (white belly, black head, wing bars, coloured fins: no recipe has a region mask yet); the other feather and scale rows wait for the batch that shows them (no new recipe code needed).

- **P8 recipes: gem and ice (2026-10-24).** The last two see-through fakes of the glass quality group, on the P4 pattern: `recipe-gem` (code 25) and `recipe-ice` (code 27), `shaders/rc_<name>.wgsl` stripped at compile time, cfg'd rows in `shader::COMPILED`, rows in `ALL_RECIPES` / `BUILT` (now 16), schema files in `src/recipes/`. Written fresh; no outside code (the plan names no research pick). Their `recipes.json` rows, extras and `STAGE` rows were already in the catalogue, so no schema change. No real refraction in either (the nature pass's glass is the see-through). Choices made:
  - **Gem** (no uv needed): the normal is split into facets by a cellular noise over the normal itself (plus a little uv, so a flat face still splits). Each facet gets its own tilt, brightness and slot on a rainbow ramp that turns with the view (dispersion); a thin dark seam sits between facets. Five variants: brilliant (a crush of small facets), step (square rings of flat steps, the emerald cut), cabochon (one smooth cell, so a single highlight ring), raw crystal (cells stretched along the point), amber (smooth, with bubbles instead of inclusions). The one environment read is the lit stage's own, through the faceted normal and a roughness that clarity raises (a recipe may not sample textures). Fresnel rim and the per-facet sun-lit sparkle (extra bit 0) and the emissive core (inner glow, extra bit 1) go in `o.sheen`, `o.glint` and `o.emit`. Facets fade to their average once under 1.5 px, measured from the normal's change per pixel (`curv` times `world_px`) plus the uv rate.
  - **Ice** (world space, like ground and stone: the pattern lies on the plane facing the dominant axis of the normal, two planes blended from high, so ground, slabs and props need no uv; a prop that moves swims through its pattern): a blue-white ramp by view angle (light rim, deep blue where you look through, milkier as clarity drops), a frost cover of fbm (needle streaks for the frost variant), cracks as the F2-F1 lines of a cellular noise (extra bit 0), at high a second, deeper crack layer that slides against the surface with the view (2-step parallax, the view's in-plane part taken in the same projection), crack groove and frost grain normals within 25 m (two planes blended, so no seam at the axis switch), sparkle specks that wink for a narrow band of view angles (extra bit 1), a wrap scatter in `o.sheen` (extra bit 2) and, for the icicle variant, rings along the vertical.
  - **Levels** (the glass group, not detail): lite is a tinted gloss with one sparkle band (gem) and white with a blue rim (ice); low adds the facets' brightness, seams, inclusions and glow (gem) and the ramp, one crack layer and the frost (ice), anti-aliased; medium adds the facet normals, dispersion tint and Fresnel rim (gem) and the crack and grain normals and the scatter (ice); high adds the per-facet sparkle with the rainbow flash (gem) and the deeper crack layer and the sparkle (ice); ultra draws as high.
  - **Catalogue numbers:** 21 rows got `params` (all `ready`): ten gems (ruby, garnet, sapphire, emerald, diamond, amethyst, clear quartz, amber, jade, rock salt: all five variants) and eleven ice rows (fresh snow, packed snow, slush, dirty snow, lake ice, glacier, ice cube, icicle, frost, sea ice, snowball: all four variants). The separate things a snow or ice look note names (tracks, heaps, a geode body, the grimy speckle of dirty snow, which the dust and mud layers draw) are geometry, decals or condition layers, not recipe work, so those rows are `ready`. Left `planned`, with the reason: gem.opal (flashing colour patches need a hue pattern at patch scale; a cabochon is one cell), gem.magic_crystal (the pulse needs a time term: P9's glow recipe), ground.snow.crust (wind ridges are a relief the recipe lacks), ground.ice.sheet_road (a thin invisible glossy layer needs alpha, not a surface), ice.frozen_waterfall (ribs run down the column; the icicle ripple rings round it).
  - **Proof:** `?set=p8` (21 shapes in four rows: cut gems, crystals and soft stones, snow and ground ice, ice props), `?set=p8&shape=cube`, `?row=<n>`; the pointed crystals and the icicle ride on a cone, the ice cube on a cube, the rest on the uv sphere. `?q=` now also sets `material.quality.glass`, the group these two recipes follow (it did not before, so low and lite looked like high in the first pass). The front-row ruby now carries its catalogue numbers (its block string in `ITEMS` changed with them).
  - **Seen** (headless, muted, `.evani/shots/p8/`; judged honestly): at high the ruby and sapphire read as faceted stones with sharp white sparkles and a faint rainbow, the garnet as a darker, busier version, the emerald as a green stone with square step rings (a first draft was a tile mosaic and was changed to rings), the diamond as a clear, grey-white faceted ball with pastel flashes (a first draft was rainbow confetti; dispersion on the base colour was cut), the amber as honey orange with cream bubbles and a soft highlight (a little flat), jade as a smooth waxy green, rock salt as pink-white broken crystals, the amethyst and quartz points as pointed prisms with a sheen. These are crushed-facet stones, not a true brilliant cut; the facets are random cells, not radial. Ice: the lake reads as dark clear ice with white cracks, the glacier as deep blue with faint cracks, the cube as clear blue ice with cracks at two depths (the deeper ones shift as the view moves), the icicle as a blue spike with rings. Snow, packed and dirty snow, slush, frost and the snowball read as soft white to grey balls with a fine grain and tiny winking sparkles: they look like snow at a distance but give little to see close up (no clumps; the recipe has no snow-specific relief). At low the gems keep their facet colours but go smooth (no facet normals, no sparkle) and the ice keeps cracks without the second layer; at lite the gems are tinted glossy balls with one highlight ring and the ice white with a blue rim. A first pass of the sea ice showed short straight slashes at the edge where the world plane switches (the crack normals read one plane); the normals now blend two planes as the colour does. The P7 pictures read as named (fish as shingled overlapping scales, feathers as rounded overlapping tips, the peacock with blue eyes, the rattlesnake with dark diamonds): no fix needed.
  - **Limits:** gem facets are cells in normal space, so they follow the normal, not the model: on a real faceted model the geometry's facets and these sub-facets combine; on a ball the facets cluster at the poles of the mapping. Ice is world-space (a moving prop swims). Snow has no relief of its own beyond grain.

Sandbox build pair (`--no-default-features`, trunk release with wasm-opt, all 8 layers on, the fourteen P4 to P7 recipes 319,511 B gzip, 738,463 raw): + gem 576 B, + ice 690 B, both +1,293 B (320,804 B; one stream, shared helpers already in).

Their `recipes.json` rows, extras and `STAGE` rows were already in the catalogue, so no schema change. Written fresh; no outside code (the plan names no research pick). No new dependency. Choices made:
  - **Snow close-up detail (the P8 weak spot), in the ice recipe.** At medium and up, for rows with frost above 0.3 (snow, frost, snowball; slush and ice are untouched): a fine grain and soft clumps (value noise and two-octave fbm, in the height function as well as the colour, so they tilt the normal; clumps bluer in the hollows); at high, glints that follow the light: each 6 mm world cell is a grain with a random tilt, and it flashes (a round dot) where its mirror direction meets the view, using the half vector of `frame.light_dir` and the eye, so they move as the sun or the camera does (the old sparkle winked on view angle only). Grain fades once finer than a pixel (`rc_aa_world`), clumps fade with distance (`rc_near`). Lite and low draw as before. Ice standalone gzip 1,102 to 1,377 B (budget 2 KB). Film (pearl, colour-shift, soap film): a cosine hue palette by view angle, scaled up for colour-shift. Twill (carbon): a two-over-two weave in uv (tow profile, warp and weft shading, a fine thread line at high, tow normals at medium). The `clearcoat` extra off leaves a satin finish (rough at least 0.45), so a game that has no layers family still has a switch.

The mirror is of the time-driven scalars, not of the pixels (a pixel test needs a GPU).

- **P10a row to glTF, family adapters and paint's clear coat (2026-10-24).** The adapter (`evani-material-recipes` feature `gltf` = `catalog`, dev and tools only; never in a game) and the coat the P9 block already carried. No new dependency (the three families and evani-gltf are dev-dependencies of the crate's tests only; evani-material-nature reaches evani-render with `forward` only, so no feature cycle is compiled). Choices made:
  - **Two routes to a block.** By name: a glTF material whose `extras.evani_material` is a catalogue id is filled by `gltf::apply_catalog` (P10b's convert will call it). By value: `gltf_material(cat, row)` then `gltf::apply` (code-built meshes, the viewer). `apply` replaces only what the adapter owns (`evani_recipe`, `evani_layers`, `evani_cloth`, `evani_kind`, the character records and six KHR extensions) and keeps textures, names, alpha mode and other extras; an unknown id is an error and changes nothing. `.glb` helpers `glb_parts`, `glb_build`, `glb_with_material`.
  - **What a row writes:** PBR factors (colour A linear, `rough`, `metal`) and `evani_material` always; `evani_recipe` for recipe-stage rows (paint included); cloth: `KHR_materials_sheen` plus the same numbers in `evani_layers` and `evani_cloth` (the loader reads the extras; a code-built mesh skips the converter, so both are written), weave plain for plain and twill, knit for knit, none for pile and satin, fuzz as the family's wrapped subsurface; metal with `aniso` above 0: `KHR_materials_anisotropy` plus `evani_layers` (drawn only where `material-layers` is on); skin, hair, eye: `evani_kind` and the family record (scatter = undertone, wrinkles x2, pore scale; highlight and shift; iris colour and pupil), with redness and the hair root baked into the base colour because the family has no field for them; foliage, thin, glass, water: the nature pass's `evani_kind` plus the transmission extensions it falls back on. Family numbers are the row's own block values decoded over their ranges, so block and family data cannot disagree.
  - **Change from plan 2.1: paint's clear coat is the recipe stage's.** `rc_paint_coat` draws it after lighting from the block's `coat` and `coat_rough`: a GGX sun lobe (Kelemen visibility) and a sky reflection on the geometric normal, taking their Fresnel share from what lies under them. It runs through a generated `rc_post` hook that `mat_extra` now calls (`mat_extra(c, ro, n, g, v, l, sun_rgb, vis)`, patch edit 5); with no paint compiled `rc_post` returns the colour unchanged. Live: `material.recipe.paint.clearcoat` (existing on/off) and new `material.recipe.paint.coat_strength` (0-2, frame word 11 as strength minus 1, so an all-zero uniform draws the authored coat). Tiers: lite folds the coat into the base roughness (paint's "one gloss lobe"); the sky reflection follows `material.quality.reflections` (none at lite). Why: a game listing paint needs no layers family (about 7.2 KB less), a live block edit moves the coat, and the coat switch now really removes it. The adapter writes no `KHR_materials_clearcoat` for paint; P10b's convert must not turn one into `evani_layers` on a paint material (a second coat in a layered game), and `paint` maps to `recipe-paint` alone.
  - **Colour-shift check (P9 weak spot).** The rings were not banding or aliasing: the hue cycled 1.2 times round the colour wheel from face-on to the edge, so a ball showed repeated bands. Colour-shift now sweeps once over half the wheel, faster towards the edge (pearl and soap film keep their thin-film rings, which are right for them). Before `.evani/shots/p9/row3-high.png`, after `.evani/shots/p10a/colourshift-after-high.png` (a smooth purple-to-blue flip).

It is on the P15 list as an open decision.

## Material catalogue batch 3, B3-P1: the shared pattern layouts (2026-10-24)

Batch 3's first package (`docs/materials/BATCH3_BUILD_PLAN.md` 3.1 and B3-P1, on the material-catalogue branch), built on branch `b3-patterns` from `matcat-engine` (batch 1 P10b). Recipe crate only: no evani-render source, no game, no new dependency. Written fresh for Evani.Dev; no outside code.
- **One shared layout helper, its own build-time feature.** `shaders/rc_layout.wgsl` (feature `layout`, stripped at compile time like every recipe) returns a unit cell (`LayCell`: edge distance, the unit's id, where the point is inside it, its direction or chequer colour) for running, stack, setts and ashlar bonds, herringbone, basket weave (the chequer is the basket with one unit a block), hex and shingle courses (each course over the one below, jittered free edges, the lap for a shadow), and draws panels, studs on a lattice, a row of studs round a unit (rivets; corners share their stud), riveted plates, stripes, crossing lines and a painted motif (a seeded rosette or star with 4 or 8 arms, a per-tile hand-painted wobble, corner quarter circles that join into circles). It is appended once after `rc_shared` when a compiled recipe calls an `rc_lay_` function (`shader::uses_layout`); `recipe-metal`, `-paint`, `-wood`, `-stone`, `-masonry` and `-ceramic` turn `layout` on, so a game with none of them downloads none of it. `stage_wgsl_with` (tests and tools) takes it from `ALL_LAYOUT`; `patch_lit` and `patch_layered` now call `stage_wgsl` directly, so a game build can only reach the feature-gated text.
- **CPU mirror under tests** (`src/layout.rs`, pure functions no game calls): every tiling covers the plane with no gap or overlap and its edge distance is continuous across joints (it changes no faster than the point moves, over 19,600 points per layout; a wrong unit at a joint would jump); a unit keeps one id over its face; exactly one herringbone strip holds each point and the lookup searches it (ratios 2 to 6); shingle courses lie over the one below; the bonds equal batch 1's masonry maths for every point (`the_bonds_are_masonrys_old_maths`); and the shader's function list equals the mirror's.
- **Masonry's bonds moved into the helper unchanged** (plan risk 4): `?set=p5` before and after is pixel-identical below the debug text, high and low. New masonry variants 6 herringbone and 7 basket (units unit-height wide, round(unit width / unit height) widths long; herringbone rows turned 45 degrees so the zigzag runs along the wall or path).
- **Opt-in extras, appended, for the batch-1 gaps and the plan's first users:** wood `studs` (bit 2: nail heads, two across each plank at joists in straight lines, a rust stain, domes from medium), stone `tiles` (bit 3: square slabs, each its own cut of the stone; numbers `tile_size` 0.1-2 m and `chequer` 0-1: dark slabs take colour C veined in A), metal `studs` (bit 3: riveted plates 2 by 1 over the new number `layout_scale`, seams, rubbed heads with a dark ring), paint `studs` (bit 4: rivets and seams under the paint, number `stud_scale`), ceramic `motif` (bit 2: one painted motif per tile, petals and corners in C, centre in A). The bit and slot numbers follow the plan's (wood studs 4, stone tiles 8, metal studs 8, paint studs 16, ceramic motif 4), so P4 to P8 extend these rather than redo them.
- **Every existing block is unchanged.** The new extras default off in `recipes.json` and the new numbers default to their stored 0 (layout_scale and stud_scale 1, tile_size 0.1, chequer 0), so a row opts in by naming them: encoding all 1,054 rows before and after differs in exactly the 11 rows below. The global extras bits renumber (45 to 50: metal, paint, wood, stone and ceramic gained one each), which only moves later recipes' `RC_X_` constants; the live switches `material.recipe.<recipe>.studs|tiles|motif` register by themselves (default on).
- **Tiers:** lite draws the layouts flat (the chequer and its joints, plate seams, the motif), faded to their average from afar so nothing shimmers; low adds per-unit tone, nail heads, rivet heads and the motif's anti-aliased edges; medium adds nail and rivet domes, seam grooves and slab bevels within 25 m; high and ultra as medium (masonry keeps its parallax).

A game lists it as `"wood-layouts"` in `[materials] recipes` (it implies `wood`); `cargo xtask check` ERRORs on a model whose wood block uses variant 4 or later when the part isn't listed, with the fix. Sizes: wood without the part 1,676 B (inside 2.0 KB), with it 2,199 B (the part costs 523 B, paid only by games that draw those rows). Why a part and not a new recipe: the rows stay wood rows (same block, same code 4, same switches), so nothing in the catalogue, the converter or a model changes. **Look unchanged:** the whole `?set=b3-patterns` grid at High and Low is pixel-identical before and after the split, and the wood rows close up (rows 4, 5, 6, 11) differ only in the clock digits of the debug text (`.evani/shots/b3-woodcmp/`). ## Material catalogue P13 and P14: the viewer's library panel, search and the open material (2026-10-24)

Branch `matcat-viewer` (worktree `Evani.Dev-matcat-viewer`), plan `docs/materials/BATCH1_BUILD_PLAN.md` 2.6, 2.7, P13 and P14.

- **Where it lives.** A new viewer family `catalogue` (`[modules] materials`, app feature `material-catalogue`; `MATERIAL_FAMILIES` in xtask gains it) turns on the kit's `catalogue` feature (the library: `kits/evani-kit-material-view/src/catalogue.rs`, data/planned.json), `evani-material-recipes/gltf` + `data` (the row-to-glTF writer and the bundled JSON, dev data inside the viewer only) and the recipe stage. The viewer's `evani.toml` also lists every recipe and condition in `[materials]` (P10b), so its app crate has `material-recipes`, `char-materials`, `recipe-<name>` x21 and `cond-<layer>` x8 features wired as P10b's check expects. No shipped game lists any of it; the 8-game byte proof stays `same`.
- **Search** (P13): folded case and accents; words from the name and id, the search words, the look note; ranked exact name, name start, name/id/search words, look note; within a rank exact words before a prefix (only the word being typed) before a typo (edit distance 1 from 4 letters, 2 from 8), name matches before search-word-only ones, then by id, so the order never changes between runs. Filters (ready/planned, the recipe groups hard/soft/living/liquid and light, each condition layer, "in the engine today", category, subcategory, batch) combine with the search; the tree's ready/total counts follow the search and filters (all 1,054 rows: CATALOGUE_PLAN section 2's counts, tested).
- **Planned rows** show greyed with a reason: data/planned.json (reasons recorded by P4-P10a and the P15 list), else "Planned for batch N", else the family's or a default line. They are not options of `kit.material_view.cat.open`, so neither the page nor an AI can open one.
- **One control API.** Opening a row is the enum param `kit.material_view.cat.open` (`none` + every ready id); the shape `kit.material_view.cat.shape`; per material `kit.material_view.cond.<layer>.on` / `.amount` (16, registered at start), `kit.material_view.extra.<recipe>.<extra>` and `kit.material_view.mat.<number>` (registered the first time a row of that recipe opens; a shared number name takes the open recipe's range). The page sets the same params, so an evani-live `param_set` and a click are the same edit. Opening a row sets every switch to the row's values; a condition is on only if the row lists it (others are ignored even if switched on). The panel also shows the engine's global `material.cond.<layer>.amount` ("weather on everything") and `material.quality.<group>` for the recipe's groups.
- **Drawing** (P14): the open row takes the styles scene's place, in the open style. Styles without a shape look draw the shape's glTF material written by `gltf_material` from the edited row, so the recipe stage (or the family: cloth through layers, skin/hair/eye through the character pass) draws it exactly as a game's model would. A switch on a recipe row only rewrites binding 12 through `BlockEdits::set_block`: the model is not rebuilt (tested by the build counter) and no pipeline is. A family row (no block) rebuilds its one model in place (`replace_glb`).
- **Styles on catalogue materials: the plan's rule.** Shaped styles (toon bands, outlines, pixel and voxel blocks, facets...) draw their treat.rs treatment fed with the row's colour A mixed a third of the way to colour B, its roughness and metalness (and a glow for fire and glow rows). Recipe detail (grain, fur pattern, sparkle) does not show inside those styles until style treatments move into the engine (Stage 8 look transfer, plan 2.7 and 8.8); the review card must say so. The brief's fallback (treatments acting on the recipe's lit result) was not needed because the plan decides it.
- **Shapes.** Each recipe's `scene` in recipes.json is now filled (ball; tile for ground, masonry, plaster; cylinder for bark; card for fire; cushion for cloth; head for skin, hair, eye; nature for the nature recipes, all still planned). New shapes: a floor tile and a card (`shapes.rs`); every generated or streamed mesh gets a uv map and tangents for the recipes' uv-space patterns. The cushion and the head are the family scenes' own models (`layer-velvet`, `char-head`), keeping their own uvs; a head row fills its own part (skin, eye or hair).
- **Swatches** are CSS chips, a gradient of colours A and B (plan 2.7).
- **Phone and tablet.** The Library is the drawer's first tab: 280 px on the left on wide screens; under 760 px it opens full height from Browse and steps aside when a row opens. Filter rows and the dock's strips swipe sideways.

## Style detail: catalogue materials keep their own pattern in every art style (Chris's decision, 2026-10-24)

Branch `matcat-styledetail` (worktree `Evani.Dev-styledetail`). Chris: "Yes, keep the detail in every style": oak still reads as oak and leather as leather in a cartoon, pixel, voxel, dither or neon style.

- **Before.** Only the realistic styles (Painterly, Realism) drew a catalogue row through the recipe stage; every shaped style redrew it from its two main colours, roughness and metalness (P14's rule).
- **Engine hook, behind a feature.** `evani-material-recipes` feature `style` (turned on by evani-render's `material-recipe-style`; only the material-view app's `material-catalogue` lists it, no game does). With it, `shader.rs` rewrites two lines of the stripped core (the last line of `mat_surface` and of `mat_extra`, matched by exact text; if either is missing the plain core is kept) and appends `shaders/style.wgsl`. The step reads one word, `kd.w` of the per-frame recipe uniform, which the plain stage keeps reserved (`conditions.rs` already tests it stays 0), so no binding, buffer size or pipeline layout changes. evani-render writes it each frame from the `RecipeStyle` world resource (absent = 0 = the plain stage). Without the feature none of this is compiled and the stage text is byte for byte the old one.
- **What the step does (shared, no per-material code).** `mat_surface` runs the recipe and its condition layers as usual, then (word non-zero) turns the patterned colour (base plus emission) into a factor against the material's main colour (colour A two thirds, B one third: the same colour the treatments are built from), in stops, posterized to the style's step; keeps the pattern's own hue as far as the style keeps colour; and hands the lit stage its own values back, so a treatment's flat colour stays flat. `mat_extra` multiplies the finished colour by the factor. Modes: tone (bands, cel, toon, low-poly, clay, yarn, pixel and voxel); dither (engraving: measured against the material's first colour, so bare iron is the ground and not iron mixed with rust; a step or more darker is solid ink, so grain lines, cracks and stripes stay lines; a little darker or two steps brighter gets sparse 4 x 4 ordered dots on half the dither cell; a first version set the ink density from the darkness, which turned oak and leather into a uniform grey and rusty iron, whose main colour includes the rust, into solid ink); neon (the tone plus one glowing contour where the pattern is two steps darker or four brighter than the material's first colour: stripe rims, scale and crack outlines, rust spots; a contour at every step lit every fur hair, and measuring against the A-B mix left bare iron sitting on the contour, glittering all over). A cell size makes tone sample the pattern once per cell: the voxel and pixel styles' cubes (the viewer places a voxel model on the shader's cell grid, a shift under half a cube, and gives each cube face its cube centre's uv).
- **One recipe call, no loop.** A first version also sampled the pattern two more times a pixel apart for neon edges (screen derivatives are not allowed after the discard) and kept the plain call as a second call site: the browser's D3D12 shader compiler inlines the whole dispatch at each call, and the pipeline build went from 32 s to 374 s with all 21 recipes. The step now calls the recipe exactly once, with no loop, and neon draws contour lines instead; `style.rs` tests that the step has one call and no loop.
- **Viewer.** A recipe row in a shaped style: the treatment's surface parts carry the row's block (`extras.evani_recipe`) and a uv map (treat.rs `Part::body`; the outline and neon trim stay plain); the styles scene clears the word each frame and the catalogue scene sets it from the open style (`style_of`). Live params per shaped style: `kit.material_view.detail.<style>.strength` (0 to 2, default `render.detail`, 1) and `.step` (0 to 1.75 stops, default `render.detail_step`, 0.5), so a person or an AI turns detail up or down per style without a rebuild. A switch on a recipe row now rebuilds the treated model (its block is in the parts).
- **Moving the treatments fully into the engine (not done; Stage 8 look transfer).** It would take: the band cut, dither and outline as shader or post passes on any model instead of viewer-built geometry (a `look` style stage after lighting reading a per-look band table, ramp and dither cell; an inverted-hull or screen-space outline pass), the voxel and low-poly reshaping as an import-time or tier-time mesh step, the style word growing into a small per-look uniform (mode, step, strength, hue, cell, line colour), and kits choosing a style per material group rather than per frame. This step is the bridge: it already runs on the engine's recipe stage, so it would carry over.
- **Bytes.** Shipped games: none lists the feature; the 8-game ship proof (EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=65e8497, rustc 1.99.1, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1) printed `same` for all 16 files against the 65e8497 baseline. The viewer (the only build with it): wasm 1,942,576 -> 1,957,099 bytes (+14.5 KB raw, +5.4 KB gzip: the stripped step WGSL, the multi-part uv model writer, the voxel uv map and the 44 detail params); js unchanged.
- **Checks.** Tests: evani-material-recipes with `style` and without (4 new: both hooks land once, the word round-trips, the step is stripped, one recipe call and no loop), evani-render `recipe_wgsl` with `material-recipe-style` and every recipe and layer (the styled stage validates with naga; an unstyled material keeps its colour) and without, the kit (24), the viewer (62, 1 new: a recipe row in a shaped style carries its block on the surface parts only, sets the word, the live strength moves it without a rebuild, the realistic style clears it, voxels take one uv per cube face, dither and neon modes). Clippy -D warnings native (recipes, render, kit, viewer with and without the catalogue) and wasm32 (viewer, render with the step). `cargo xtask check`: clean.
- **Seen** (headless, muted, `.evani/shots/styledetail/`: `before/`, `after/`, contact sheets in `sheets/`, phone in `after/phone-*`): oak, leather, tiger fur, snake scales and rusty iron (oxide on, full) in all 24 styles. Before, every shaped style drew each as one flat colour (oak, leather and snake were near-identical tan balls). After, each can be told apart in every style: tiger stripes and snake blotches everywhere, per cube in Voxel, Pixel and HD-2D; oak grain strokes, leather crack cells and rust spots in the toon, cel, storybook, comic, gothic, low-poly, clay and yarn styles; ink grain lines, crack speckle and dotted rust in Dither; grain, crack outlines, glowing stripe and scale rims in Neon. Weakest: at the coarse cube sizes (Voxel 0.12, Pixel 0.16) oak's thin grain and leather's thin cracks become speckle, so those two differ there mainly by shade and speckle density; Ink brush (85 % grey) loses most of the rust's colour. The pipeline build time with all 21 recipes and the step was 64 s against 32 s before, measured on a heavily loaded PC; the step adds one recipe call's worth of code at most.
