The card was not deleted and no check was changed to hide them; the viewer was never taken through the kit process, and whether it should be (or whether viewers get their own, shorter card) is Chris's decision, put to him at the hand-over.

## Material catalogue batch 2: options for the existing recipes and the catalogue data fixes (B2-P2 to B2-P5, 2026-10-24)

Branch `b2-options` (from `matcat-engine` at 24a2ecc2; plans BATCH2 and BATCH3 committed first). Batch 2's plan (`docs/materials/BATCH2_BUILD_PLAN.md`) packages P2 (ground), P3 (stone), P4 (bark and ice) and P5 (catalogue data) built together, since all four touch the same shared lists. The new foliage recipe (P1) is another branch; P6 merges.

- **Rule: nothing earlier moves.** Every new extra is `default: false` in `recipes.json` and every new number's default sits at the bottom of its range (so it encodes to 0): all 194 earlier rows encode to the same 32 bytes, and the new variants are appended. Seen: the `?set=p4`, `p5` and `p8` sandbox captures at high and low, before (the batch-1 tip's proof page) and after, are pixel-identical below the debug overlay (`.evani/shots/b2-options/before` and `after`, compared with `.evani/tmp/b2/pngdiff.mjs`).
- **Ground** (+3 extras, +3 numbers n7 to n9): `cracks` (F2-F1 lines of a cellular noise, shaded plates, dark gaps; with `sparkle` high the plates take colour C: alkali; cracks also parallax at high), `furrows` (uv rows along u for ploughed ground; on the road variant two ruts at fixed v with edges in colour C, so wagon ruts and a trail share one switch), `cover` (cells of short strokes in colour C over up-facing faces only: forest floor, corral straw). Numbers `crack_scale`, `furrow_scale`, `cover`. No new variant was needed: the road variant is the rut switch.
- **Stone** (+4 variants porous, ropy, clastic, flowstone; +1 number `pits`): one relief function `rc_stone_r` per variant, used for colour and for the normals (so no per-variant bump code); flowstone also lowers roughness to a third. The vein scale sets the feature size.
- **Bark** (+3 variants fibrous, ringed, banded; +2 extras `marks`, `embers`; +1 number `cord_twist`): all periodic in u (strands count a whole number around the trunk; the noises are the circle noises of P6), so `?yaw=` shows no seam. `embers` writes `o.emit` from colour C scaled by the furrow mask: steady, no clock, and it switches the colour-C patches off so the burnt trunk has no glowing blotches.
- **Ice** (+1 extra `ridges`, no number): wind ridges (a slow directional sine warped by noise) in the height function, lighter and shinier on the crest; it turns the normals on even when frost is low.
- **Live switches** (default on, registered with the compiled recipe): `material.recipe.ground.cracks|furrows|cover`, `material.recipe.bark.marks|embers`, `material.recipe.ice.ridges`. The extras bits renumber (ground +3, bark +2, ice +1): total 45 to 51; the foliage recipe's three make 54. Hard-coded numbers in two `shader.rs` tests changed (fur's base 24 to 29, the last bit 44 to 50); P6 must renumber them again after merging foliage (code 20 sits between keratin and organic).
- **Catalogue data (P5).** `rock.obsidian` moves from `glass` to `gem` (raw crystal, clarity 0, dispersion 0, black, sparkle low): an opaque stone must not be drawn see-through. `ground.ice.sheet_road` ("Black ice") becomes a new status `alias`: its row is `recipe ground` with its base's conditions, `params.alias_of = "asphalt.road"` and `cond_defaults.wet = 1.0`; `Catalog::resolved` returns the base row under the alias's own id (and the alias's amounts laid over the base's), `encode` goes through it, `validate` refuses an alias whose base is missing, planned or itself an alias, that has numbers of its own, or that has another recipe or conditions. Rule: weather and wear stay condition layers. `cond_defaults` rows: sand.wet (wet 0.8), grass.frosted (snow 0.4), cave_wall (wet 0.6), stalactite (wet 0.5), mossy_boulder (growth 0.6). The catalogue still has 1,054 rows; per-recipe counts change (glass 29, gem 13, ice 13, ground 45) and the plan's section 12 table follows. The CSV has no status column, so the alias needs no new column: `import_csv.mjs` is unchanged. For the viewer (P14 and B2-P8): an `alias` row opens its base with the condition on.
- **Rows with numbers** (22, all judged ready from the `?set=b2-options` captures at high, low and lite, `.evani/shots/b2-options/`): ground cracked_dry, alkali, ploughed, wagon_ruts, trail, forest_floor, corral_dirt; snow.crust; stone limestone, travertine, pumice, lava.cooled, conglomerate, cave_wall, stalactite; bark redwood, cypress, vine_woody, palm, cherry, aspen, burnt; plus obsidian on gem. Honest notes: the cover strokes read as sparse straw and needles (the hoof prints are decals, later); cave_wall and stalactite read as smooth damp stone with faint streaks, their wet default is not in the proof (the proof's blocks carry no condition amounts); the palm's rings are soft; at lite the new variants draw their flat colour (bark: stripes, as before).
- **Sizes** (gzip -9 of the stripped WGSL, standalone): ground 1,331 to 1,923 B (budget 2.0 KB), stone 999 to 1,348 B (1.6 KB), bark 1,474 to 1,744 B (2.0 KB), ice 1,377 to 1,483 B (1.6 KB). All four inside their classes.

- **B2-P1 foliage recipe (2026-10-24, batch 2, branch `b2-foliage`).** Foliage (code 20) moves from the nature family into the recipe stage, so leaves, needles and grass take the condition layers (rain, snow, mud...). Feature `recipe-foliage`, `shaders/rc_foliage.wgsl` (stripped at compile time), cfg'd row in `shader::COMPILED`, rows in `ALL_RECIPES`, `BUILT` (now 22), `STAGE` (group foliage, 3 extras) and `EXTRA_NAMES`; schema `src/recipes/foliage.rs`. Written fresh; no outside code, no new dependency. Choices made:
  - **Backend `recipes`, `also: ["nature"]`** (the paint precedent): the adapter still writes the nature kind (turf maps to `grass`), so a game that also has the nature module keeps its placed back-light; `[materials] recipes = ["foliage"]` now maps to `material-recipes` + `recipe-foliage` only. Test `foliage_alone_reaches_no_nature_module` resolves the template app with exactly those features (`cargo tree`, wasm32) and finds no evani-material-nature.
  - **Variants** leaf 0, needle 1, grass 2, straw 3 (kept), turf 4, moss 5, litter 6 (appended). **Numbers** variation, thickness (n0, n1 kept), vein, gloss, edge_dry, blade_scale (2-200), bare, underside. Two numbers mean a second thing on some variants, documented in the schema file and shader: `thickness` is the blade width for turf and litter (above 0.66 a turf blade becomes a three-leaflet clover), `bare` is the share of berry specks (colour 2) on needles. **Extras** back_light 1, veins 2, bare 4 (live switches `material.recipe.foliage.*`, default on). Inserting code 20 into `STAGE` moves the global extras bits of organic, ceramic, gem, ice, fire and glow up by 3 (48 bits in all); everything is generated from the table and the tests hold it (the plan's renumbering hazard; B2-P6 regenerates once).
  - **Pattern space:** uv for the cards (leaf, needle, grass, straw) and moss; world space from above (`rc_proj`) for turf and litter. Leaf: midrib along u = 0.5, side veins slanting to the tip (v = 0). Needles: strands slanting off the twig with dark gaps, so an alpha card only needs the spray's outline. Turf and litter: one randomly turned tapered blade (or fallen leaf) per cell, kept inside its cell (no grid cuts), two layers, a third finer one at High; bare patches show colour C (the soil). Moss: cellular cushions with soft creases and fine fronds.
  - **Back-light** (Medium and up, extra `back_light`): the sun through the leaf, `max(-g.l, 0) * (0.9 + 3 fs)` with `fs` the forward scatter looking into the sun, times (1 - thickness), colour C (turf: colour A brightened, from the forward scatter only), into `o.emit` with the sun colour; snow on the material stops it (`rc_amount(b, 3)`). It is not shadowed (the recipe stage has no shadow lookup), so a leaf in a shadowed canopy still glows a little from behind.
  - **Underside:** the lit stage turns a back face's normal to the camera, so the recipe tells the back from the uv winding on screen (the uv Jacobian's sign flips when a card is seen from behind) and tints it towards colour C by `underside`.
  - **Not done here:** `ground.grass.frosted`'s default snow amount (`cond_defaults` rows are B2-P5's, which also updates the catalogue test that assumes none); its numbers are set, the frost comes from the snow layer in a game.

Fix found on the way: the proof's `rewrite` replaced a shape's whole PBR block and so dropped its base texture; it now merges the factors in.

- **B2-P9 real-GPU frame time (2026-10-24, batch 2).** Measured on this PC's RTX 4060 Ti: the headless Chrome adapter reports `nvidia lovelace` (not a software fallback), timestamp queries on, and the numbers are the engine's own 2 s median GPU times per pass (the overlay), sampled three times, 1280 x 720 and 1920 x 1080, bloom, vignette and shadows on (`.evani/shots/b2-p7/gpu-timing.txt`). The first sample of a page is a warm-up and is ignored below.
  - **Turf** (`?set=b2-plants&row=3`, three grass grounds filling about a third of the frame): 720p total GPU 1.0 to 1.1 ms at lite, 1.1 ms at low, 1.1 to 1.4 ms at high, 1.1 to 1.3 ms at ultra (forward pass 0.58, 0.65, 0.73 to 0.91, 0.75 to 0.87 ms); 1080p 2.2 to 2.3 ms at high and 2.0 to 2.6 ms at ultra (forward 1.5 to 1.8 ms). The turf's own cost at high is about 0.15 to 0.35 ms at 720p for that coverage, so a ground that fills the whole screen costs roughly 0.5 to 1 ms more at 720p and 1 to 2 ms at 1080p.
  - **Fur** (batch 1's `?set=p6`, a row of furred balls): 720p 1.4 to 2.1 ms at high and 1.6 to 1.8 ms at ultra (forward 1.1 to 1.6 and 1.2 to 1.4 ms); 1080p 1.8 to 2.5 ms at high and 1.9 to 3.1 ms at ultra (forward 1.3 to 2.1 and 1.4 to 2.3 ms). Batch 1's earlier fur number came from a software adapter and is superseded by these.
  - **Verdict against the plan's rule** (file a trim if turf or fur costs more than 2 ms at high): neither does; the worst high-quality frame is 2.5 ms of GPU time in all at 1080p, of a 16.7 ms frame. Fur at ultra and 1080p reaches 3.1 ms in total, still far from the budget; no trim is filed for B2-P10. The scenes are small (a row of balls, three tiles), not a whole terrain or herd, so a full-screen terrain and many furred animals should be measured again when a kit has one.

Each feature's own cost in the stream: berries 60 B, glints 37, clover 40, moss second octave 19, underside tint 17, back-light turf term 12, third turf layer 5; dropping all of them saves about 190 B and still leaves the recipe over, with the look changed on seven rows. Look-neutral rewrites do not help because gzip already makes repeated code cheap: folding the relief taps into one helper (the plan's trim idea) measured 11 B *worse* (1,460), and type-inferred `vec3(` constructors 5 B worse (1,454); both reverted. **Left as is: +1,513 B (full build) against 1.2 KB.** Recommended: accept 1.5 KB for the added cost of the first foliage recipe (a foliage-only game still saves about 29 KB of the nature module); or cut berries and glints (about 100 B) if Chris prefers the line to the look.

Scree, railway ballast, cinders and gravel road drew as rounded pebbles because gravel stones are domes; `crushed` takes each cellular cell as one fragment with straight sides (F2-F1 gives the gap lines), a flat top chamfered to the gaps and a height of its own, so facets light differently at Medium and up. `clump` means pores for this variant (dark pits in each fragment; cinders 0.6, the others 0). Jitter 0.6 (gravel 0.8) for more even sizes. Rows: scree (stone_amount 0.9), railway, cinders, road; pea, shingle and creek stay gravel. Cost: ground +85 B standalone gz (1,933 to 2,018 B, against 2.0 KB: about 18 B over) and +75 B in the stream; left as is.

It names no resolution and P9 measured *whole-frame* GPU time, not the material's own cost. Numbers (P9, three samples each, first is warm-up): turf high 720p 1.08 to 1.38 ms, 1080p 2.19 to 2.34 ms; fur high 720p 1.43 to 2.14, 1080p 1.77 to 2.49 ms (2.75 in the re-run below). **Whole frame at 1080p High: turf 2.0 to 2.3 and fur 1.9 to 2.75 ms are over 2 ms; at 720p both are under, except one fur sample at 2.14.** So P9's "none passes the 2 ms rule" holds at 720p and for turf's own cost, but not as a total at 1080p. Re-run now at 1080p lite against high (same scenes, GPU clocks ramp over the samples, so read ranges): turf lite 1.41 to 2.17, high 1.21 to 2.04 ms (no measurable cost of the turf detail; the frame is the shadow, bloom and tone-map passes); **fur lite 0.52 to 0.74, high 1.89 to 2.75 ms: fur's own cost at 1080p High is about +1.0 to 1.8 ms (forward pass 0.32 to 0.45 up to 1.37 to 2.21)**, for a row of balls filling a third of the screen. ## Sun bake: long models (2026-10-25, branch `sunbake-fix`)

- **The bug.** Found on the material catalogue's P10b proof: eight balls of radius 0.5 m in a 9.68 m row, 24 cm apart, read 9.1% darker baked than with a shadow map on Lite and Low under the sandbox sun (11.6 points under the toon look's sun), though each ball alone, or two side by side, read fully lit. Cause, confirmed: `sun::Grid::empty` laid its 64 cells over the model's longest side, so the row got 15 cm cells, and a ray starts `START` = 2 cells (30 cm) off its surface: a ball's rays towards its neighbour started inside the neighbour and read blocked. Reproduced in `model_wgsl` `close_parts_of_a_long_model_do_not_shade_each_other` before the fix (rows of 1 to 8 balls along x, y and z: up to 11.6 points off the shadow map).
- **The fix.** A model is long when its longest side is over `WIDE` = 2 times its middle side; a long model's 64 cells are laid over twice its middle side instead of its longest one (the row: 3.1 cm cells), never finer than 8 x 64 cells along the longest side (`LONG`) and never so fine that its drawn triangles' area covers more than 4 times a cube's six 64 x 64 faces (`SURFACE`). Every other model keeps its cells, so its cones, byte for byte. Deterministic: only the cell size changes, from the drawn level's box and area, summed in part and triangle order. After it, the row reads within 2.5 points of the shadow map everywhere (whole and ball by ball, every shipped sun), and the real `p10b.high.glb` and `p10b.low.glb` (matcat-engine) read 100.0% lit as the shadow map does (they read 90.9% before).
- **Tried and dropped.** Sizing every model's cells from its whole box (as many cells as a cube of the same surface): it fixed the row too, but cut the Frontier Marshal's cells by a third (it is 2.0 x 2.2 x 0.5 m in its T pose) and it read up to 6.3 points darker than the shadow map, over the 5 its test allows. A sweep showed why: finer cells see cloth layers 1 to 3 cm over its coat that the shadow map's normal offset skips (54 of 3,907 sampled vertices), and its lit share moves about 1.5 points with any small change of cell size. Sizing from the two longest sides moved the Marshal's high-sun case to 10.6 points against 10 allowed. Only the long-model rule leaves every non-long model as it was. `WIDE` = 3 left a 3-ball row (about 5 cells between the balls) 6.5 points off under the toon sun, so 2.
- **Time and memory** (`tests/sun_bake_cost.rs`, native, opt-level 3; frames at `FRAME_UNITS`, peak scratch read after every item via `Bake::scratch_bytes`). Every shipped model, Lite and Low, is unchanged: Frontier Marshal (Lite and Low files) 50 ms in one go, 61 frames, 2.0 MB peak; proof kart 19 ms, 15 frames, 0.7 MB; proof crate 24 ms, 16 frames, 0.7 MB; proof barrel 16 ms, 11 frames, 0.5 MB; layer models 19 to 47 ms, 25 to 46 frames, 0.5 to 2.1 MB (times vary a few ms run to run; cells, frames and peak are identical before and after). The p10b row: 11 ms, 13 frames, 0.35 MB before; 51 ms, 39 frames, 1.9 MB after, the Marshal's range. The test bounds every shipped model and the row to 8 MB and 200 frames.
- **Workarounds kept.** The hair layers 10 mm apart and the velvet pouf instead of a curtain (entries above) stay: the head is not a long model, so its cells did not change, and the curtain's dark folds come from one cone per vertex, not from cell size. A flat field of close objects (a 2D grid, not a row) or a cube-shaped cluster still needs about 7 cells (64 over its longest side) between parts under a low sun along them: a known limit, covered by `baked_sun_draws_no_smear_on_any_model` for every model the project ships.
- **Byte proof** (all 8 games `--ship`, EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=65e8497, rustc 1.99.1, against matcat-engine's `sha-base.txt` for 65e84978; 87500f5b differs from it in tests and one unused import only). Same, byte for byte: 2d-platformer, base-building-rts, match-3, model-view (its shipped build has no model shader and no bake), tactical-fps, top-down-action-adventure. Changed: kart-racer and sandbox, the two shipped builds with the model shader and the bake: wasm +590 bytes raw (+356 and +313 gzip) for the long-model rule and the area sum; their js the same size, only wasm-bindgen's numbered glue names moved (`__wasm_bindgen_func_elem_2879` to `_2881`). The 590 bytes include whatever of `Bake::scratch_bytes` and `Bake::cell` (added for the cost test, called by no game) survives the linker.
- **Pictures** (`.evani/shots/sunbake/`, headless and muted, `tools/live-check/capture.mjs` plan mode on Lite and Low, the bench camera path at 0, 15, 30 and 45 s and 0 again, base 87500f5b against this branch). Model-view: every shot identical. Sandbox: the settled shots (30 s, 45 s, and 0 s at the end) identical on both tiers; the first ones differ only where the Marshals' bake was still running when they were taken, as the first and last shots of one run differ in either build. Kart-racer: only the racing karts' positions differ (the race keeps running between shots, also within one run). No shipped model is long, so no shading changed, as the cost test's identical cells say.

## Tool apps: an explicit app kind that skips only the entity count (2026-10-25)

Chris's decision, recorded by the orchestrator under his "follow my recommendations" rule: the material viewer is a tool, not a game, and gets a ROADMAP.md line with status `review`. Tools skip ONLY the review's "game objects live in the ECS" entity count (KIT_PROCESS item 12); the kit-params half of that item and every other check stay, and games are unaffected.

- **How:** `kind = "tool"` at the top of `apps/<id>/evani.toml` (absent or `"game"`: a game). `evani_guide::appkind` reads it; the review's architecture check (`checks::architecture`) skips the entity count only for a tool that keeps the tool rule, and still needs a `kit.<id>.*` param.
- **The tool rule (so a game can't skip the check by claiming the kind):** a tool has no kit gameplay, shown by all of: `[modules] physics = "none"` and `net = false`; its kit is not a genre in `catalog/genres.json`; its kit's row is in ROADMAP.md's "Tool apps (not games)" table (where a reviewer sees it listed as a tool); its kit crate does not depend on evani-physics, evani-net, evani-combat or evani-destruct (dev-dependencies included). `cargo xtask check` reports each broken rule as an `app kind` ERROR, and the review refuses the claim and checks the entity count as for a game.
- **Tests:** `appkind::tests` (each rule broken alone refuses the claim; the kart racer's manifest with `kind = "tool"` is refused on physics, genre and roadmap; on this repo every genre game is refused the kind and the material viewer is a real tool) and `checks::tests::a_tool_skips_only_the_entity_count`.
- **Rejected:** a per-check skip list in evani.toml (any game could list any check); judging "no gameplay" from the live entity count itself (a game that keeps its objects outside the ECS would pass as a tool, which is the case the check exists to catch).
- **Bytes:** tools only; no game crate changes, so every shipped file is unchanged by this.

Branch `matcat-engine`, after the merge of `matcat-viewfix` (f6871b2f) and the tool kind (7cc79ffd).

- **Run video: the real cause.** "The screencast sent no frames" came from the page, not the screencast: the capture script's new page probe counted 3 frames in 23.6 s during the video (`.evani/tmp/vid/err.log`). A frame-rate probe on its own bridge (`.evani/tmp/vid/probe.mjs`) showed the settled viewer drawing 60 frames a second on High and Ultra, at 1280 and 1920 wide, with and without the turntable and after a held moment, and 1 frame in 88 s right after a tier change: while the page builds pipelines it draws nothing. The review's video started straight after the Ultra showcase, so under load (check --full, other builds) the page was still building; on its own it had settled in time, which is why the same steps alone gave 241 frames. Not a headless flag, GPU or occlusion fault.
- **Fix** (`tools/live-check/capture.mjs`): before it records, the video waits until the page draws at least 20 frames a second over two 1 s windows in a row (up to 180 s, logged when over 3 s); a video that still gets no frames says what the page drew over the same time. **Guard:** `review::tests::the_run_video_waits_for_the_page_to_draw` (the wait sits between the video's capture.frame and its screencast, its rate is at least 10, the failure names the page's frames). **Proof:** the review's capture steps (showcase Low and Ultra at 1920x1080, then the spin video) rerun after the fix: the page drew 0.1 frames a second, settled after 25.3 s, then 599 frames over 10.0 s (60 a second), `video.webm` made (`.evani/tmp/vid/err2.log`).
- **Flipped normals.** `crates/evani-gltf/tests/normals.rs` listed the kart proof models (kart-racer and the sandbox copy) as known faults, 402 and 8 vertices. 401 of the kart's were its two mirrored right-hand wheels: the test compared world-space normals with world-space faces without the glTF rule that a mirrored node's front face is clockwise (the engine draws them right, `model.wgsl` `mirror`). The test now flips the face for a negative determinant (and its synthetic case covers a mirrored node). The 9 real ones (the barrel's 8 at two stave seams, pointing inward, and one kart body corner) were repaired with the new `tools/models/fix_flipped_normals.py` (reports, or `--fix` in place: the normal becomes its triangles' area-weighted normal, the tangent is made orthogonal again; same size and layout). The known list is empty.
- **Kart-racer bytes.** The proof models ship in kart-racer as its rival karts' part pack (streamed after the title): `proof-kart.glb` and `proof-barrel.glb` changed (same sizes, 66,072 and 21,568 bytes) and their `stream.json` hashes; the sandbox's copies the same. No wasm or js changed by this (the files are fetched at run time).
- **Rose.** Thin rows with the `petal` variant (the roses) open on a new `petal` shape: a cupped card (9 x 11 vertices, the sides forward, the top rolled back) cut by a petal mask (a narrow claw, a broad rounded top with a dip in its rim), drawn double sided like the leaf cards.
- **Garden leaf.** The pool and lamp scenes' leaf on a stem was a flat slab; it is now a leaf-shaped blade standing on the stem's top: its outline is geometry, its edges fold up with the width, and an underside meets the top at the outline with a thicker midrib, so it is a closed thin solid (46 vertices, every edge in two triangles). The first versions failed the viewer's geocheck (an open surface, floating off a stem too thin to hold it, steep folded ends); fixed in the mesh and the stem (6 cm), not tagged: geocheck material-view 5 issues, 0 untagged (the 5 tagged are the head's shells, tagged before). The nature leaf box follows the blade. A build without models keeps the slab.
- **Capture script, Chrome's port file:** a geocheck run failed with EBUSY reading `DevToolsActivePort` while Chrome still held it; `capture.mjs` now reads it again on the next try (EBUSY, EPERM, EACCES).
- **Tests:** `catalogue::tests::the_petal_and_the_leaf_blade_are_sound` (no degenerate triangle, unit normals on their triangles' side, the petal cupped and its uv over its mask, the blade closed with no inverted corner, pointed at both ends and under 64 vertices); the kit's shape test covers both roses.
- **Byte proof** (8 games `--ship`, EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=65e8497, rustc 1.99.1, at 9d11e8ad, against `.evani-tmp-matcat/sha-base.txt`; `.evani/tmp/r2/cmp.out`): 12 of 16 files `same`. kart-racer and sandbox wasm +590 bytes raw (+356 and +313 gzip): the sun-bake fix, their only reason; their js the same size (wasm-bindgen's numbered glue names only). kart-racer's streamed models (not in the wasm): `proof-kart.glb` and `proof-barrel.glb` changed at the same sizes (66,072 and 21,568 bytes; the repaired normals), `proof-crate.glb` the same, `stream.json` new hashes for the two (640 bytes; 672 in the base, whose copy has CRLF line ends).

## 2026-10-25 — Tier switches no longer freeze the page (matcat-engine)

- **The defect.** After the Ultra showcase step the material viewer drew almost nothing for 25 to 30 s. Measured in a headless, muted Chrome on this PC (`.evani/tmp/tierfreeze/probe.mjs`: its own bridge, the page's WebGPU calls and presented frames timestamped from the first script on, a fresh profile each run): every tier the page had not shown before stopped it for 28 to 53 s (Medium to Lite 52.4 s and 28.6 s in two runs, Lite to Low 53.2 s, Low to High 31.3 s); a tier shown before took 0.02 to 0.6 s. Each switch built exactly 2 render pipelines from one 191 KB shader module (the model pipeline at 1x and 4x MSAA). `createRenderPipeline` itself returned in under 1 ms on the page thread: the compile runs in the browser's GPU process, which presents nothing meanwhile (the page's requestAnimationFrame stopped too), and a text compiled once is cached, which is why repeats were fast.
- **The cause.** Diffing the shader text per tier: one line changed, `case 0u` of the `char_params` slot body. evani-material-character wrote the tier's quality and MSAA, and every character slider, into that slot body as constants, so each new value rebuilt both model pipelines (the slot sits in the model module, with all 22+ recipes patched in). Not a variant explosion and not synchronous creation on the frame thread: one needless rebuild of one huge module.
- **Fix (engine).** The values are data. `evani_material_character::params::CharLive` (29 vec4s, a generation counter) is kept in step with the params and the tier; evani-render's `gpu/char_live.rs` uploads it to a 464-byte uniform at binding 14 of the model material group when the generation moves; the slot's body is fixed for the session (`shader::DATA_BODY`, reading `char_live`), so neither a tier change nor a character slider ever rebuilds a pipeline. A live edit of the slot can still set a body of constants (`params::body`). The model pipeline now has 10 uniform buffers in its fragment stage (WebGPU guarantees 12). Edits to shared engine files are same-line and cfg'd; the new code is behind `char-materials` (and not `relief`).
- **Second stall: relief bakes.** The first Lite to Ultra switch also held the page thread 0.6 s: the playground relief re-baked its patterns at full size on the frame, though start-up had baked them; Low's first visit baked at 128 for 125 ms. `Relief` now keeps earlier bakes (`cache`, at most 24) and bakes the Lite and Low sizes at start-up too, so no tier switch bakes.
- **After** (same probe, Lite, Ultra, Lite, Low, High, Ultra, High; `after2.json`, `load1.json`): lightly loaded, the longest frame gap per switch 38, 21, 21, 64, 77, 18 and 25 ms, frames steady again within 68 to 104 ms, 0 pipelines and 0 shader modules built on any switch. Under load (`cargo xtask check --quick` compiling at the same time, plus another worker's build): 48, 27, 22, 73, 81, 18 and 18 ms, 0 pipelines. The page's start-up also lost the two rebuilt pipelines (37 to 35) and settles in 35 to 45 s instead of 60 to 119 s. The remaining 64 to 81 ms on Low and High is one main-thread task on the frame the new tier's 11 to 18 render targets and maps are made (not traced further), under the 100 ms target.
- **Checks that keep it fixed.** Review item 30, tier switch (docs/KIT_PROCESS.md): `capture.mjs --tier-switch lite,ultra,lite,low,high` measures the frame gaps (`tools/live-check/frame-gaps.mjs`) before any other capture, since a cached compile would hide a freeze, and `kitchecks::tier_switch` fails a gap over 250 ms or a switch that never draws steadily again, naming the pipelines it built (the margin over 100 ms is for review runs under load; the pre-fix gaps were 28 to 53 s). Every game's review runs it. Headless, for any game's own tests: `evani_core::tier_switch::tier_switch_test` cycles every tier and fails if a switch queues a shader slot rebuild or changes a slot body; material-view and sandbox call it. Tests: `tier_switch::tests::a_tier_written_into_a_slot_fails_and_data_passes`, `params::tests::tier_and_params_move_the_data_never_the_slot_body`, `values_and_constants_agree`, the char WGSL validation with the shipped data body (`char_wgsl`, `char_layers_wgsl`: the `char_live` uniform 464 bytes), `relief::tests::tier_switches_reuse_earlier_bakes`, `kitchecks::tests::a_tier_switch_that_stops_the_frames_fails`, `review::tests::the_tier_switch_runs_before_every_other_capture`.
- **Chrome's port file, every script.** The EBUSY retry `capture.mjs` had is now `tools/live-check/devtools-port.mjs` (`waitDevToolsUrl`), used by all 12 scripts in tools/live-check and tools/bench-runner; `review::tests::every_script_reads_chromes_port_file_through_the_shared_helper` fails any script that reads `DevToolsActivePort` itself.
- **Left as is.** Other runtime slot rewriters (fog, nature, film grade, photoreal tonemap) rebuild their pipelines when their own sliders move, not on a tier change; the fog and nature slots sit in big modules, so dragging those sliders can stall the same way. The headless guard covers tier switches only.
- **Byte proof** (8 games `--ship`, EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=65e8497, rustc 1.99.1; `.evani/tmp/r3/`): against this branch's previous head 16afb434 (`.evani-tmp-matcat/sha-base-16afb434.txt`) all 16 files `same`; against `.evani-tmp-matcat/sha-base.txt` (65e8497) the same 14 `same` as the last round, kart-racer and sandbox wasm +590 bytes (the sun-bake fix, unchanged). None of the 8 ships the character materials; material-view (not in the baseline set) changes by the fix. **Found on the way:** the first build changed all 16 files (wasm the same size or a few bytes off, new contents): only the new `evani_core::tier_switch` module, a pub module no game calls, reshuffled every game's wasm. It is now compiled for native targets only (`#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`, it drives `App::run_headless` for tests), and that alone brought all 16 back to `same`. A test-only helper in a crate every game links belongs behind that gate.
- **Quick mode note.** `cargo xtask check --quick` after an evani-core change builds all its dependents together, so their features merge: it reported an unused import in the 2D platformer kit and two module-list tests in base-building-rts that `check --full` (each game on its own) does not. Not fixed here; `--full` is clean.

## Material catalogue batch 3, B3-P2: cut-out holes, one path with the glTF alpha mask (2026-10-25)

Branch `b3-patterns`, after joining `matcat-engine` at 378f9b02 (batch 2 joined; DECISIONS "Join: batch 2 into matcat-engine"). Batch 1's P15 verdict on the see-through pass stands as written there: "Blend (see-through) pass for fire, smoke, steam, holograms and glass: yes, built in batch 3 as B3-P3", an opt-in `material-recipes-blend`; this package is the cut-out (B3-P2), not the blend.

- **The join first** (as the orchestrator asked): both sides kept. The extras bits merge without overlap (76 in all). Stone clashed: both batches took variant 4 and number 7, so batch 2 keeps them (porous to flowstone, `pits`) and batch 3's terrazzo moves to variant 8, `tile_size` and `chequer` to numbers 8 and 9 (rows encode by name; the proof's two stone codes regenerated). The b3-patterns proof grid gets its own number (18; 12 is batch 1's p12). The material viewer gains batch 3's cloth, thin and wood-layouts features and `cutout`. Batch 1's planned list drops the plank deck and denim (drawn in batch 3).
- **One cut-out path: the glTF alpha mask.** Batch 2's leaf cards are cut by their texture's alpha (alphaMode MASK, the model pass's own discard). The cut-out extends that path rather than adding a second one: procedural holes from the block apply only to MASK materials (`model_mat.flags.x`), after the recipe and the existing alpha discard, and the catalogue writes every cut-out row as `alphaMode: MASK`, `alphaCutoff: 0.5`, `doubleSided: true` (base alpha 1, so a reader without the recipes draws it solid). Leaves are unchanged in the colour pass.
- **Build-time switch.** evani-material-recipes `cutout` (`shaders/cut.wgsl`, `shaders/cut_stage.wgsl`, two line edits to the patch), evani-render `material-recipes-cut` (the depth pipeline), app feature `material-cutout`, listed as `"cutout"` in `[materials] recipes`. It implies no recipe. `check` ERRORs, with a `fix:` line, on a model carrying a cut-out row without it (wood's lattice needs `cutout`, not `wood-layouts`). Off, none of it is compiled: the stage text and patch are exactly what they were (`without_the_cut_out_nothing_changes`).
- **The holes.** Five kinds from recipe and variant, no texture: metal `grate` (variant 6: bearing bars 1/(2 ls) apart, cross bars every fourth), `chain link` (7: two wire sets at 45 degrees, woven, 1/ls apart), `mesh` (8: hexagonal wire, cells 1/(2 ls)); wood `lattice` (12: slats at 45 degrees both ways, plank width wide, open share by a new number `opening`, default 0 so every existing wood block encodes exactly as before); thin `lace` (7: a fine hexagonal net, a seventh of a motif, with a six-petal flower and an eyelet in each petal per motif cell). Metal had no free number slot, so its wire widths are fixed shares of the cell per kind; `layout_scale` sets the size.
- **Edges and distance (prior art as ideas only).** Each wire set's coverage is the exact overlap of its nearest wire with the pixel's footprint across it (the screen derivatives projected on the set's normal, a box filter), so a wire thinner than a pixel still covers its true share and never vanishes; under 2 px per period a set fades to its average (the open share), so a far fence reads as an even see-through and never shimmers. Two sets combine as a + b - ab; lace's flowers by distance, fading to their area under 4 px. The kept test is the forward pass's own 2x2 screen-door threshold, and a kept pixel the holes only partly cover is marked with alpha 0, so the tonemap pass's existing tent blend smooths the edge (alpha-to-coverage would have needed a second colour pipeline and a changed output; hashed alpha shimmers without TAA). `material.recipe.cut.min_px` (0 to 3 px, default 0) draws every wire at least that wide for games that want far fences readable; it rides in bits 8-15 of the off-bits word because word 31 is batch 2's style step.
- **Look.** Round wire bends the normal across it (chain link, mesh) from medium within 25 m; where two sets cross, the lower one darkens beside the upper (woven chain link, lattice); a grate's cross bars sit flush, a little darker; lattice draws its grain along each slat in rc_wood. Every tier cuts the same holes; lite draws them with the same edges and drops only the shading.
- **Shadows.** The shadow map, its cascades and the AO depth prepass all use `draw_shadows`, so one second depth pipeline (`model_cut_shadows.wgsl` plus the same `cut.wgsl`, the block, the uv transform and the 2x2 threshold on the shadow map's texels, which PCF blends) serves every MASK part; everything else keeps the depth-only pipeline. It drops what the colour pass drops: the texture's alpha under the cutoff and the holes. So, with the cut-out on, light comes through grates, fences, lattice and lace, and leaf cards cast leaf-shaped shadows instead of solid quads (an improvement batch 2's leaves get only in games that list `cutout`; games without it are byte-identical). Skinned parts keep solid shadows (no skinned cut-out row exists). The plan accepted solid shadows; the task asked for holes in them, so they are built.
- **Rows drawn.** build.grate, build.chain_link, build.mesh, wood.lattice (batch 3: 4); roof.sod (batch 2's foliage turf with bare earth) and asphalt.cracked (batch 2's ground cracks on road), which only waited for batch 2's recipes; batch 1's cloth.lace.white (cut kind 5), wall.paper.damask (the wallpaper motif, tone on tone) and paper.newsprint (a new thin variant: columns of word-like dashes, never letters, headlines and halftone boxes), which the critic flagged blank. Wallpaper's lite now draws its print (stripes and motif) instead of an average tint, so the same look holds on every device; only the fade, joins and grain drop at lite.
- **Sizes** (stripped WGSL, gzip -9, measured standalone): the hole maths 1,284 B, the colour stage's mat_cut 578 B, the shadow shader 606 B: about 2.2 KB for a game that lists `cutout`, against the plan's 300 B, which assumed a one-line discard with no shadow holes, no edge filter and no lace. Trim plan, if a game misses its download target: split lace's flowers and the hex helper behind the recipes that use them (thin, metal), about 400 B.
- **Proof.** `?set=b3-patterns&row=13` (the four cut-outs) and `row=14` (lace, damask, newsprint, sod, cracked asphalt), with a new `?far=<k>` (the close camera k times further back) and a deeper floor under the back rows so their shadows land. Contact sheets in `.evani/shots/b3-cutout/` (high, low, lite; close, mid, far).
- **Checks** (`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`, low priority, `.evani/tmp/cut/`): `cargo xtask check` clean. Recipes crate all features 39 unit (5 cut-out: kinds, wires and holes close up, never vanishing far away, `min_px`, and the shadow test: a shadow map of each kind filtered like the engine's lets its open share of light through), 17 catalogue, 11, 6, 3; evani-render `recipe_wgsl` 10 (new: the cut-out patch validates on every text, shadow tail, skinning and sample count with naga's uniformity analysis; without the cut-out the text is unchanged; the hole-aware depth module validates); guide 115 (new: `cutout_is_listed_and_checked`); sandbox 25; material-view kit 26 and app 65; clippy `-D warnings` on the wasm renderer with the cut-out (with and without shadows) and the recipes crate with all targets. `cargo xtask check --full`: two errors, then one: the known look-parity `baked_sun_draws_no_smear_on_any_model` on `p10b.high.glb` (90.9% baked, as before this work; left to its own fix), and three material-view tests whose premise the batch-3 join changed (velvet now carries a block: cloth is in the recipe stage), updated to test a pure family row (skin) and velvet's block, then green when rerun alone.
- **Byte proof** (the 8 games' ship builds, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=65e8497`, the earlier proofs' scripts, `.evani/tmp/cut/cmp.out`): **16 of 16 `same`** sha1, raw and gzip, against `sha-base.txt`. A first run had kart-racer's and sandbox's wasm the same size but other bytes: the new lines in `gpu/models.rs` and `shaders.rs` moved the line numbers built into bounds-check messages. The shadow draws now live in a child file (`gpu/models/cut.rs`) and the depth module at the end of `shaders.rs`, so no existing line moves; the rerun is 16/16.

## Material catalogue batch 3, B3-P3: the see-through pass (sorted blend, refraction copy) and the glass rows (2026-10-25)

Branch `b3-patterns`. Batch 1's P15 verdict ("Blend (see-through) pass for fire, smoke, steam, holograms and glass: yes, built in batch 3 as B3-P3") and the research report of 2026-10-25 (options 1 and 2 together). Prior art read for ideas only, all code written fresh: Godot and PlayCanvas (sorting per object, a priority override, no OIT), Bevy's alpha-mode list (the shape of the mode field), three.js transmission, Filament's thin model and Babylon.js (the copy, mip from roughness, tint by absorption).

- **Rows.** The catalogue's eight batch-3 glass rows: glass.window.wavy, glass.window.frosted, glass.stained.red, .blue, .amber, glass.leaded, glass.wired, glass.glass_block. The brief named clear, tinted, dirty, cracked and windscreen; the catalogue holds what batch 3 owns, so its rows were built and the catalogue was not contradicted (batch 1's clear window draws on the same path; the windscreen is batch 11's; no dirty or cracked glass row exists). Batch 3: **90 of 90 drawn**.
- **The glass recipe stage** (`recipe-glass`, code 24, `rc_glass.wgsl`, 1,132 B gzip against the plan's 1.5 KB; this is B3-P10a's recipe, built here): glass moves to backend `recipes`, `also: ["nature"]` (a game with the nature module keeps its placed refraction); variants window, bottle, crystal, stained + leaded, wired, block; numbers thickness, frost, waviness (batch 1's, unchanged) + pane_scale, backlight; colours tint + came; extra backlight (`material.recipe.glass.backlight`). Leaded diamonds and block units come from the shared layouts; waviness and a block's lumps bend the normal (the refraction reads it); stained glass glows when the sun is behind it; Fresnel raises opacity edge-on. Every level draws the same panes, lines, tint, frost and waviness (the same look on every device); lite's streaks come from two sines instead of noise taps.
- **Sorted blend** (`material-recipes-blend`; `"blend"` in `[materials] recipes`, following the cut-out's precedent rather than the plan's `blend = true`, because `[materials]` takes only `recipes` and `conditions`). A material whose glTF alphaMode is BLEND carries its mode in the free material word 15 (from its block: over for glass, smoke and steam; add for flames and holograms; refract for frosted, wavy and block glass; over for a BLEND material without a block) and a sort priority in word 19 (`extras.evani_sort`). The opaque pass skips those parts; after the opaque models and the world particles the forward pass draws them through **one** blend pipeline per sample count: the same patched module with a pipeline-overridable constant `REC_BLEND = 1`, premultiplied alpha (src one, dst one minus src alpha), add as alpha 0 in the same state, destination alpha kept (the tone map's screen-door marks survive), depth tested, never written. The stage premultiplies the recipe's colour before lighting, so a pane's reflections and highlights are not dimmed by its low alpha. One draw per instance, ordered by priority, then far to near by the part's centre, then by run and instance (stable). Per object is enough for panes and cards; an emitter card is one object, so smoke sorts per emitter. `material.recipe.blend.enabled` off draws them opaque (the light version), `material.recipe.blend.sort` off draws in model order.
- **Refraction** (`material-recipes-refract`; `"refraction"`, implies blend). On a frame with refract-mode glass, after the forward pass and its depth resolve, the resolved colour is copied to a half-size Rgba16Float texture with three mips (three small passes), and a one-sample glass pipeline (its own module: the patch with `mat_refract`, group 2 the copy and a sampler, group 3 the lights) draws that glass over the resolved colour with the resolved depth: a thin-glass offset (bent normal minus the face's, times thickness, projected), the mip from roughness with four taps a mip texel apart (a strong frost reads soft, not blocky), tint^(0.5 + 2 thickness) for absorption. On every tier, so a phone frosts like a PC. Clear, tinted, stained, leaded and wired glass skip the copy. Glass does not see other refracting glass. The copy is made only on such a frame and freed after 240 frames without one; `material.recipe.blend.refraction` (0 to 2) scales the bend, 0 skips the copy and draws them as over.
- **Shadows.** A blended part goes through the hole-aware depth pipeline, now built for the cut-out or the blend: a 4x4 stipple on the shadow map's texels keeps the share of texels the material blocks (glass: one minus what comes through, from its body's alpha and its tint's brightness; smoke and steam a third; flames and holograms none), and PCF blends it into a partial shadow. No new shadow target. The AO depth prepass skips blended parts. Tested on the CPU mirror: a clear pane lets about 87% of the sun through, frosted about half, deep red stained glass under 15%, and the stipple keeps each density to one level in 16.
- **Soft fade against depth on smoke and steam: skipped.** The forward pass writes the depth it would read (with MSAA a 4x target, resolved only after the pass), so a depth read means ending the pass and copying, or a second pass; the brief allowed it only without an extra copy. Smoke and steam keep their soft card edges.
- **Fire, smoke, steam and holograms** moved onto the blend path by the adapter (alphaMode BLEND from the block), their look not changed: the recipes already wrote their alpha. At lite, fire and glow keep batch 1's lite branches (a static glowing card; the hologram without scanlines), which predate this work.
- **Byte-identical without it.** Every existing renderer line keeps its place: same-line cfg'd additions in `gpu/models.rs`, `frame.rs`, `pipelines.rs`, `model.rs`, `frame/ambient.rs`; new code in `gpu/models/blend.rs` and at file ends. The recipe patch is unchanged without `blend` (test `without_the_blend_pass_nothing_changes`).
- **Measured** (stripped WGSL, gzip -9): the blend stage 363 B (blend.wgsl and the stub) + the stipple 496 B; refraction 508 B more, in the glass module only; the glass recipe 1,132 B. GPU (batch 2's P9/P10 method: the overlay's 2 s median GPU times per pass, headless muted Chrome on the RTX 4060 Ti, three samples a page, the first a warm-up; `.evani/shots/b3-blend/gpu-timing.txt`): the copy 0.01 to 0.03 ms at 720p and 0.04 to 0.05 ms at 1080p, the glass pass 0.07 to 0.15 ms at 720p and 0.08 to 0.12 ms at 1080p, at lite and low alike (nine panes, three refracting). The over draws ride in the forward pass, whose totals swing with the GPU clock ramp as batch 2 found, so they have no clean delta. The render tier stayed the browser's auto pick (ultra, 4x MSAA): `?q=` sets the material levels only, as batch 2 measured. **Phone memory for the copy:** half size, 8 B a texel, three mips (x1.31): 2.4 MB at 1280x720, 5.4 MB at 1920x1080, about 6.8 MB at a phone's 1080x2400, only while such glass is on screen.
- **Bytes for games that list it** (the sandbox's release wasm, gzip -9, `--no-default-features` with models, shadows and glass, then adding each feature; no wasm-opt): glass alone 541,083 B; **+ blend 6,654 B** (the blend stage and stipple WGSL, the blend pipeline, the sort and order, the switches, and the hole-aware depth pipeline the stipple rides on, which a game without the cut-out did not carry); **+ refraction 2,737 B more** (the glass module text, the copy and its three passes, the glass pass). Over the plan's 2.5 KB for the blend. Trim plan, for B3-P13 or the first game that misses its target: build the blend pipeline from the model pipeline's own descriptor (one function with a blend flag, about 1 KB), and let a game without shadows drop the stipple pipeline (already so; with shadows it is the price of glass shadows). Games without the features: 0 B (the 16-file proof below).
- **Byte proof** (the 8 games' ship builds, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=65e8497`, the earlier proofs' scripts, `.evani/tmp/blend/cmp.out`): **16 of 16 `same`** sha1, raw and gzip, against `sha-base.txt`.

## Material catalogue batch 3, size trim of the cut-out and the see-through pass (2026-10-25)

Branch `b3-patterns`, from e1fc46da. Chris's rule: engine lightness first, the look unchanged. The cut-out (`cutout`) was 3.5 KB gzip against its 300 B plan and the see-through pass (`blend`) 6.7 KB against 2.5 KB. The written trim plans were applied first, then everything else that would give bytes without moving a pixel.

- **Method.** The sandbox's release wasm (`cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p evani-sandbox --no-default-features`, no wasm-opt, gzip -9, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=65e8497`) with `models,shadows,recipe-glass`, then each feature added (`material-cutout`, `material-blend`, `material-refract`). Where the bytes go was read from the same builds with the name section kept (`CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_STRIP=none`, own target dir): per-function code sizes of a feature build against the base. WGSL sizes: `wgsl_strip` re-implemented in Python, gzip -9 (it matches the earlier figures to the byte: cut 1,284, cut_stage 578, blend_shadow 495, refract 509, glass 1,129).

| gzip bytes over the base (541,090) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `cutout` | +3,493 | +3,496 |
| `blend` | +6,654 | **+4,506** (-2,148) |
| `refraction` on top of blend | +2,737 | +2,743 |
| `blend` + `refraction` | +9,391 | **+7,249** (-2,142) |
| `cutout` + `refraction` (the cut-out's shadow pipeline is shared) | +11,262 | **+9,007** (-2,255) |

- **What gave the bytes.**
  1. **The sort (-1.9 KB gz, the whole win).** `sort_far_to_near` used the standard library's stable `sort_by`, which brings about 4 KB of code (driftsort, quicksort, small sorts, all specialised for `SortKey`). It is now a 40-line heap sort. The order is total (ids differ), so any correct sort gives the same order; a new test checks it against the standard sort on 7 sizes with many ties.
  2. **`wrap_return`, the draw list, the pass helper (-0.2 KB).** The patch that wraps the final return found the last `return` with `rfind` and rebuilt it with `format!` and `replace_range`; it is now one forward `find` (the lit stages mix the fog colour only in that return), a byte scan for the closing bracket and two `insert_str`s (same text; every patch test passes). `blend_frame` no longer keeps a second `Vec` of draws (the sort key carries run, instance and mode; the tie-break is the same, runs and instances come in order). The two glass render passes share one builder.
  3. **The written plan: the blend and glass pipelines from the model pipeline (-135 B, not the planned 1 KB).** `models::pipeline` takes a `see` argument under the blend feature (0 opaque, 1 blend, 2 glass: the module constant, the copy as group 2, the blend state, no depth write, one sample for glass); `blend_pipeline` and its copy of the descriptor are gone. Every changed line in `models.rs` and `pipelines.rs` is a same-line cfg alternative, so no line moved. The 1 KB was an estimate; the descriptor code is small once the compiler has it.
  4. **The stipple table (-26 B).** `rc_bs_th` computes the 4x4 Bayer value from the bits of x ^ y and y (the same sixteen floats); a test compares it with the table.
- **Tried and left.** Reading the model shadow stage's text from the one stripped copy (the cut-out depth module held a second copy of `shadows_depth.wgsl` and `model_shadows.wgsl`): -5 B gzip (-1.4 KB raw, but gzip already finds the repeat), so reverted. **Cut plan, splitting lace and the hex helper behind the recipes that use them: about 190 B for a game without `thin`** (measured by deleting lace from `cut.wgsl`: 1,284 to 1,092), not 400, and it would stop cutting a lace block in a game that does not compile `thin`; not done. Shorter private WGSL names (`rc_cut_*`, `RcCutG`, `mat_cut`): -31 B, and every test that names them would change; not done. Type-inferred constructors and the like were already measured as no gain by the foliage trim (gzip makes repeats cheap).
- **The cut-out is 70% shader text** (cut 1,284, cut_stage 578, its depth module 560, the stand-ins, and the hole-aware depth pipeline's 1 KB of Rust): apart from the lace split above there is nothing left to cut without changing a hole, a wire's edge or a shadow. Left at +3.5 KB; the plan's 300 B assumed no shadow holes, no edge filter and no lace.
- **Look.** Before and after pictures of the same proof pages (`?set=b3-patterns` rows 13 and 14 at high, low and lite, close, mid and far; `?set=b3-glass` rows 0 and 1 at high, low and lite, close and far, plus `sun=back`, `blend=0` and `refract=0`), hidden muted Chrome, one page at a time: every picture is pixel for pixel the same below the debug overlay (the overlay's fps text differs). The fire sheets (`row=1`) move with the clock, so no two captures of even the same build match: the old build against itself differs on 118,000 pixels (mean difference 0.53 of 255), the old against the new by the same amount (0.53 to 1.1), and one old and one new capture that happened to land on the same frame are identical to the last pixel (difference 0, below the overlay). The code the fire draws through is the glass sheet's (the same blend pipelines, return wrap and order), and that sheet is static and identical. `.evani/tmp/trim/shots-before`, `shots-after`, `noise`, `fire`.
- **Checks.** `cargo xtask check --quick` clean for the changes (clippy ok; its test run failed two `base-building-rts` tests that pass when the crate is tested alone: features unified across the run, nothing to do with this work). Recipes crate, all features: 46 unit (2 new: the heap sort against the standard sort, the Bayer bits against the table) + 17 + 11 + 6 + 3. `cargo xtask check --full`: the known look-parity `baked_sun_draws_no_smear_on_any_model` on `p10b.high.glb` (90.9% baked, fixed on matcat-engine) is the only error; everything else is as before.
- **Byte proof** (the 8 games' ship builds, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=65e8497`, rustc 1.99.1, against `sha-base.txt`): **16 of 16 `same`**, sha1, raw and gzip (`.evani/tmp/trim/cmp.out`).
- **For later.** A game that lists `cutout` pays 3.5 KB and one that lists `blend` 4.5 KB (7.2 KB with refraction). What is left in `blend` is the stipple shadow's pipeline (shared with the cut-out), 1 KB of WGSL and the order and draw code; a smaller step would be dropping glass shadows' stipple for a game that does not want them (a switch, a change of look, so not done here).

## B4-P2 leather: embossed scales and crazed cracks (2026-10-25, batch 4, branch `b4-p2` from `matcat-engine` 16afb434)

Batch 4 build plan section 3.2, package B4-P2 (leather: `embossed`, `crazed`). Written fresh; no outside code, no new dependency, no tier file touched. Worktree `..\evani-dev-b4-p2`; the cargo target and TEMP were on a second drive (`<scratch>\evani-b4-p2`) because the first drive was full while this ran.

- **Schema, appended only (nothing earlier moves).** Variant `embossed` (index 4); extra `crazed` (leather's bit 2, `default: false`, live switch `material.recipe.leather.crazed`); number `craze_scale` (n7, 1 to 50, default 1, so it encodes to 0 and every earlier leather row keeps its 32 bytes). `STAGE` leather extras 2 to 3: the total is 55 deny bits (was 54), so every recipe after leather (fur on up) shifts one global bit (fur's base 29 to 30, foliage.veins 40 to 41, glow.hologram 53 to 54); the three hard-coded tests follow, and a new line holds `leather.crazed` at bit 29. Other packages that add extras (B5-P1's fur, B5-P2's hide and keratin) renumber at integration, as the foliage join did.
- **Embossed** (pressed snake-scale leather): overlapping round scales from two staggered lattices of discs (radius 0.68 of a cell, the scale with the higher centre drawn on top), so each row's tip overlaps the next. A dome (lit crown, darker rim), an outline on the top scale, a soft shadow on the scale beneath, a per-scale tint of +-8 percent from a hash of the centre, glossy tops (the existing roughness response to the dome). Scale size is about an eighth of `grain_scale` across a uv. My first try used `rc_hex` cells and read as a honeycomb of tiles, not scales; the staggered discs replaced it (`rc_hex` is not used).
- **Crazed** (old cracked leather): a fine F2-F1 crack network (`rc_voronoi2`, jitter 1) at `craze_scale` times 2 cells per uv, drawn in the crease colour darkened (x0.4), rougher (+0.3 in the cracks), deep in the normals, and it opens with the wear layer (width 0.05 plus 0.10 of the wear amount, so the Mud, Dust and Wear conditions still behave as before). Each plate also takes a +-8 percent tint from its cell id. It works on any variant; the row uses smooth.
- **Rows** (both `ready`, both original numbers): `leather.embossed_scale` (embossed, 5c3418 over 180a03, rough 0.3, grain scale 56, depth 0.9, seam strength 0.6) and `leather.cracked_old` (smooth, 4a3020 over 160a05, rough 0.85, grain 70, creases 0.3, wear lighten 0.3, craze scale 14, extras crease_relief and crazed). The two rows carry no condition default amounts.
- **Sizes** (stripped WGSL, gzip -9, standalone, `.evani/tmp/b4-p2/gzsize.mjs`): leather 861 B to 1,175 B (**+314 B**; budget 1.4 KB and +500 B: inside). The viewer build is a dev tool; the byte-budgeted ship builds are in the proof below. GPU: no frame-time pass was run for this package (the plan's "leather page <= +0.05 ms" is for the final B4-P9 GPU table); the code added for earlier variants is untouched, a smooth or tooled row only adds one extras test and a few `select`s.
- **Look checks** (headless, muted, `.evani/shots/b4-p2/sheets/`: `sheet-high.png`, `sheet-low.png`, `sheet-styles.png`, per row `high|low|lite|tile|styles`): at High, Low and Lite both rows keep their pattern (scales, crack web); the colour at Lite is the same, only the normals and glints drop. In Realism, Toon, Painterly and Low-poly: the crack web and the scale rows are visible in all four; **weak spot: in Painterly the scales on the embossed row are faint** (the style's own surface treatment swallows the shadows), the crack network on the cracked row stays clear.
- **Not done here:** `leather.tooled`'s carved revisit (B4-P2b, after the batch 3 join); the sandbox proof grid (`?set=p6`) is unchanged (the two new rows are judged in the material viewer, whose shape for leather is the ball); a frame-time measurement.
- **Checks:** recipes crate tests (all features 26 + 17 + 11 + 7 + 3), evani-render `recipe_wgsl` 7 (naga on every text with all eight layers), the viewer builds and draws both rows; `cargo xtask check` clean; `cargo xtask check --full` clean (every game's tests, and the 9 games' builds). `--quick` showed two failures in crates this package does not touch (an unused import in `kits/evani-kit-2d-platformer/src/draw.rs` under quick's combined clippy run, and two `base-building-rts` app tests that check feature lists); both pass in `--full`'s per-game runs, so they come from quick mode building many packages with one feature set.
- **Byte proof** (the 8 games' ship builds, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=65e8497`, rustc 1.99.1, run with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` on a second drive, `.evani/tmp/b4-p2/proof.mjs`) against `.evani-tmp-matcat/sha-base-16afb434.txt` (matcat-engine at 16afb434, the sun-bake baseline): **all 16 files `same`**, SHA-1 and raw size identical for every wasm and js (kart-racer wasm 1,031,978 B, sandbox wasm 651,439 B, as the baseline). The build folder being on E: changed nothing. None of the 8 games lists leather, so they pay nothing for the new variant and extra, as the build-time on/off rule requires. ## Material catalogue B5-P2: hide bristles and plates, keratin hoof, scutes and banded (2026-10-25)

Branch `b5-p2` from `matcat-engine` 16afb434 (worktree `..\evani-dev-b5-p2`, build output on a second drive through a junction at `target`; C: was full). Plan: `docs/materials/BATCH5_BUILD_PLAN.md` section 3.2 (hide and keratin, one package for batches 5 and 6). Recipe files only (`rc_hide.wgsl`, `rc_keratin.wgsl`, their schema rows, `recipes.json`, `shader.rs`'s extras table), 12 catalogue rows, one viewer line. No engine, render, converter or tier code changed.

- **Hide gains** `bristles` (extra bit 2, numbers `bristles` = how many cells hold a hair, `bristle_scale` = cells per uv, 10 to 200) and variant `plates` (4; number `plate_scale`, 1 to 20 per uv). Bristles are sparse short hairs that stand along v, one at most per cell, rooted low and leaning a little; their colour is picked from the skin under them (pale blond on light skin, near black on dark), not colour B. Reason: the plan says colour B, but colour B already draws the wrinkle creases and the blotches, and a spotted pig has pale skin with black blotches and needs both hair colours; picking by the skin's brightness gives "pale on pink, black on dark" with no extra colour. Plates are a cellular noise with a crease wherever two cells meet (colour B, depth `wrinkle_depth`), a fine crackle and a tone of its own per plate; relief within 25 m is doubled and its step finer (the folds are narrow).
- **Keratin gains** variants `hoof` (6), `scutes` (7), `banded` (8) and number `bands` (0 to 16 stripe pairs per unit of u, rounded to a whole number so the stripes close round a model; any variant). Hoof: fine tubules down v (a per-tubule shade), the usual growth rings, a paler thinner edge at the end of v. Scutes: hexagonal plates (`ring_scale` x 0.15 cells per uv), each with growth rings round a point between its middle and a corner (a hash picks it), a dark seam at its border, a tone per plate. Banded: rows across v (`ring_scale` x 0.25 per uv), small plates along each row offset half a plate per row, soft dark joints between rows and dark gaps between plates, a tone per plate.
- **Defaults that keep old blocks byte-identical.** The new numbers default to their lowest value (`bristles` 0, `plate_scale` 1, `bristle_scale` 10, `bands` 0), which encode to a zero byte, so every earlier hide and keratin row encodes to the same 32 bytes (a test holds toad.warty and horn.cattle to it).
- **One more extras bit.** Hide has 3 extras now, so the global extras table is 55 bits (was 54; the deny bits are 128): `material.recipe.hide.bristles` is bit 37, keratin and every recipe after it moved up by one. Games derive the bits from the same table at build time, so nothing stored changes; the table test and name test follow.
- **Live params** (registered only when hide is compiled, default on): `material.recipe.hide.bristles`. The numbers are on the viewer's sliders (`kit.material_view.mat.<number>`) like every recipe number. `lite_keeps_the_pattern` holds: every new variant, the bristles and the stripes draw at Lite as at Low; Medium and up add the normals as before.
- **Bytes** (stripped WGSL, `gzip -9`): hide 749 -> 1,101 (+352; budget 1.2 KB, +450), keratin 833 -> 1,198 (+365; budget 1.2 KB); fur untouched at 1,007. The plan's bases (755, 842) were counted with another tool, 6 to 9 bytes higher than `gzip -9` on the same text; by zlib level 9 the new keratin is 1,178 and hide 1,081, so both are inside 1.2 KB by either count. Held within budget by: one tone line for hoof and plates, a hash-chosen ring centre instead of a corner table, and joint and gap sharing one expression.
- **GPU:** no real-GPU timing taken here (the plan's budget is at most +0.05 ms on the pages); bristles cost one hash cell per pixel, plates one cellular search (the same as the warty variant), scutes one hex lookup, banded none. To be measured with the batch's frame-time package (B5-P6).
- **Rows drawn** (12, `ready`): batch 5: pig.skin pink, black, spotted (plain skin, bristles, spotted has blotches); horse.muzzle dark (velvety, rough 0.85, few whiskers), pink (grey freckles from `spots`, pale whiskers); horse.hoof dark, pale, striped (stripes `bands` 4). Batch 6, drawn early as the proof of the other new parts: rhino.hide (plates), walrus.hide (large soft folds and pale bristles), turtle.shell (scutes, amber and brown), armadillo.shell (banded). B6-N3 can retune the four. pig.skin.belted waits for the body-region mask.
- **Viewer:** a hoof opens on the cylinder (its tubules and stripes run down v; on a ball they bend into the poles); every other row opens on its recipe's shape. A test holds it.
- **Seen** (headless, muted Chrome, the material viewer built `--ship`; `.evani/shots/b5-p2/`): `sheet-high-realism.png`, `sheet-low-realism.png`, `sheet-lite-realism.png` (the 12 rows at High, Low, Lite in the Realism look, which draws the recipe stage as a game does), `sheet-high-toon.png` and `sheet-high-voxel.png` (the same rows in two shaped looks); the single pictures are in `f-high`, `f-low`, `f-lite`, `f-toon`, `f-voxel`. **Same pattern at every tier:** Lite and Low draw each row's pattern as High does (plates, folds, hairs, stripes, scutes, bands, freckles, blotches); High adds the surface relief (the rhino's folds, the pigs' skin, the hoof's tubules) and Low and Lite do not, which is the existing rule for relief. **Fixed from the first pictures:** pig bristles were invisible (hair too thin, pale on pink too close to the skin: wider hair, blond colour, denser), pigs' ridged wrinkles drew like contour lines (plain skin, finer scale), the muzzle's freckles were discs (finest blotch scale), the turtle was lemon yellow (brown amber), the walrus's pitted domes looked like craters (large soft folds instead). **Every art style keeps the detail:** in Toon each row keeps its pattern in banded tones (plates, bristles, stripes, scutes, bands, spots all readable, hoof tubules as streaks); in Voxel (0.12 cubes) the stripes, spots, scutes, the pig's blotches and the armadillo's band survive, **weak spots:** the rhino's folds and the walrus's folds turn to dark cubes among grey or pink ones (the rhino still reads as stone-grey slab, told from the walrus by colour), pig bristles (pale ticks thinner than a cube) are one pale cube in a few, and the pink pig differs from the plain pink muzzle mainly by speckle. A full 24-style sweep is for the batch's final package (B5-P7); two styles were taken here.
- **Tests:** `catalog.rs::b5_p2_hide_and_horn_rows_use_the_new_parts` (the 12 rows are ready, use the variants, bristles on where the number is, stripes only on the striped hoof, old rows' new numbers are zero bytes); `shader.rs` extras tests (55 bits, `hide.bristles` is 37); the viewer's shape test (a hoof opens on the cylinder). Recipes crate all features 26 + 18 + 11 + 7 + 3 pass; `evani-render` `recipe_wgsl` (7: every recipe alone, together and with all eight layers, naga) passes.
- **Checks.** `cargo xtask check --full` prints `evani check: clean` (8 warnings, none new; `.evani/tmp/b5-p2/full2.log`). `check --quick` ran the plain check clean; its clippy and test steps, which run every dependent crate together, stop on two things that are not from this package and pass alone: `evani-kit-2d-platformer` has an unused import (`ParamValue`, `src/draw.rs`) that `clippy -D warnings` refuses on this base too (DECISIONS B2 notes it at 87500f5b), and two `base-building-rts` tests (`modules_match_features`, `finds_one_toggle_per_compiled_effect`) compare `cfg!(feature)` with a build whose features the other crates unified; `cargo test -p evani-base-building-rts` alone passes 5 of 5. Clippy `-D warnings --all-targets --all-features` on `evani-material-recipes` and `evani-kit-material-view`: clean. Recipes crate tests, `recipe_wgsl` naga tests: pass (above).
- **Byte proof** (8 games `--ship --no-diff`, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=65e8497`, rustc 1.99.1, built at a422f247 with the target folder on a second drive through a junction, since C: was full) against `.evani-tmp-matcat/sha-base-16afb434.txt`: **16 of 16 files `same`**, raw and gzip unchanged (`.evani/tmp/b5-p2/cmp-b5p2.out`). Games that list no hide or keratin pay nothing; only the viewer (which lists them all) grows.

## L4 cloth: patterns and sheen in the recipe stage, 28 rows (B4-P3a/b, B4-N2b; branch `matcat-b4-cloth`, 2026-10-26)

Plan: `docs/materials/BATCHES_7_9_PLAN.md` package L4 (batch 4 build plan B4-P3a, B4-P3b, B4-N2b). Written fresh for Evani.Dev; the sheen follows Filament's published cloth model as an idea only (Estevez and Kulla's Charlie sheen, Neubelt and Pettineo's visibility, the wrapped diffuse); no outside code, no new dependency, no tier file touched.

- **Cloth recipe, appended only.** Variants `felt` (6, matted fibres at two crossing angles over a cloudy density, no weave), `open` (7, a loose plain weave, muslin), `herringbone` (8, a 2/1 twill whose diagonal mirrors every 12 threads); extras `sett` (bit 4) and `slubs` (bit 5); numbers `sett_scale` (n7, 1-64 repeats per uv), `sett_kind` (n8, 0-7), `slub` (n9). All default to their stored 0, so every cloth row that drew before keeps its 32 bytes (a test holds it). Cloth's number slots are now full; P9-3 has the extras bits 6 and 7 left.
- **The sett** (coloured yarns): the warp and the weft each carry a mirrored band sequence (a band in C, a dark band of C, a thin line in B; 8 kinds packed into 8 u32 in the shader: chambray, gingham, pinstripe, ticking, plaid, tartan, houndstooth, windowpane); the weave decides which shows, so a far check is the true mix of its yarns (each band fades to its share under 1.5 px). Chambray, pinstripe and ticking colour the warp only. Houndstooth is gingham by whole threads (4 and 4) on a 2/2 twill, which gives the real jagged tooth. Cloths without crossing threads (knit, pile, satin, felt, flatweave) show the warp for stripe kinds and the warp-weft mix for checks.
- **Slubs:** sparse thickened stretches of yarn along the weft (only the peaks of a stretched noise, so no wood-grain look) and soft short flecks in C.
- **Sheen and fuzz moved into the recipe stage (B4-P3b).** `rc_cloth` leaves `o.sheen.w` below -1 (sheen roughness and fuzz packed in), and `rc_cloth_post`, called from the generated `rc_post` only in builds with `recipe-cloth`, draws the Charlie sheen of the sun, the sheen of the surroundings (a two-number curve fitted to three.js's sheen albedo, within about 0.1 of it for roughness 0.15 to 0.9, instead of its two polynomials: about 80 B less), the base dimming by the sheen's energy, and the fuzz (the look's light ramp replaced by the cloth's tinted wrap, as the layers family's cloth diffuse did). The plain weave and the knit, which the layers family drew from its weave texture, are now procedural in the recipe (same thread fade, 6.7 to 3.3 px). Live: `material.recipe.cloth.sheen_strength` (frame word 10, bits 24-31; 0 bits = as authored). Cloth rows' glTF now carries only the block: no `KHR_materials_sheen`, `evani_layers` or `evani_cloth` (a build with the layers family would otherwise draw a second sheen). `[materials] recipes = ["cloth"]` now turns on `material-recipes` and `recipe-cloth` only; a `cargo tree` test holds that a cloth-only game has no evani-material-layers. No catalogue recipe maps to the layers family any more; metal's brushed streak shows only in builds that have it some other way.
- **Open weave and the cut-out.** Cut kind 6 (recipe 10, variant 7): warp and weft threads half a period wide, the gaps cut when the game lists `cutout`. Without it the gaps draw dark: `check` gives a note, not an error (`cut::OPTIONAL`, `is_cut_required`). The cut-out's wire normals skip kinds 5 and up (lace and cloth draw their own relief).
- **Look kept for the cloth that drew before** (`.evani/shots/matcat-b4-cloth/final-old-*`, beside `before-*`): the 11 cloth rows (cotton, burlap, canvas, denim, chunky knit, velvet, silk, the carpets and rug, the wagon cover) look as they did through the layers family. Found by looking: the first try faded plain and knit threads at 1.5 px (the recipe rule), so burlap and the knit showed a fine grid at the viewer's distance where the layers family drew them smooth; they now fade as the layers' tile did.
- **Rows (28, all `ready`, original numbers):** batch 4's 27 (13 plain weaves, 8 twills, 6 wool and felt) and batch 1's striped wool blanket (felt with a ticking sett: cream with a red band and dark lines). Highlights: gingham (red on white, 20 repeats per uv), plaid (red, dark green, a yellow line, on twill), tartan (a red Stewart-like sett on twill), houndstooth (black and white, 2/2), pinstripe (pale lines on charcoal worsted), ticking (navy stripes), chambray (blue warp, grey-white weft), herringbone tweed, slubby linen and homespun, felts. Denim faded and black carry a wear default (0.35, 0.2) for their pale folds. The catalogue has no per-material reference pictures (the viewer's References are the art styles'), so the rows were tuned against the fabrics themselves over three rounds of viewer captures. Batch 1 now draws 102 rows (the blanket).
- **Sizes** (stripped WGSL, gzip -9, `.evani/tmp/b4-cloth/gzsize.mjs`): cloth 1,071 to 2,363 B (+1,292). The plan's lines were "cloth stage <= 2.0 KB (+700 B), sheen <= +400 B": inside the absolute 2.4 KB, about 190 B over the two deltas added (2,171 B), because the plain weave and the knit that the layers family drew from its texture are now drawn by the recipe (the plan's sheen line did not count them); trims already taken: the sett table packed into 8 u32 (about 40 B), houndstooth through the gingham row, the fitted sheen-light curve (about 80 B). The cut-out text +47 B (only games listing `cutout`); core unchanged. **A game that lists cloth now downloads about 1.3 KB more recipe text and no layers family (7.2 KB): about 5.9 KB lighter than before.**
- **Checks:** recipes crate all features 91 pass and `recipe-cloth` alone 55; evani-render `recipe_wgsl` 12 (naga on every text, with a new cloth + paint + all eight layers set; the run once crashed with all tests in parallel while the PC was short of memory and passed alone and again with two threads); evani-guide 122 (new: `cloth_alone_reaches_no_layers_family`, `open_weave_cloth_wants_the_cutout_but_draws_without`); material-view app 72; clippy `-D warnings` on the recipes crate (all features, none, cloth alone, wasm32), evani-guide and evani-render's tests; `cargo xtask check`: clean (8 warnings, none new). **Already failing on the base, not touched:** evani-xtask `review::tests::the_tier_switch_runs_before_every_other_capture` expects an older line of `tools/live-check/capture.mjs` (the file now adds `|| PLAN?.settle`).
- **Byte proof** (8 games `--ship`, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=65e8497`, rustc 1.99.1, target on a second drive) against `.evani-tmp-matcat/sha-base-36c616bf.txt`: **16 of 16 files `same`** (`.evani/tmp/b4-cloth/cmp-b4cloth.out`).
- **Captures** (headless, muted Chrome; `.evani/shots/matcat-b4-cloth/`): `sheet-final-new-ultra.png`, `sheet-final-new-low.png` (all 28 rows), `sheet-final-old-high.png`, `sheet-final-old-low.png` beside `before-high/`, `before-low/` (the 11 older cloth rows), single frames in `final-*`. Lite and Low keep every pattern (checks, stripes, slubs, felt, herringbone); thin lines (pinstripe) fade to their share on Low's smaller pixels. **Weak spots:** muslin's open weave shows faint ripple lines where its threads are about 2 px (the cut-out's fade zone); tweed reads mostly as its twill diagonal, the flecks are subtle; the plaid and tartan setts are three-band simplifications, not named clan setts.

- **What:** 42 rows go from planned to ready, numbers only on the skin, eye, keratin, metal, paint and leather recipes (0 B of shader code; 24 B a row in a game's material table, only for games that list the row): `skin.tone` steps 01 to 10 in warm, neutral and cool (26 new), `eye.brown`, `hazel`, `amber`, `grey`, `blue`, `blue_pale`, `teeth.stained`, `teeth.gold`, `nails.natural`, `nails.painted`, and the leathers `dark_brown`, `black`, `oxblood`, `rough_out`, `buckskin`, `patent`. The 30 tones are set so the lit cheek L* steps evenly on Ultra (80, 77, 73, 69, 63.5, 59, 53, 47, 39, 31) and Low shows the same order and spacing about 2 L* higher. Undertones: warm is about 7 degrees more yellow-orange in hue than neutral, cool about 9 degrees pinker; the scatter colour (the warm band at the shadow edge) is orange-red, red-orange and rose-red by undertone. Two rows are a compromise on numbers alone: `teeth.stained` puts its stain in the keratin ring edge (long vertical streaks, not a pure gum-line gradient), and `nails.natural` has no pale free edge (the recipe has no tip mask); a real tip needs a keratin variant.

## Material catalogue P9-1: metals and tools, numbers only (2026-10-26)

- **What.** 35 rows of batch 9 go from `planned` to `ready` with numbers on recipes that already exist: 16 metals (polished steel, parkerized, wrought iron, aged brass, bronze, hammered copper, engraved silver, rose gold, nickel, chrome, pewter, tin, lead, aluminium, titanium, gunmetal), 6 fittings (silver and iron buckles, zip, copper rivet, spur, concho), 6 blades and tools (blade edge, saw blade, file, anvil, barbed wire; whetstone and grindstone on `stone`), plate and scale armour, and 4 ammunition rows (brass cartridge, lead ball, shotgun shell on `plastic`, powder on `ground`). Only `catalog/materials/materials.json` changed: no shader, no Rust, no viewer file.
- **Left out (2): `tool.chain` and `armour.mail`.** The plan put both on the `chain link` variant. That variant is a cut-out wire weave at most 20 cells a uv with a fixed thin wire, so on a ball it reads as a fence or a net, not as links or rings (looked at on Low and Ultra, `.evani/shots/matcat-b9-n1/r1`). They stay `planned`; they need either a ring pattern in `cut.wgsl` (a shader change) or a modelled chain. Not forced.
- **Base colours.** A metal's colour A is its F0 (the metal slot is 1, so the base colour is the reflectance at normal incidence), stored as sRGB8. Hue ratios come from published normal-incidence reflectance (linear: steel and iron 0.56 to 0.63, chrome 0.55, titanium 0.54/0.50/0.45, nickel 0.66/0.61/0.53, aluminium 0.91/0.92/0.92, silver 0.97/0.96/0.92, copper 0.96/0.64/0.54, brass 0.91/0.78/0.42, rose gold between gold and copper). In the viewer's pale sky and sand the pure values washed out the warm metals (copper and rose gold looked pink), so copper, bronze, rose gold and brass keep the hue ratio but a lower, more saturated value, as the older polished rows do (compare `metal.copper.polished`). Finish is the roughness: mirror 0.03 (chrome) to 0.12 (steel), plating 0.14 to 0.2 (silver, nickel), satin 0.24 to 0.5 (tin, aluminium, pewter, brushed), cast and worn 0.55 to 0.7 (iron, lead, anvil, parkerized 0.78 with a low metal slot 0.35 for its phosphate coat).
- **Approximations the numbers allow.** Cartridge copper tip: colour B at a high edge polish (the tip is a convex edge). Whetstone oily centre: `wet` 0.45 as the row's default. Anvil and rivet: `wear` defaults. Shotgun shell is the red paper tube only; its brass base takes `ammo.cartridge.brass`. File teeth use the diamond-plate bars at layout 20; zip teeth the embossed squares at 14.
- **Checked.** All 35 rows opened in the viewer on Low and Ultra (`.evani/shots/matcat-b9-n1/final/sheet-low.png`, `sheet-ultra.png`, one picture per row beside them; two rounds of retuning before it: `r1`, `r2`; the older gold, copper, silver and steel rows as a reference in `ref`). Recipes crate catalogue tests (`--features data --test catalog`) 19 pass. `cargo xtask check` clean (8 warnings, none new). **Byte proof:** 8 games `--ship`, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=65e8497`, rustc 1.99.1, against `sha-base-36c616bf.txt`: 16 of 16 files same sha1 (no game lists these rows).
