## Smooth tier switching: spread model reads, warm the other sample count, tier-settle, keep the old copy (ov1, 2026-11-02)

Overnight item 1 (CORE_REQUESTS `model-read-spread`, `tier-settle`, `bake-keeps-old-copy`; the Ultra bench row). Branch `ov1-tier-switch` from m1-foundation 3f908b84.

- **The stall was one frame doing a whole file.** The first visit to a tier read that tier's `.glb` in the frame it arrived: decode every meshopt view, then prepare every primitive. material-view's 850 KB `char-head.high.glb` held that frame 345 to 367 ms in the live (dev) build. Now `evani_gltf::Reading` (one meshopt view a step) and `model::steps::Steps` (one primitive a step) do the same work in steps, and `model::read::Reads` runs them with about 4 ms of each frame (`read::BUDGET_MS`, at least one step). The one-go `Gltf::from_glb` and `prepare` run the same steps back to back, so there is one reader, not two. Files added from memory (`add_glb`, `replace_glb`) and native runs still read at once (their callers expect the parts). While a tier's file is read its handle keeps drawing the previous tier's file, as before.
- **The Lite and Low sun bake's setup was the second one-frame cost** (`Bake::new`: 56 ms for the Lite bust, 92 for Low, 285 for the full bust, native dev build). `sun::Init` builds it in steps (model space a part a step, then the grid, then the vertices' copies, votes and surfaces a share at a time; `Firsts`, `VoteSteps` and `SurfaceSteps` are the old functions made resumable). `Bake::new` runs `Init` to the end, so the bake bytes are the same however it is split (test `the_bake_setup_spreads_over_frames_and_bakes_the_same_bytes`, and the existing `sun_bake_cost_on_shipped_models`).
- **The bake now has a time budget, not only a unit budget.** `FRAME_UNITS` was sized for a shipped desktop build (about 4 ms in a browser). A dev build pays about ten times that a unit, so after a first visit to Lite or Low the frames ran 20 to 40 ms of main-thread work for seconds, and spreading the reads made that long enough for the live tools' frame-time watch to put the tier back (seen at 12 s; the unchanged engine was not put back within 15 s, but ran 20 to 28 ms frames in the same window). The GPU side now measures what a unit costs and gives the bake about `sun::BAKE_MS` (4 ms) a frame, never more than `FRAME_UNITS`: a shipped desktop build bakes exactly as before, a phone or a dev build takes more, lighter frames. A model drawn only as a handle's last tier while the handle's own file loads (`Models::standing_in`) is no longer baked: it is about to go.
- **No pipeline on the switch.** The tier-switch freeze check saw one pipeline built on a switch to Lite in some runs: the 1x material pipelines are dropped as stale when the 4x pass takes over on Ultra, and a later switch to Lite needs them. The build queue (`pipeline_queue.rs` `Twins`, feature `forward`) now queues, once nothing a draw asked for waits, each drawn pipeline's other sample count (1x for Lite and Low, 4x for Medium and up), behind every other job and only for a sample count some selectable tier uses. Twins are not counted in `data-evani-preparing` (the page's "preparing materials" stays as it was); capture builds write `data-evani-warming`. No bytes are downloaded for it: the same shaders, compiled earlier.
- **tier-settle.** `evani_core::tier_settle::TierSettle` (plain data) is fed by the renderer's capture builds once a frame: settled after three quiet frames with the tier's size and sample count in use and no drawn model, handle file, upload, cone bake or pipeline build of it under way. The page reads `data-evani-tier-settled="<tier>"`, `data-evani-settling` while not. `capture.mjs` waits for it before every capture and its tier-switch check reports `settled_after_ms`, slow frames, what was built (labels and entry points), and `reverted` when the live watch put a tier back. Ship builds write none of it.
- **bake-keeps-old-copy.** A model uploaded again on a cone tier (`replace_glb`) waits behind the copy on screen and takes the slot once its cones are in (`model::swap`, generic over the copy so the native tests drive it: `a_rebuilt_model_keeps_its_old_copy_on_screen_until_the_new_cones_are_in`). `data-evani-baking` still counts it, so captures wait for the new look.
- **Measured** (material-view, live build, headless Chrome, RTX 4060 Ti, the review's order Lite, Ultra, Lite, Low, High starting on Ultra; longest frame gap, limit 250 ms): before 72 to 997 / 23 to 45 / 75 to 110 / 162 to 179 / 314 to 367 ms (one or two pipelines on a switch to Lite in some runs); after, in `cargo xtask review material-view`, 75 / 23 / 30 / 86 / 73 ms, 0 pipelines and 0 shader modules on every switch, each tier settled in 2.1 to 3.3 s. Logs: `.evani/tmp/ov1/before1..5.log`, `after1..6.log`, `review1.log` of the ov1 worktree (removed after the join; the numbers are here).
- **The Ultra bench is not fixed, and it did not regress.** Its 2D phase (450k sprites) is main-thread bound: the frame callback takes 19.1 ms of a 19.5 ms frame while the GPU needs 3.3 ms (bench runner `--raf-log`, new). Of the callback, the bench's own sprite generation is 5.7 ms, the engine's sprite order check and pack 7.0 to 8.8 ms and the 28.8 MB upload 3.7 to 4.5 ms (temporary timers, not kept). Nothing in that path changed since the 2026-10-29 card (17.80 ms, PASS); on this branch four Ultra runs gave 18.04, 19.86, 18.66 and 20.04 ms on the same build, so the 20.64 ms FAIL of 2026-11-02 is the spread of a phase that sits at its 18.33 ms limit on a shared PC. Tried and not kept: 1 MB upload pieces (31.5 ms, far worse), wasm SIMD (no change: the pack is limited by memory traffic, 450k sprites moved three times a frame). The lever is the sprite record (64 bytes, 12 of them padding that `msdf` and `lights2d` use for their own flags): a smaller record would cut the pack and the upload by about a fifth, but it changes every game's sprite layout, so it is filed in CORE_REQUESTS (`sprite-record-size`), not done here. The limit is unchanged.
- **Tier cost order (card item 11).** The card's FAIL (High 1.81 ms under Medium 2.30) read the plain bench path because no stress run was on file. A fresh `cargo xtask bench --stress` (5 runs, GPU clock 2535 to 2760 MHz, 100 % busy) gives Lite 7.55, Low 9.94, Medium 17.61, High 17.73, Ultra 31.01 ms: the order holds, and the card re-run reads PASS. The same re-run's tier-switch item measured 515 ms twice while another worker's headless Chrome (an Ultra-Water comparison) held the CPU and the graphics card; Lite to Ultra, which loads nothing, took 230 ms there against 19 to 23 ms in every other run, and a timing run straight after on the same load gave 170 / 49 / 49 / 108 / 128 ms. The item is load-sensitive on a shared PC.
- **Byte proof** (ship builds of the nine games on the main line d479e7c5 and on this branch merged with it, rustc as installed, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=d479e7c` on both sides, wasm raw / gzip): 2d-platformer, match-3 and top-down-action-adventure byte-identical (no 3D path: nothing of this reaches them; no shipped line moved in the shared files, new code is appended). 3D games without models carry only the background warm-up (`forward`): base-building-rts +1,865 / +709, tactical-fps +1,878 / +820. Games with models carry the stepped reader, the stepped bake setup, the bake's time budget and the keep-old-copy slot as well (`models`): model-view +1,882 / +1,047, sandbox +7,139 / +3,317, kart-racer +7,230 / +3,680, material-view +6,836 / +3,100 (its build is from before the last two one-line fixes, which move no code for it). Capture builds only (live, never shipped): tier-settle, `data-evani-warming`, `handles_settled`, `ModelGpu::settling`.

## Material-view art redo: bust hair and jaw, lawn, raw meat, roan at phone size, phone dock, Low ball shadow (mvart, 2026-11-02)

Critic round 10 (mean 1.82, R8 and R10 at 1) named six must-fix items. Chris chose a proper redo, not holding the rows. All six are art or viewer fixes; the Ultra bench FAIL (Done-when 3) stays with the separate engine job `sprite-record-size` (CORE_REQUESTS).

- **Bust hair (tools/blender/bust_build.py).** The slicked-back bun is replaced by a soft layered crop. Locks grow from a whorl at the crown (an axis from (0, 0.02, -0.02) tilted back) and fall in every direction: a fringe over the forehead, the temples down to the outer eye corner's height, over the tops of the ears and down to the nape. Where the hair ends is a table of skin points by bearing round the whorl (`_EDGE`). It must stay single-valued and gentle in bearing (steepest 0.62 rad of whorl angle per rad of bearing): two points at one bearing scrambled the side edge, and a sideburn step in front of the ear (slope about 2.5) ran the edge along the locks and cut them into slivers. 56 locks round the whorl, each its own length (0.95 to 1.07 of the edge), taper over their last 8 mm to a rounded point at least a fifth of a lock wide, so the edge is staggered tips, never one line, and the real hairline sits under the hair. Per-lock random values are blended smoothly across the grooves (a field that jumps between locks threw the surface projection off). Grooves are shallow (9 % of the depth, faded in only where a lock is over 2.5 mm wide): at 22 % they caught the sky as pale carved ridges on Low and Ultra, and the bake's lit share drifted 6.1 points from the shadow map's (`baked_sun_draws_no_smear_on_any_model`). v reaches 0.94 10 mm before each tip, so the shader fades the tips into wisps (at 5 mm the fringe ended in hard spikes; at 14 mm the Ultra fringe read grainy). The dark base layer sinks under the skin before the tips part. **Converter-proofing:** geocheck validates the Medium file, the converter's 50 % simplification of the master. A second, shorter layer of locks with its tips in the first layer's notches, long narrow tapers and the sideburn step all left narrow slots or slivers that it folded into 2 to 6 non-manifold edges; one layer, wide-opening notches (taper short against the lock's width) and the gentle edge give 0. Flipped triangles (geocheck's `inverted`: a face against the sum of its corners' smooth normals, which geocheck builds from the triangles, so the file's normals do not matter) came from the master itself: the script's own fold test used the field's normals and missed tiny tip triangles, which every level then inherited. `unfold` now runs geocheck's exact rule on the skin, hair and base after `finish`, smooths folded corners toward their neighbours and collapses a sliver wound the wrong way round (shortest edge, link condition, no seam copy); a lock-length pattern whose tip ended behind the left ear on a sliver no smoothing could turn (seed 1 to 4 in `_lock_value`) was re-rolled. Result: the master has 0 folds by geocheck's rule in the hair and base, and every tier's top level has 0 non-manifold edges and 0 flipped triangles (converter report and a local check with geocheck's rule). Raising the converter's unfold rounds from 8 to 32 was tried and changed nothing; it is not kept. Self-crossing triangle pairs in every part of the master: 0.
- **Jaw.** One broad soft mass under the cheeks (ellipsoid at (0, -0.05, 0.032), radii 5.0 / 4.3 / 5.1 cm, blend 3.0 cm), a thicker jaw capsule blended over 4.6 cm and softer cheeks: the lower face rounds from ear to chin instead of two flat planes meeting in a V (a first trial at 5.4 / 4.6 / 5.4 cm read as a moon face).
- **Build time.** `BUST_REUSE=<earlier build> BUST_REUSE_PARTS=head,eyes,top,socle,lips` reuses unchanged parts, so a hair trial rebuilds in about 5 minutes instead of 25 on a loaded PC.
- **Converted** with `cargo xtask convert --tiers lite,low,medium,high` (lip textures byte-identical to before); `char-head.glb` is the High file as before. Triangles per level 0: Lite 20,558, Low 34,266, Medium 68,534, High 102,800 (before: Lite 19,060). Files about Lite 191 KB (was 158), Low 286 (245), Medium 509 (450), High 948 (853). `sun_bake_cost_on_shipped_models`, `model_read_spread` and `baked_sun_draws_no_smear_on_any_model` pass on the new files.
- **Lawn (rc_foliage.wgsl, turf from Low up).** Standing blades: the surface is the top of a layer of blades 2.4 cells deep and the eye ray is marched down through it (6 steps on Low, 8 on Medium, 10 on High and Ultra), laying the blades it meets front to back: two interleaved cell grids at twice the row's blade scale, each blade with its own height, lean (toward the mowing direction), taper and tint, dark at the root, light at the tip, darker the deeper the ray has gone; thatch at the bottom. Lite and far turf keep the painted blades. Seen low over the lawn, blades hide the sky sheen and the look's rim: the turf is fully rough and its occlusion drops to 0.2 at grazing views (the "pale veil" on the half of the bank facing away from the sun was that additive light, proven by the trial).
- **Raw meat (rc_organic.wgsl, rc_organic_food.wgsl).** Flesh whose colour B (the fat) is lighter than A is meat: its fat is now thin seams between warped muscle bundles (bright core feathering into the muscle, broken in places) plus a fainter fine network and small flecks; each bundle its own shade of deep red; wet muscle (roughness 0.24) and less glossy fat; the fibre grain is a quarter as strong (at full strength it read as wood grain). The old broad fat bands (the camouflage) remain for flesh whose B is darker (jerky) or for builds without the food part (`RC_ORGANIC_FOOD`).
- **Roan at phone size (rc_fur.wgsl).** A ladder: as single white hairs fall under a pixel, white tufts three times their size take over, softened toward the same average; the strand grain gets a coarser twin along the same flow. On the phone page the coat shows hair instead of a plain pink ball.
- **Phone dock (panel.rs, short screens).** The materials and shapes halves are parted by a rule and a half with chips off an edge ends in a solid fade with an ellipsis; `box-sizing` keeps the two halves side by side.
- **Shader ball on Low (scenes/layers.rs).** A second soft disc where the sphere's own shadow lands (offset away from the sun by its centre height over the sun's height), so Low shows the shadow behind and to the side as Ultra's shadow map does.
- **Bytes.** Only games that list these recipes grow (material-view and sandbox; no other game lists foliage, fur or organic): foliage about +650 B gzip (plan M1: under 1.5 KB), fur about +90 B (M4: under 500 B), organic +16 B (1,138 B by the P8-4 count, budget 1,164) and its food part +430 B (M2: under 800 B; `organic_food_part_stays_inside_its_byte_budget` now allows 880 B, was 420).
- **Not mine, fixed in passing.** `skin_turns_down_the_grazing_sky` (evani-material-character) searched the shader text for "\n}\n", which a Windows checkout (core.autocrlf, CR LF) never contains; it now normalises the line endings first. It failed the same on the main checkout.
- **Round 11 (independent critic, extra round agreed with the orchestrator): FAIL, mean 1.91.** Fixed by its verdict: raw meat, the roan coat at phone size, the phone chip row; the bust's R10 rose from 1 to 2. Three must-fix items left, answered here for round 12. **Lawn:** a surface effect cannot break a patch's outline, so the lawn row now opens on its own shape, `lawn` (catalogue `shape`, kit `SHAPES` appended so earlier shape numbers keep their meaning): the same bank with 4,500 closed three-sided blade spikes, 6 to 11 cm, leaning along the mowing stripes, placed by an integer hash (deterministic); the turf's standing-blade march runs only on faces turned up (the spikes take the painted colour) and every turf face is fully rough with grazing occlusion (the blade sides had caught the sky). Proof shapes are not geocheck scenes; the spikes are closed meshes anyway. **Fringe on Low:** one sample a pixel cuts the tip fade hard (character.wgsl `char_out`, 40 %), so the fringe's deep notches read as torn holes; over the forehead the lock lengths now vary a quarter as much and the tips taper over 4.8 mm instead of 12, a nearly level, gently scalloped fringe; sides and back unchanged. The bust was rebuilt and reconverted; every tier is free of non-manifold edges, duplicates and flipped triangles. **Shader ball on Low:** the studio sun is front right and high, so the sphere's shadow falls back left, mostly hidden behind it; a tight cast disc under the foot (0.3 m, the ball's 0.75 m height) plus six 0.27 m discs across the shadow's width at the shadow points of 0.35 and 0.55 m now show its left limb's shadow past the outline, as Ultra's shadow map does (one 0.38 m disc on the middle line had its dark core hidden behind the sphere).
- **Round 12 preparation (fresh captures after the takeover).** The lawn's spikes did show, so that fix stands; it gained density (7,500 blades, a little wider) and a rim of 800 blades up to 7 cm outside the bank, so the foot line is no ruled edge. The Low ball's discs sit at three heights (at two they parted into stacked lobes). **Low fringe, the real cause:** the calmer fringe of round 11 did not cure it, since one sample a pixel cuts `char_out` at 40 % and on a coarse level v runs over big triangles, so the cut through the tip fade wandered into a torn edge. With `CHAR_MSAA == 1`, long strands (`long`) now keep their lock coverage but drop the tip fade: the model's own locks end the hair. Their tips lighten over the last stretch (`extra`, and `albedo` on faces out of the sun, which the sun-scaled `extra` cannot reach) and lose the sky sheen, so the edge eases into the skin. Tiers with MSAA are unchanged by this. The bust's calm and short tips now cover the forehead and temples (`_front`, bearing up to about 60 degrees), and the dark base sinks sooner and deeper; every tier passes the sun-bake test. Lite's level 0 reports one `duplicate` and one `non_manifold_edge` from the simplifier (a finding in the converter's report, not an error; Low, Medium and High have none).
- **Round 12 (independent critic, the last agreed round): FAIL, mean 2.00 (22 of 33), every item 2, a first.** Lawn and Low ball shadow fixed; must-fix: Low hairline, metal sphere. The critic's write was blocked, so the builder saved `critic-round-12` from the orchestrator's summary and marked it so. The orchestrator then decided: fix those two, confirm them in fresh captures, join as work in progress, the card stays `review` and is **not** passed; no critic has judged the follow-up fixes. **Low hairline:** the solid edge read as hard, so long strands on one sample a pixel now stipple their tip fade (negative alpha asks `char_out` for the noise test; lock edges and short strands keep the clean 40 % cut of critic round 2), with lifted tips so the dots are not dark. **Metal:** the sphere reads the look's `metal` row (rough 0.35, metallic 0.8), satin by construction; under the look's `film` feature the row is polished steel (rough 0.12, metallic 1.0, base 0.80/0.81/0.83), which mirrors the sky and horizon on Low and Ultra. - **Joined as work in progress (2026-11-03), not passed.** The card stays `review`: critic round 12 FAIL 2.00, and three card FAIL lines are known: Ultra bench (`sprite-record-size`), hand-over (side branch; clears once joined) and the critic. **Checks, all at 02533a6e (main 0e0d850b merged in):** material-view, kit, studio, convert, character and recipe tests pass; evani-render `model_wgsl` (bust bake) 11 pass; the look's tests pass; games: platformer, match-3, sandbox and model-view pass (model-view needs `--features models`, which it is built with; without it every tier file is refused by design); RTS 13, kart 190 plus `replay_proof`, tactical-fps and top-down pass (one batch first hit STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED while Evani.App restarted, so processes never started; re-run, all pass); clippy (viewer, kit, character, the look with all features, wasm) clean; `cargo fmt --check` is advisory (12,435 project-wide diffs, none acted on). ## Ribbons and trails: the `trails` effect (R5, ov5-ribbons, 2026-11-03)

- **What.** The catalog's `trails` effect (cost 1, works with 2d, pseudo-3d and 3d) as its own evani-fx feature: `effects = ["trails"]` in evani.toml. Kits tell `evani_core::trails::TrailQueue` where each emitter is once per fixed tick: `point` (a strip that faces the camera: flames, exhausts, comets), `ribbon` (a strip with a span the kit gives: a blade's sweep, a tyre mark flat on the ground), `cut`, `clear`, and `style` (colour and end colour, width, life, additive, `Space::World3d` or `Space::Screen2d { layer }`). Ideas from Effekseer's ribbon and track nodes and its life curves; nothing copied, written from our own design (no new dependency, nothing redistributed, so its tool licences do not apply).
- **How it draws.** One ring of 64 points per emitter in a storage buffer, written a point at a time. The `trails.sim` compute pass (a workgroup of 64 per emitter) ages every point in closed form from its fixed-step tick and the frame's alpha, and writes one aged point per slot: position, the strip's direction there (shared by the two segments that meet at the point), width, span and premultiplied colour. The draws bind that buffer twice, a point apart, so each instance sees a point and its neighbour with no vertex-stage storage and no CPU mesh, and draw a cubic through the two along their shared directions, cut into 4 / 3 / 2 / 1 quads on Ultra / High / Medium / Low. At a point both segments compute their corners from exactly the same numbers, so joints share their corners exactly (test `neighbouring_segments_share_their_corners_at_speed`, bit-exact at 0.02 to 1.5 rad a tick, from three eyes, camera-facing and ribbon). A strip thinner than 1.5 px on screen (a tyre mark seen along the ground, a far trail) is widened to 1.5 px on screen, in clip space so it keeps its own depth, and drawn fainter by the square root of the widening (its soft edge shrinks by as much), so it stays a faint line and one seen nearly end-on fades out (review round 2's N1: the first floor widened in world space without limit, so a strip pointing along the view ray stretched along it and could reach behind the eye; test `widening_a_thin_strip_keeps_its_depth` checks the reviewer's cases, spans within 1e-4 rad of the eye ray at 0.7, 3 and 60 m). World strips draw with a slope-scaled depth bias (4, 4.0; reversed Z, so towards the eye): review round 1 found the kart's tyre marks missing in the low side view, and the cause was not thinness (they are 1.5 to 7 px there, test `the_side_view_sees_the_marks_thick_enough_to_draw`) but the ground winning the depth test against a strip 2.5 cm above it at that grazing angle; with the bias they draw whole (`.evani/shots/r5-ribbons/side-test` against `side-test2`, flame off). The 4 km ground plane of the proof lot is what costs the depth precision at 13 m; the bias has no clamp, so a mark just behind the foot of an object can show over its bottom few pixels (README Trails says so). The head sits a tick behind the sim, on the emitter's interpolated draw; a strip's first point and a quiet emitter's head taper to a point; colour, width and alpha follow the point's age through `fx.trails.width_curve` and `fx.trails.alpha_curve`; a soft edge fades the outer `fx.trails.soft` of the half width. World strips draw in the forward pass after the particles (depth-tested, no depth write), screen strips between the sprite layers: in 2D games always, in a 3D game only with evani-render's `trails-screen` (a 3D game downloads no screen code; a screen strip without it is reported once). Compute and draws are one shader module. Premultiplied blending, so blended and additive strips share a draw. The triangles count in the overlay's totals.
- **Long lives.** The ring always covers the life: the newest point follows the emitter every tick and is only left behind every `ceil(life / 62 ticks)` ticks (a 2.6 s tyre mark keeps a point every 3 ticks); an emitter standing still moves its newest point instead of using up the ring.
- **Tiers.** Caps 64 / 32 / 16 / 8 emitters (Lite as Low, VR as Medium), `fx.trails.max_trails` lowers it. The rings are made once for 64 emitters (about 400 KB of GPU memory), so a tier switch never drops a strip (the first proof run showed the kart's marks vanish on a switch when the rings were remade; fixed). With every slot taken a new emitter waits: recycling a busy one would cut two strips short every tick. Only emitters with points hold slots: a `style` call for an emitter with no slot waits for that emitter's first point in the same frame, so idle emitters that style every tick never starve a drifting kart on Low (test `an_idle_style_holds_no_slot`). When a frame's point writes never reached the GPU (a device lost or not ready) or the rings are made anew, every strip starts again instead of joining points the GPU never had (test `writes_that_missed_the_gpu_restart_the_strips`). The effect starts on wherever a game lists it (as `lights2d`); the budget, a look's veto and adaptive quality still apply.
- **Live and bake.** `fx.trails.width`, `.life` (multiples of what the kit asks), `.fade`, `.soft`, `.max_trails` (owner `fx.trails`, `BakeTarget::Look`, level labels in `SHOWS_FROM`: all show from Low), and the two curves through `curve.get` / `curve.set`. evani-live's bake now sends formulas owned by `fx` to the look like their params; the round trip with the real effect is tested (`the_trails_curves_and_params_bake_and_come_back`: `curve.set` and `param.set`, bake, a game built without live from the baked files comes up with the tuned curve and width). A trail curve given an expression body reads flat.
- **Deterministic.** Points carry their fixed tick; the system keeps no wall clock and no random numbers (`the_fixed_step_alone_decides_the_points`: the same ticks give the same point writes at even and uneven frame times). Visual only: nothing feeds back into the game.
- **Zero bytes for others.** Every hook in an existing file is appended to an existing line behind `#[cfg(feature = "trails")]` (panic locations are in the wasm); the queue in core, the system in render and the effect in fx are each behind their own feature. Byte proof (ship builds of the eight games and material-view at 0e0d850b and on the branch at d5142c5e, rustc 1.99.1, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=r5pin00`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1`, one worktree and one target folder): all 18 wasm and js files have the same SHA-1 and size (material-view wasm 3,149,513 `70948a29…`, 2d-platformer wasm 681,455 `5b542c53…`, base-building-rts 757,954 `5b7bbb58…`, kart-racer 1,137,035 `e735a8fc…`, match-3 698,646 `d2684298…`, model-view 590,344 `d1991924…`, sandbox 702,289 `4d30dfc6…`, tactical-fps 774,100 `14b1e776…`, top-down-action-adventure 624,966 `d3e11b19…`).
- **Size for a game that lists it: over the plan's estimate (a deviation, for Chris's sign-off).** Growth of the shipped wasm + js at d5142c5e: the sandbox with particles and formulas, with and without trails, **+18.7 KB raw, +8.2 KB gzip, +7.0 KB brotli**; match-3 (2D, already has particles, keeps the screen strips) **+19.1 KB raw, +8.5 KB gzip, +6.8 KB brotli**. The plan's line was "under 4 KB brotli". The first build was +9.5 KB; cut by shipping the shaders without comments, indentation or spaces beside operators (squeezed at compile time, the sources stay readable), registering the two curves without the general formula path (no name parsing, no expression evaluator, no sort), keeping per-emitter GPU data in place instead of rebuilding it each frame, a table for the params, one shader module for compute and draws, and the screen-space strips left out of 3D games. The last two (review round 1's suggested cuts) saved under 0.5 KB raw, less than estimated, and the round-1 robustness fixes (thin-strip floor, restart after missed writes, style handling, triangle counts) added about as much back. Function sizes (an unstripped build) put most of what is left in the system's frame (point bookkeeping, ageing, groups: about 4.5 KB raw), the GPU side (pipelines, compute pass, buffers, draws: about 3.3 KB raw) and, in a game with no formula of its own, the curve registry entry (about 2.5 KB raw). Under 4 KB would need the live curves replaced by plain params in games without formulas and a redesign of the CPU side; the orchestrator's decision was to record the number and take it to Chris. For scale: the shared particle system is 7.5 KB. Against the ~5 KB target the orchestrator set after round 1, the effect is about 2 KB over.
- **GPU cost (owner's OK for a short graphics-card test, 2026-11-03).** RTX 4060 Ti, Chrome WebGPU, 1600 x 900, the tier's whole cap of emitters of 64 points each (`?set=stress`), frames uncapped so the card runs at its working clock, the strips' draws switched off and on every 240 frames with the compute pass running throughout (so no other pass moves), the draw's cost the median over neighbouring windows: **Ultra 0.0225 ms (compute 0.0041 + draws 0.0184), High 0.0143, Medium 0.0113, Low 0.0063** against the plan's 0.2 / 0.12 / 0.06 / 0.02. A second run on the final drawing code (thin-strip floor, depth bias): Ultra 0.0041, High 0.0051, Medium 0.0092, Low 0.0030 ms, the draws at or under the timer's resolution; the spread between the two runs is the measuring noise, both far under budget. At 60 frames a second the card idles at low clocks and the same comparison read between -0.06 and 0.95 ms (noise and clock steps), so those runs are not used. Phone: not measured (phone: measure).
- **Parity (the plan's internal reference).** A kart drifting at 20 m/s round a figure of eight and a sword swinging at up to 0.22 rad a tick (the tip moves 0.43 m a tick), in the sandbox (`trunk build --features trails-proof`, `?tr=strip|dense|off&view=0..7`), against the same paths drawn as dense particles (4 sub-steps a tick, 8 across a blade), same camera, same held tick; harness `tools/trails/trail-shots.mjs` (headless, muted, SwiftShader, a steady one-tick clock). Joints share their corners exactly (test above). Coverage, steady colours, actor and bloom off, against the off picture: strip 39,059 to 381,830 px against dense 34,729 to 410,349 px on the eight views (kart-side 39,059 against 40,193; in round 1 the strip covered 5 px there, from the depth fault described above); strips in 1 to 3 pieces (a kart's two marks and its flame), the dense particles in 1 to 2 with up to 2 loose specks (`.evani/shots/r5-ribbons/final3/report.json`). Temporal score (a still camera, steady colours, worst change between frames among pixels the marks cover in both, away from the strips' moving ends, ends behind the camera or off screen ignored, the disc capped at 120 px; pass line under 0.1 at the 99.9th percentile): **strip 0.000 to 0.020 on all eight views** (5,708 to 241,615 covered pixels per step, none empty), dense 0.000 to 0.071 (whole-frame numbers 0.024 to 0.29: the moving ends and the kart). Curve rounding: at 0.25 rad a tick the plain points turn 14 degrees at a joint, the High curve at most 5, within 1 cm of the arc. Blind critic (judged before the key): review round 1, the trail preferred on 6 of 8, rubric mean 2.50, the side kart view at 1 of 3 because its marks were missing (the depth fault); **review round 2 on the re-shot pairs, the trail preferred on 7 of 8, mean 2.63, no line below 2 (pass)**. The one view still lost is the sword seen edge-on, where the sheet reads hard.
- **Checks.** evani-core 149 (2 trails), evani-render 15 trails tests without the 3D path and 14 with it, evani-fx 12 (3 trails), evani-live 107 (the bake round trip with the real effect), sandbox proof 7 tests; wasm `cargo check` of evani-render with `trails` alone, with `forward`, `msdf`, `forward,pseudo3d` and `forward,particles,meshes`; `cargo xtask check` clean; clippy `-D warnings` clean on evani-core (trails), evani-fx (trails), evani-live, the sandbox proof and evani-render for wasm (trails, forward, trails-screen, particles). The byte proof was taken at d5142c5e; the later commits change only trails-gated files and the sandbox proof. Full check before the join (after merging m1-foundation at 133d9923): tests of every engine crate, look and game, each game in its own cargo command (two games in one command share their effect switches, so base-building-rts's own feature asserts fail there; alone it passes 5 of 5), clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean, `cargo xtask check` clean.

## Evani.Model construct: procedural modelling of exact pieces (2026-10-25)

- **Placement (Chris, 2026-10-25, "Yes, start it now").** The model-building ("construct") work runs on the Evani.Model track from 2026-10-25 by Chris's approval, as an extension of its brief (docs/MODELGEN_PLAN.md section 6, option 1: "Into the Evani.Model track now, as an extension of its brief"). It runs only at build or convert time and adds nothing to any game's download. Packages MG1 to MG10 of the plan, one worker session each, MG1 (construct core) first; each still ends with Chris's review. Broadside's Node generators are reference input only (read as data, never copied or run); Chris's rule "own tools only" applies.
- **MG1, construct core (2026-10-25).** New dev-only crate `crates/evani-construct` (std plus serde_json, already pinned: no new dependency). `vec`, `dmath`, `rng` and `expr` moved down from evani-model into it and are re-exported by evani-model unchanged; proof: the 320 files evani-model writes for its 31 benchmark intents (every tier, glb and normal maps) are byte-identical built before and after the move. The `.glb` writer for construct models lives in evani-model (`construct_out`), as the plan says; `evani-model construct` and `cargo xtask model` drive it, and the converter takes the files in its Evani.Model mode unchanged (generator `Evani.Model ... (construct)`). evani-guide gains a path dependency on evani-construct so `cargo xtask check`'s stale-recipe rule hashes a recipe with the same function that wrote the report (content hash over a canonical JSON form with sorted keys, so key order and whitespace never make a model stale). Construct files carry glTF materials named after the catalogue material with `baseColorFactor` = the brightest piece tone and COLOR_0 the rest of the way down, so glTF viewers show exact per-piece tone and the engine (which reads only the factor today) shows the material colour. Nothing here is in any game's dependency tree; details in docs/MODELGEN_PLAN.md section 7.
- **Geocheck for one model (`cargo xtask geocheck --model <folder|file>`, 2026-10-25, MG1).** Geocheck could only check a whole game through a kit adapter, so a model outside any game (construct output, or a converted model before a game takes it) had no geometry check. The new mode reads the tier files through the engine's own reader (evani-gltf), splits each primitive into its pieces by shared edges, and runs overlaps (every pair of pieces), floating (per output node, on a ground plane at the model's lowest point), mesh validation and z-fighting (36 orbit cameras per tier); it also draws each tier as read for review (`views/`). evani-geocheck's `cli` feature gains optional path dependencies on evani-gltf and evani-model (both in the workspace; no new crate in Cargo.lock); evani-live's use of the library (`default-features = false`) is unchanged. Errors become tools: every later construct package and any converted model can use it.
- **Byte proof, MG1 (2026-10-25).** Ship builds of the eight games (rustc 1.99.1, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=65e8497`, two jobs, below-normal priority): built at b56f3fae (a clean detached worktree) and at modelgen-core a12f4b82, all 16 shipped files (wasm and js per game) are the same SHA-1, +0 bytes raw and gzip. The construct crate, the writer, `cargo xtask model` and geocheck's `--model` reach no game's dependency tree. Script and fingerprints: `.evani/tmp/modelgen-core/` (`ship.sh`, `sha-before.txt`, `sha-after.txt`, `compare.txt`).

## Engine pack: the engine inside every Evani.App install, Phase 1 (2026-10-27, branch `engine-pack`, not joined)

- **What and why.** Chris: ship the Evani.Dev engine "included in the app install, so everybody gets it, no matter what"; only ready-made assets download. Phase 1 of `.vibedeck/plans/engine-in-app-roadmap.md` is the delivery framework: `cargo xtask engine-pack` (a versioned, pinned pack per platform with a sha256-per-file manifest, `--verify` and `--repro-check`), the requirements checker `evani-reqcheck` (also `cargo xtask doctor --requirements`) and the contract with Evani.App, `docs/ENGINE_PACK.md`. It runs ahead of its stage (6), so it stays on its own branch until Chris signs off a join; STAGES.md is unchanged.
- **Decisions** (full list with reasons: docs/ENGINE_PACK.md section 7): the installer grows to what the full engine and toolchain need, trimmed (owner); tools we may not ship (Microsoft C++ Build Tools, Windows SDK, Xcode Command Line Tools) are detected with "To build games you need <tool>, because <why>" and the official link, never worked around (owner); old engines kept: current plus every pinned version, at most 3 extra, mapped to Evani.App's `.evani-build-` / `.evani-keep-` / `.evani-live` classes (owner, orchestrator); first-build cache measured, not shipped (owner); full-installer updates are a separate Evani.App item (owner); the checker is a std-only program so it runs before any Rust; `kits/evani-kit-kart-racer` ships because `evani-geocheck`'s optional dependency on it must resolve; the pack lives outside Evani.App's install folder (staged in `resources/`, moved to the data folder).
- **New dependency:** none from crates.io. `evani-xtask` depends on the new workspace crate `tools/evani-reqcheck` (std only).
- **Engine changes for a read-only pack:** `EVANI_ENGINE_ROOT` and pack-relative engine lookup for the prebuilt xtask; `EVANI_TOOLS_DIR` for the converter and font tools; `EVANI_STATE_DIR` for the live session files; the tab's launcher runs the pack's prebuilt bridge. Without these variables everything behaves exactly as before.

## Engine pack: programs must start on a clean Windows (2026-10-27, branch `engine-pack`, not joined)

- **Defect.** Evani.App's Windows Sandbox test: the pack's own programs (`evani`, `cargo-xtask`, `evani-reqcheck`, `evani-live-bridge`, `evani-convert`, `evani-model`, upstream `trunk`) imported `VCRUNTIME140.dll` and did not start on a fresh Windows (STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND, no output), so the requirements checker could not report the missing Build Tools.
- **Fix.** The packer builds the six prebuilt tools with `-C target-feature=+crt-static` (windows-x64), through its own `RUSTFLAGS`, not a Cargo config, so normal builds are unchanged. A new check reads the import table of every `.exe`, `.dll` and `.node` in the pack and fails on `VCRUNTIME*`, `MSVCP*`, `ucrtbase.dll` or `api-ms-win-crt-*` unless the program is on `runtime_allow` in `packaging/engine-pack.json` with a reason; it runs in the pack build and in `engine-pack --verify`.
- **trunk (chosen: leave as upstream's build, allow-listed).** Building it from source would add its whole dependency tree to the vendored set and replace the upstream build whose SHA-256 we verify; it only runs after the Build Tools (which bring the runtime) are installed. Same for KTX-Software's `ktx.exe`/`ktx.dll` (model textures) and sharp's `libvips-42.dll` (universal C runtime only). No Microsoft DLL is shipped.
- **New dependency:** none. No PE-parsing crate (`object`, `goblin`) is in `Cargo.lock`, and the import table is a few table walks, so the check has its own 60-line reader (tested on real programs built with and without a static C runtime) instead of a new pinned crate.

## Material-view round 14: soft Low hairline, rim that follows the sun, Low body shadows (mvart14, 2026-11-03)

- **Low hairline without a stipple.** Critic round 13 saw the Low hair's stippled fade as a halftone dot band (round 2 had already ruled out a dot spray on Low). On tiers without MSAA the long strands now fade their colour and light into the scalp's over the fringe's last band (86 % to 96.5 % of a strand) and are cut only where the tips dive under the skin (the last 2 to 3 %), so the cut runs through skin-coloured hair over skin. New param `material.hair.scalp_color` (entry 29 of the `char_live` uniform, now 30 vec4s; a material's `evani_hair.scalp_color` wins, words 12, 13 and 15) and `material.hair.scalp_fade` (0 = the old clean cut). Ultra's MSAA path is unchanged. The negative-alpha stipple path in `char_out` is gone.
- **The film rim follows the sun.** It added a fixed amount of sky-coloured light, so under the night preset's dim moon (sun luminance 0.12) it outshone the light on every grazing surface and the far lawn read grey whatever its colour, matte or fog. It now scales by the sun's luminance below 1 (every day preset is at or above it), and leans harder to the shadow side (0.25 to 2, was 0.45 to 1). The viewer's presets raise the back kick to 1.0 with wrap 0.3.
- **Night foam.** Shoreline foam covered what lay under it at full strength while its own light (sky and sun) was near black at night: dark smudges along a lamp-lit basin's waterline. It now covers only as far as its light shows it.
- **Low body shadows** (kit only): on tiers without a shadow map the bust and the style shapes throw sun-projected soft ovals (`scenes::common::body_shadow`) where Ultra's map draws their shadows, instead of one disc swept from the foot.
- **Hedges and pool framing** (data): foliage leaf cells 34 per metre at variation 0.65 (26 and 0.22 read as a smooth ball, 13 to 16 as a cracked-shell net); the pool camera centres the whole garden and its fit width covers it, so the tuning panel no longer cuts the lantern and the right hedge.

## The material library in every game (Chris, 2026-11-03)

- **What.** Every game in `apps/` and the example game (examples/ground-textures) carries the `[materials]` feature lines the sandbox and material-view had: `material-recipes`, `recipe-<name>` for the 29 recipes and the two parts, `cond-<layer>` for the eight layers, `material-cutout`, `material-blend`, `material-refract`, `material-layers`, `char-materials`, `material-nature`, with `evani-material-recipes` and `evani-material-nature` as optional dependencies (the example also gains `models` and evani-gltf, as materials ride on models). So any game can list any catalogue recipe or condition in its evani.toml `[materials]` and `cargo xtask build` draws it; kits and looks reach it through the game they are built into (a kit never depends plainly on an optional engine crate, and never on a look). `cargo xtask new-game` copies the sandbox, so new games get the lines too. No evani.toml changed.
- **Proof that each game, kit and look can use it.** `tools/evani-guide/tests/material_library.rs`: (1) every game and the example can list every recipe, part, switch and condition (the check's own `cargo_problems` finds nothing, and both crates are optional dependencies); (2) for each of the ten games, so for each of its kit and look (and every kit and look crate is checked to be in a game), one ready catalogue row per recipe is found by its id, encoded into the 32-byte block the converter writes into a model, and the features it needs are wired: 29 materials per game. Plus part (e): the seven newly wired games build for the web with wood, metal, the wet layer and the nature family on, clippy clean.
- **Bytes: nothing for a game that lists none.** Ship builds (rustc 1.99.1, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=mrgall00`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1`) of the nine games: at the main line 424de68a; at the merged branches before the wiring (c92f8502); at the head with the wiring (93390d9d); and at that same head with only the wiring commit reverted (scratch e15ff676). With and without the wiring every wasm and js has the same SHA-1 and size, so the wiring adds 0 bytes to every game on every tier (the wasm and js are one download for all tiers, and no asset changed). Proof files: <scratch>\evani-mergeall\tmp\sha-*.txt.

## Field sea: wave textures on a moving mesh, breaking crests, Ultra-Water's sea state (storm-swell, 2026-11-02)

Chris, of the library's ocean: "the waves do not reach the velocity we had in the pictures I started with; get this to a proper storm level swell" (the reference: Ultra-Water, three.js, https://github.com/Humpalumps/Ultra-Water, MIT, Copyright 2026 Humpalumps), and later "the waves are not cresting, you know folding over, not all of them should but some should, and then they make splashes".

- **Why the old sea couldn't do it (5 Whys, measured).** Same settings, Ultra-Water draws 2.94-3.01x our heights: its unit-variance complex gauss, the 2 inside `sqrt(2 S ...)`, `h0(k) + conj(h0(-k))` and an unnormalised inverse FFT make 8x a literal spectrum's variance, x1.15 from its wind `cos^2` branch integrating to 2 (`E:` scratch `variance.mjs`: Hs 13.3 / 19.7 / 49.0 m against 4.5 / 6.6 / 16.7 m at 9 m/s 120 km, 15/250, 25/700 x1.4). And the classic per-pixel march can't draw that: each pixel re-sums 14-26 waves per step and the steps grow with height (open deck 5.9 -> 16.3 readings a pixel at 2.95x), so calibrated heights tripped the GPU watchdog. Five rounds of adding storm code to the shared shader also slowed every default sea by 5-9 %.
- **Decision (orchestrator, research in `.vibedeck/research/2026-11-02-*-round-6.md` and `*-fft-cascade.md`).** Precomputed wave textures on a displaced mesh, as Ultra-Water, Sea of Thieves and Atlas do; our own code and a direct sum, not an FFT (the sea is deterministic from the sim time; a few hundred thousand texels of a few dozen waves cost less than a port of Stockham passes, and no FFT code ships). The classic sea stays for every sea that doesn't opt in: **its code is back to m1-foundation's exactly**, so default seas are pixel-identical and cost what they did. The rounds 1-5 per-pixel storm code is gone.
- **Opt-in.** `material.nature.water.wave_field` (0/1), or any of `mid_waves`, `foam_streaks`, `spindrift`, `breaking` above 0. `wave_height` range 0..5 and `sea_swell` 0..3 (Ultra-Water's sea state at equal settings is `wave_height` = 2.95 x waveScale). All are registered, live and bakeable; everything ships only with the `spectral-sea` part.
- **Engine (`evani-render` feature `effect-mesh`, turned on only by the part).** `TargetDesc::fixed` (a fixed-size graph target), `PostRecorder::draw_mesh` (N vertices from the vertex index, no vertex buffer; a depth target of its own, cleared or kept; `field` target at binding 4 in both stages), `PostEffect::mesh_shader`. All behind `cfg`, down to a separate match arm in `create_pipeline`, so games without it are byte for byte what they were.
- **Waves (`src/sea/field.rs`, `shaders/sea_waves.wgsl`, layout `sea_field_bands.wgsl`).** A new table of 288 wind and 32 swell components (`spectrum::field_table`, x 0.72 to 48, exact stratum energy, generated, test-checked), spaced evenly by wave length ratio down the tail so every band holds about three dozen. 8 bands 2.83x apart from the longest wave (quantised to 2^(1/4) so a slider's small move doesn't reshuffle them), each on a periodic tile of 8 of its longest waves (times its own factor so tiles never line up), 128 texels and a wrap border, wave vectors snapped to the tile's lattice. The 390 x 1041 rgba16float atlas (a render target, so no storage-texture question on phones) holds squeeze, height, slope, folding tensor, folding a moment ago and curvature, and a row of per-band variances.
- **Mesh (`shaders/sea_field.wgsl`).** Rings at the finer of 2.6 % of the distance and an even step of view angle down from the eye, out to the horizon's last pixel, segments over the view's headings, all round the rest point the squeeze carries under the eye (a uniform word worked out on the CPU: rings round the eye's own point left a void in front of a low eye when the waves carried that water away); 6 (R-1) S vertices (Ultra 768 x 768, High 576 x 576, Medium 384 x 384, Low 160 x 192 and flat, the waves' light only). A band stays in the geometry while its shortest wave has about two vertices, and in the light while it spans two to four footprints; what's lost goes to the roughness. Over a beach the waves shrink as the classic sea's and no vertex goes under the bed (15 cm clamp), so it never bottoms out.
- **Light.** Whole-surface slope and folding per pixel (the kept bands' slope through the inverse transpose of I - lambda M, so short waves steepen where long waves bunch them up: Ultra-Water's silver crest lines), roughness stack (base, unresolved Cox-Munk, what the footprint filtered), squeeze lambda = min(1.2 choppiness, 0.45 / rms slope) so crests sharpen without Ultra-Water's "liquid metal" spikes, facets always carrying a share of the wind's slope, warm sky near the sun in the reflection, crest glow by height and folding, Jacobian foam on a lace with clear water through it (no bubble net), 18 km haze.
- **Breaking crests (`material.nature.water.breaking`, `shaders/sea_field_break.wgsl`, `sea_spray.wgsl`).** Seeded cells travelling with the waves break with a chance rising with the wind (none under 7 m/s, never all). In a breaking cell the wave about the breaking length (a third of the peak's, its phase and height from that band's height and slope, so long swell doesn't count) goes over where it stands 1.2 to 2 of its rms: water from behind the crest moves forward together and the push drops to nothing within less than the lip's own length ahead of it, so the top ends up over water that started ahead of it (test `a_breaking_lip_truly_overhangs`), its underside running back into a hollow face. The lip is about 1.5 times the wave's height, at most 12 % of its length, in tongues along the crest that wander; then it falls, white water tears off its tip and spills down the front further as it goes, spray puffs fly from the crest behind the mesh's depth, and a foam patch stays behind and fades. Full on High and Ultra, a lean and thinner splash on Medium, none on Low; labelled in the panel.
- **Library.** Rough and Storm draw the field sea (Storm about 1.4x the old storm, Hs 19 m; Rough about 1.3x the old rough), test rocks gone from the ocean views.
- **Shared measure.** `tools/nature/sea-match-metrics.mjs` (method in its header): flat-capture horizon, one fixed row a view (per moment a cloud edge moved it 40 px and turned whole Ultra-Water frames into crests: rough read 43.7 % for a true 27.5 %), linear values, per-channel exposure fit, sun-glint disc excluded, moments with the camera under the water and broken frames (a flat void over the bottom of the picture: Ultra-Water's camera just under its surface, which its rig check misses) left out for both engines.
- **Same light in the comparison.** The rig gave ours the presets' dim sun (`glint` 0.3 / 0.25, which also switches the harness's sky to a storm deck) and pale cool sky against Ultra-Water's open sun: most of what read as "turquoise, polished, weak glitter". Matched views set glint 1 and the sky and sun colours measured from Ultra-Water's captures; water median colour and brightness came within about a third. Presets keep their own sky.
- **Results** (rig views with the same camera, sun and measured sky colours on both; 16 moments; ours drawn on the CPU, Ultra-Water's captures from the rig).
  - Crests over the horizon (Ultra-Water / ours, Ultra): open deck 0.8 / 4.0 %, low trough 97.3 / 98.5 %, sunset 37.6 / 39.0 %, rough 22.9 / 30.2 %, storm 93.1 / 98.9 %. One moment to the next swings 2 to 21 points. Whitecap share 1.96 / 1.15, 2.06 / 2.21, 0.31 / 0.98, 0.75 / 0.84, 0.29 / 0.23 %.
  - Waves: rms slope by wave length from 0.5 m to 128 m, along the wind, open and rough 0.85-1.21 x Ultra-Water's, storm 0.62-0.96; across it 0.94-1.36 (`r6` probes on both engines' own water). Height tails: skew 0.08 against Ultra-Water's 0.05.
  - Light: water median brightness within about a third in open deck, low trough and rough; storm and sunset darker (sunset median 0.032 against 0.056, its highlights brighter: 0.38 against 0.28 at the 90th percentile). A low sun's road: 1.4-1.7x the water beside it against Ultra-Water's 2.7x, its brightest glints as bright.
  - Motion (30 frames 1/30 s apart): shimmer 1.52-1.77 against 1.51-1.69.
  - Speed, like for like (RTX 4060 Ti, 1600 x 900, a busy machine, median of 3 runs of 5 frames; GPU timestamps on both): our sea pass (wave textures, mesh, spray) on Ultra 1.55-2.3 ms (open deck 1.9, low trough 2.3, sunset 1.55, rough 1.8, storm 2.0), High 1.5-2.1; Ultra-Water's water work (simulation, caustics, reflection, water pass; its own GPU timer over 120 frames) 0.9-1.4 ms, its whole frame 1.3-2.0. The wave texture pass reads only its band's waves (a binary search in the sorted table: the same picture to the bit, a third off the sea pass). Round 5's rough, storm and beach on Ultra: over 8 ms. All four levels draw, 0 holes and 0 refraction rims in the harness.
  - Default seas: 24 of 24 harness pictures of the classic sea (calm, sun, reef, old rough, storm and beach, every level) identical to m1-foundation's, to the bit. Byte proof: the eight games' 16 shipped files the same SHA-1 and size as d479e7c5's (rustc 1.99.1, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=3f908b8`); an earlier build of this branch differed by 13 bytes of panic line numbers, fixed by keeping every existing line of evani-render where it was.

- Field sea, review fixes after the QQ cap (2026-11-03, worker 4; Ultra, CPU pictures, the shared metric over 16 moments):
  - Lone pointed peaks: the mesh's sideways squeeze is capped from its own stretch tensor (`fd_squeeze_cap`, mirrored by `field::squeeze_cap`): along its strongest axis at 0.65 (the mesh never folds), along its weakest at 0.18 (water bunched from every side, the pyramid, eases off first). A test holds both. Far crests: a band stays in the mesh while its shortest wave has about seven vertices (gone by three; was five to three), so a far crest is drawn round, not as a few straight edges.
  - Irregular, wind-lined detail: 864 wind waves in the wave textures (was 288; about 108 a band): the sum no longer reads as an interference pattern of dimples. Each band's slope goes through its own squeeze (Ultra-Water's assemble: slope / max(1 - lambda M, 0.2)) in place of one inverse Jacobian of the whole sum. Share of near-water brightness change that runs up and down the screen (wind-lined ripples; r6/tools2/coh.mjs, 3 moments): open deck 0.66 against Ultra-Water's 0.69, rough 0.66 / 0.71, sunset 0.76 / 0.73, storm 0.58 / 0.67 (0.50-0.58 before).
  - Crest share (Ultra-Water / ours): open deck 0.8 / 0.9 (was 4.0), low trough 97.3 / 95.2, sunset 37.6 / 34.6, rough 22.9 / 25.0, storm 93.1 / 94.8.
  - Breaking crests: the hollow under the lip is shallower and shorter (0.2 + 0.55 of the lip over 0.12 of the breaking length: no pit in front of the crest; the overhang test still holds); the lip is lit by the mesh's own curl with the ripples over it, its underside in its own shadow; collapse white water is solid by the crest and streaks along the wind further down; the foam patch it leaves thins on a crest's back seen edge on (the hard white plates). Spray unchanged.
  - Low sun: the glow round the sun gathers close to it at dusk and the road's highlights are less compressed: road over the water beside it 2.4-3.6 on five of six moments (median about 2.65; Ultra-Water about 2.7), was 1.4-1.85.
  - Tried and dropped: reflecting the drawn sky where the frame shows it (its thin cloud streaks aliased into dotted contours on smooth water), a narrower wind spread (no gain), stronger noise ripples (too faint to matter). The faint dotted threads along crest outlines in the low trough remain: not foam, glitter, the sun's highlight or hidden back faces (pixel-identical with each switched off); the reflection gives them; a widened lobe where the mesh turns edge on helps a little.
  - Speed (RTX 4060 Ti, busy shared machine, 3 runs): our sea pass on Ultra 2.6-4.5 ms in the steadiest run (noisy: 1.2-11 ms across runs); Ultra-Water's water work 1.1-1.5 ms. The cost is the tripled wave table. Round 5 was over 8 ms. Next step for speed: the wave pass recomputes each component's numbers per texel and each of its three tiles re-sums the same waves; a per-frame component row (one small pass) or multiple render targets would cut it about three times.
  - Defaults and games: only the field sea's files changed (crates/evani-material-nature shaders/sea_field*.wgsl, src/sea/{field,spectrum,tests}.rs, behind `spectral-sea`, which only material-view uses): the classic sea and the eight proof games are untouched by construction.
  - Directional streaking (Chris, the 48b07016 build): rows of dotted streaks over nearly every wave at grazing views. 5 Whys: fine bands aliased along the view; each band was faded by a nearly round pixel footprint (x stretch^0.35) while a grazing pixel spans 5-16 times more water along the view, worst on wave backs tilted away; the atlas has no mip chain or anisotropic filtering, so that fade was the only filter. Ruled out by pixel A/B: glitter, foam, the sun's highlight, the sampler (linear in the engine and the harness), the rest-point lookup inside a triangle; the mesh's rings only set the lines' spacing. Fix: the stretch comes from the slope the pixel sees (min of flat water's and the mesh facet's), bands fade by footprint x stretch^0.75 (cap 16), and a band the full along-view footprint would fade is read twice, a quarter of it either way along the view, and averaged (anisotropic filtering by hand). Pixel-scale speckle (tools/nature/sea-speckle.mjs, water band below the horizon): 1.4-2.0 before, 0.9-1.2 after, Ultra-Water 1.3-1.5 (its real ripples and sparkle; the measure can't tell those from aliasing, the pictures can). Test `fine_bands_never_alias_along_the_view`.
  - Why no mip chain for the wave textures (as Ultra-Water has): the eight bands' three tiles are packed in one atlas with a one-texel apron, so mips would bleed between tiles; the engine's fixed render targets have one level, and building mips each frame would need new evani-render passes. The two-tap filter covers the aliasing for two extra reads on one or two bands a pixel. A per-band texture array with mips is the clean next step if the engine gains it.
  - Foam must have a cause (Chris: a round foam patch with no break under it). 5 Whys: the patch was the breaking cells' foam; `brk_foam` laid a round patch at the middle of every cell whose event timer ran, whatever wave stood there (the white water checked for a tall crest, the patch never did); it was added as 'the patch a break leaves behind' with no link back to the break. Two more foams had no event: the gale's foam streaks were also drawn from noise alone where no foam was, and folding foam (the surface bunching past the threshold) was kept at a quarter in troughs, where water bunches without breaking. Fix: folding makes foam only on a crest's upper half (now), or carried on from a moment ago when the water then stood on a crest folding (the wave textures keep that moment's height: tile C .z); the streaks only shape carried foam; a break's foam (`brk_foam_src`) lies only where the cell's crest went over, along that crest where it fell, a band down its face, carried back as the wave moves on and fading, and only if the wave stood tall at the break (the white water's own test at birth, eased as the foam ages because the group's height spreads as it travels). Foam view (dev builds only, `capture`: param `material.nature.water.foam_debug`, shader sea_field_debug.wgsl; ship builds get neither): red new from an event now (a crest folding or going over, the shore), blue carried, white fading, yellow none. Before (the old logic): 52,122 yellow pixels in five library pictures (the round patches and the noise streaks); after: none, and none in 60 Ultra and 40 Medium/High pictures of rough and storm seas every 10 s over the 300 s loop (tools/nature/sea-foam-view.mjs). Tests `every_patch_of_foam_has_a_cause`, `the_foam_view_is_dev_only`. The switch rides the spray word's bit 16 (`FOAM_DEBUG_BIT`; the breaking chance is masked to its byte in the shader and in Rust).
  - Final numbers at the foam commit (CPU pictures, 16 moments; GPU timers, RTX 4060 Ti, busy shared machine, 3 runs, medians): crest share Ultra-Water / ours: open deck 0.8 / 0.8, low trough 97.3 / 94.6, sunset 37.6 / 34.6, rough 22.9 / 24.8, storm 93.1 / 95.1. Wind-lined share of near-water detail: 0.69 / 0.70, 0.71 / 0.69, 0.73 / 0.79, 0.67 / 0.61. Sunset road 2.4-3.6 on five of six moments (one has a near wave over it). Speed: our sea pass on Ultra 3.1-4.6 ms (open deck 3.85, low trough 3.95, sunset 4.35, rough 4.55, storm 3.1; High 1.8-5.3, noisy), Ultra-Water's water work 1.1-1.3 ms; 1.55-2.3 ms before this round's fixes (the 864-wave table, the two reads along the view, the break foam's checks); round 5 over 8 ms. The next speed step stays the per-frame component row or render targets for the wave pass (about three times off it).

- Field sea, review round 6 r1 fixes and Chris's library report (2026-11-03, worker 5; Ultra, CPU pictures, the shared metric over 16 moments; GPU timestamps, RTX 4060 Ti, one short run):
  - Fine ripples back, no streaks (r1 H1). 5 Whys: the streak fix faded every band by one round footprint stretched 8x along a grazing view, so ripples across the view went too; the faded slope all went to roughness, so the sun's glints became broad bright blotches; the stretch came from the mesh facet (or flat water), so wave backs near the eye and slopes facing the eye were over-faded (vertical hatching on flanks). Fix (`fd_surface`): each band's slope is split along and across the view; the part along the view fades by the footprint along the view, the part across by the plain footprint, both with a mip-like fade (0.35-0.9 of the band's shortest wave); how far the view grazes is read per band off the surface the longer bands make (a smooth tilt, no facets); the filtered slope goes to the roughness at a share (0.35 round, 0.7 in its own direction; all of it gave the blotches), through an anisotropic GGX (along and across the view). The two reads along the view stay for bands the long footprint fades. The atlas's band row now carries each band's slope covariance (it held an unused summed amplitude). Pixel-scale speckle (tools/nature/sea-speckle.mjs, moments 0/2/4): open deck 1.14-1.45 (was 0.96-1.17, Ultra-Water 1.44-1.51), rough 1.01-1.32 (0.99-1.16; 1.32-1.44), storm 1.22-1.43 (1.19-1.26; 1.50-1.67); grazing streak set without dotted rows. Tried and dropped: more waves in the fine bands (twins in the wave pass, a mirrored second read): little visible gain for the cost.
  - Crest outlines (r1 M5): a shading normal tipped away from the eye at an outline saw the water at full grazing (Fresnel near one, a one-pixel bright thread). It is bent back until it faces the eye a little.

## evani-grass: procedural cinematic grass and crops (grass, 2026-11-03)

Chris chose "One grass first, then add the others" and option 1 of the prior-art card (build our own in the Ghost of Tsushima style; research .vibedeck/research/2026-11-03-procedural-cinematic-grass-and-crops-evani-grass.md). Defaults taken from the brief: the crate is named `evani-grass`, and trampled grass springs back slowly by default (`material.grass.trample.half_life` 8 s, slower when wet) with `material.grass.trample.keep_flat` to keep it down.

- **What it is.** A new optional crate, `crates/evani-grass`: every blade is a cubic Bezier strip generated on the GPU each frame; no meshes or textures ship. Four kinds are parameter sets of the one system (`Kind::Meadow`, `Lawn`, `Mud`, `Wheat`; `material.grass.<kind>.*`). A game turns it on with `[modules] grass = true` in evani.toml (new key in xtask's and evani-guide's readers; the app's `grass` feature; `evani-grass` added to `OPTIONAL_CRATES`, so a kit can't carry it as a plain dependency).
- **Render hook (CORE_REQUESTS `world-draws`).** Game passes can't draw geometry with the scene's depth and MSAA, so evani-render gains the opt-in feature `world-draws`: a module puts a `WorldDraw` in the `WorldDraws` resource; the renderer gives it one compute pass of its own before the graph walk (timed under its name, here `grass`) and calls its draws inside the forward pass after meshes and models, with the pass's sample count, formats and views. Two calls are appended to existing lines of `gpu/frame.rs`, the timer's `compute_pass` cfg is widened and the new module files are declared at the ends of `lib.rs` and `gpu/frame.rs`, so no line moves (panic locations are in the wasm). Only evani-grass turns it on.
- **Generation every frame, not cached tiles.** The research suggested building tiles as they come into range and spreading the builds over frames. Here the CPU lists the 4 m tiles in reach and in view each frame (nearest first) and the GPU regenerates each candidate blade from a hash of its tile, patch and index, then culls it (frustum, LOD keep at its own distance) and appends it to one of three LOD buckets (near, middle, far: 15/9/5 vertices on High), each drawn with one indirect draw. The cost is the same every frame, so a fast camera never waits on tile builds (the pitfall the research names); there is no tile cache to manage. A blade is identical every frame and on every device (integer hashes, no `rand`).
- **LOD and budgets.** Full density to the tier's full-density distance, then `(full / d)^2` (blades per pixel stay about even) with the survivors widened up to 2.2 to 3x and never thinner than about a pixel; blades in the last quarter of their kept share grow in and the last fifth of the reach shrink away, so nothing pops. Far blades hand over to a shared "far sward" shading that the ground carpet under each patch continues, so no line shows where the blades end. Short kinds are drawn less far (`plan::reach`: a lawn about 45% of the tier's reach). Per bucket, the CPU scales the plan so it fits the bucket's cap with room for GPU culling (`plan::SURVIVE` 0.7) and stays under the tier's candidate budget; it thins evenly instead of dropping tiles (the first version filled the buckets in job order and lost whole near regions).
- **Tiers** (`plan::TIERS`; quality follows the device tier or `material.grass.quality`): Lite 25k / Low 40k blades drawn at most (phones; 7/5/3 vertices; 48 and 64 cell trample windows; no translucency), Medium 200k (5 segments near, 128 cells), High 360k (7 segments, 192 cells, translucency), Ultra 600k (7/5/3 segments, 256 cells, 85 m reach).
- **Wind**: one field, a slow sway, gust waves travelling downwind (`wind.gust_speed`, `wind.gust_scale`) and a per-blade flutter; the bend angle grows with the blade's length, so the tip moves with the square of the height. The far carpet brightens in the same gust waves.
- **Trampling**: characters are stamped each frame as capsules swept from last frame's position into a toroidal window that follows the camera (centred just in front of the eye; cells snapped to the grid, so the window scrolls without popping: only cells coming in are cleared). The first version centred it on the walker, so a path he had left more than half a window behind was wiped, which also hid `keep_flat`: caught by the trampling pictures. Each frame every cell relaxes by `0.5^(dt / half_life)`, with `half_life * (1 + wetness * trample.wet_slowdown)`. Visual only: render time, never fed back into the simulation.
- **Wetness**: `material.grass.wetness` darkens the blades (`wet.darken`), adds a tight wet sheen (`wet.gloss`, High and Ultra full, Medium full, Low 0.6), droops them (`wet.droop`) and slows their recovery; bare soil turns to shining mud. Muddy ground (`mud` kind) has wet soil and puddles even when dry.
- **Lighting**: rounded normals across each blade, wrapped diffuse, root occlusion by depth in the sward, back-lit translucency and a rim towards the sun (High and Ultra; Medium half), wet gloss; the scene's sun, ambient and fog slot (the slot body is spliced into the grass shader and rebuilt when it changes). Blades cast and receive no shadows (the world-draws hook has no shadow-map access yet; a follow-up).
- **Robust**: pipelines are built inside error scopes; a shader that fails is reported once in the ErrorLog and the grass switches off instead of erroring every frame (Tint rejects `a * b ^ c` without brackets, which naga accepts: found that way).
- **Proof game**: `examples/grass-field` (its own workspace like the ground-textures proof): a dust field with the four patches, a walker who crosses the meadow and leaves it, the daylight look with evani-material-proc's sky dome. Views and flags in its main.rs; pictures and timings with `tools/grass/grass-shots.mjs` (headless, muted Chrome; virtual clock with held frames; SwiftShader for pictures, the graphics card only for the timing run), sheets with `tools/grass/sheet.mjs`.
- **GPU cost** (RTX 4060 Ti, Chrome WebGPU, 1600 x 900, the meadow view with the walker, frames uncapped, adaptive quality off; the grass compute pass plus the forward pass with grass less without it, medians over 10 s; owner's OK for graphics-card runs: Evani.App's away decision "Yes, a short test", then Chris via the orchestrator "GPU can be used ... not clog up the GPU if not needed anymore"; every browser closed by its PID). Final build (ea0faec7): **Low 0.17 ms** (0.031 compute + 0.140 draw, 49k blades planned), **Medium 1.15 ms** (0.089 + 1.057, 144k), **High 1.54 ms** (0.185 + 1.359, 301k), **Ultra 2.59 ms** (0.301 + 2.292, 474k). An earlier run on 01f897ca: 0.20 / 0.73 / 1.14 / 1.61 ms; the draw part moves with the card's clock on a PC shared with other builds, so read both as the range. The compute pass alone is steady (0.03 / 0.09 / 0.19 / 0.30 ms). Phone: not measured (phone: measure).
- **Size** (the proof game, `trunk build --release`, wasm-opt z, with and without the `grass` feature): **+23.6 KB gzip / +19.6 KB brotli** of wasm (+54,639 bytes raw: 647,294 against 592,655) and +0.35 KB gzip of js (+2,742 raw). The WGSL ships squeezed at compile time (`wgsl.rs`, the trails shaders' rule: no comments, indentation or spaces beside operators), which took 3.7 KB gzip off the first build (+27.3 KB). Most of what is left is the param table's names and descriptions (the live tools' schema), the three-stage WGSL and the wgpu glue. Nothing for a game that doesn't list it (byte proof).
- **Byte proof** (zero bytes for others): ship builds (`cargo xtask build <id> --ship --no-diff`) of the nine in-tree games at m1-foundation 89fd89af and on this branch with that commit merged in (a5f2c2a2; the render hook is unchanged since), rustc 1.99.1, `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=grass000`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1`, target and TEMP on E: (`/e/evani-grass/proof/byteproof.sh`): **18 of 18 wasm and js files the same SHA-1 and size** (material-view wasm 3,162,487 `fbd57bdc…`, 2d-platformer 681,455 `24f2677e…`, base-building-rts 757,954 `ed282682…`, kart-racer 1,137,035 `2f194acd…`, match-3 698,646 `da399e18…`, model-view 590,344 `37c181c6…`, sandbox 702,289 `4afd81c2…`, tactical-fps 774,100 `717311c4…`, top-down-action-adventure 624,966 `2b8c0cfe…`). Match-3's first candidate build died at process start (`STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED`, during an Evani.App restart) and was rebuilt alone. Declaring the `world-draws` feature on evani-render did not move any game's bytes.
- **Checks** (the full check in parts, each under 50 minutes): (a) `cargo xtask check`: `evani check: clean`, 9 warnings, all older ones about other games; (b) clippy `-D warnings`: evani-grass all targets native and wasm32, evani-xtask and evani-guide all targets: clean; (c) tests: evani-grass 13, evani-guide 148, evani-xtask 180, evani-render with `world-draws` 92: pass; (d) `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` of evani-render with `world-draws` alone, with `shadows,models,particles,trails`, with `camera-range,capture,game-passes`, and of evani-grass with `capture,camera-range`: pass; (e) the byte proof above. The WGSL is validated with naga in the crate's tests (layouts checked word for word against the CPU packing); Chrome's Tint is stricter (it rejects `a * b ^ c` without brackets), so every shader was also built in the browser by the picture runs.
- **Pictures** (graphics card, 1280 x 720, High unless named): `.evani/shots/grass/r6/` (eight views, rain, wind for all four kinds, the five tiers, sheets) and `.evani/shots/grass/r7t/` (trampling and keep-flat); the early review's three findings (straight blades, uniform colour, washed-out sky) were fixed before them.
- **Not done / follow-ups**: shadows on and from grass; terrain height (patches are flat rectangles); cutting and harvesting, trees and bushes, genre kit integration and deploying were out of scope.

## Procedural library: base, registry, features and viewer (proclib, 2026-11-03)

- **Brief** (Chris, confirmed: "Procedural library framework, 1/10 asset pass", part 1): the shared base of an Evani.Dev procedural library and the full asset manifest; architecture and integration over quality. Defaults taken: crate names in the existing style (`evani-procedural`, `evani-procedural-lib`); unclear or unlinked assets get a name-based placeholder and a flag (none were unlinked); the storm sea, ocean and grass plugged in as they are. docs/PROCEDURAL.md.
- **Manifest**: `catalog/procedural/library.json`, imported from Chris's list "Each asset has a clickable source reference next to it" by `tools/procedural/import_docx.py`: 24 categories, 360 assets (15 each), each with its feature, live param prefix, source link and type, the licence the list states (Apache-2.0 100, MIT 58, not stated 202; three.js links are recorded as `licence_known: MIT`), status, path and style coverage. 2 built, 10 wrapped, 348 placeholders.
- **Two crates, not 24.** `evani-procedural` is the base (the `ProcAsset` trait, `Registry`, `ParamSpec`/`Values`, styles, noise, mesh helpers, the placeholder, `ProcScene` and `ProcModule`); `evani-procedural-lib` holds every asset behind its own feature, one module per category. One crate with 360 features (generated from the manifest by `tools/procedural/gen_library.py`) means category workers edit only their category's file and the manifest, never a shared Cargo.toml by hand, and the build still compiles only what is listed. No third-party crate was added.
- **evani.toml**: `[modules] procedural = ["terrain", "geometry-cube-cuboid"]` rides the material-module rule (`evani_guide::manifest::MATERIAL_MODULES` gains `("procedural", "evani-procedural-lib")`): app features `procedural` and `procedural-<part>`; a part the library has no feature for is a check ERROR. xtask's manifest, `without_each`, `base`, build facts and review's module lists know it.
- **Live params**: `procedural.<category>.<asset>.{on,seed,<param>}` in the one param registry (Look Lab, viewer and AI agents' `param_set`). Wrapped modules keep their own names; the library adds only the `.on` switch.
- **Styles first-class** (Chris via the orchestrator, 2026-11-03: Realism first, all 24 styles later): `generate(values, seed, style)`; every asset lists its native styles, Realism (`WK24`) for now, others fall back to it and the registry reports the fallback. The manifest's `styles` column records coverage.
- **Wrapped as they are**: water-oceans (spectral sea), water-ocean-waves (the storm sea: the spectral sea on its storm preset), water-lakes/ponds/rivers and textures-glass (the nature pass), sky-dynamic-sky-dome (evani-material-proc sky), vegetation-short-grass, vegetation-long-grass and agriculture-wheat-plants (evani-grass). `ProcModule` hosts the nature and grass modules when a game lists only library entries (`hosted_elsewhere` for an app that adds them itself). No wrapped crate changed.
- **Built**: geometry-cube-cuboid (inspired by three.js BoxGeometry, MIT: per-face segment grids) and terrain-rolling-hills (inspired by THREE.Terrain, MIT: a height grid of layered value noise). Written fresh; nothing copied. `src/template.rs` is the asset to copy.
- **Viewer**: the material-view Studio's existing Procedural tab: the 24 categories as folds (count and built count), every asset a card with an On/Off switch (its `.on` param; off removes it from the view), its param panel (seed and params, live), the style note and its evani.toml line. The tab's JSON (`catalog/procedural/procedural.json`) gains `category`, `asset`, `stage_as` and `alias` (the storm sea, pond and river are aliases of the Ocean and Lake items on their own preset) and three grass items. material-view lists every category; it carries `meshes` and evani-grass from now on (dev tool, never shipped).
- **Proof of gating** (`python -I tools/procedural/gate_proof.py`, examples/proc-field built `cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` with the engine's ship profile, rustc 1.99.1, raw cargo wasm before wasm-bindgen and wasm-opt):

  | Build | wasm | added | gzip | added gzip | assets in the wasm (by name) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | none (no `procedural` line) | 1,515,729 | 0 | 439,247 | 0 | none; no `evani.module.procedural` |
  | one asset: terrain-rolling-hills | 1,540,134 | +24,405 | 449,471 | +10,224 | only rolling hills; no placeholder code |
  | one category: geometry | 1,547,577 | +31,848 | 451,521 | +12,274 | only geometry's 15 (14 found by name; "Cone" is too short to scan) |

  A game without the line has no dependency on the library: zero bytes. One asset carries the base (module, registry, mesh library upload: about 10 KB gzip) and that asset only.
- **Not done / follow-ups**: the 348 placeholders (category batches in the report); non-Realism styles; per-vertex colour and materials per asset; GPU generation for CPU assets; the wrapped grass in the Studio view has no trampling.

## Procedural realism round 9: object-local recipes, layered concrete, real relief (2026-11-04)

Chris's concrete spec (binding) and the round-9 brief.
- **Object-local position** (CORE_REQUESTS `object-local-position`, done): the recipe patch adds `local` and `lnorm` to the model stage's vertex output only where its vertex shader builds the mesh's own position; `MatIn` carries them (`local`, `ln`), `MatFrame` their derivatives, `mat_l2w` maps an object-space tangent to world space with no matrix. Modules without them pass the world position. Only recipe builds change.
- **Concrete** is plaster variant 5 drawn by its own part file (`rc_plaster_concrete.wgsl`, compiled with plaster): four layers in object space, the normal from the height (`rc_h2n`, shared), five presets as numbers (`surface::concrete_preset`), six diagnostic views in plaster's crack slot (concrete's cracks are geometry). Not done: Medium and Low baked maps; those tiers draw fewer layers.
- **Edge wear** (`detail::EdgeWear`, `edge_wear`, `box_arrises`): broken chips concentrated on a few arrises, most intact; `refine_near` (conforming longest-edge bisection) in place of 1-to-4 splits near a carving (an arris's slivers multiplied to 78,000 triangles).
- **Grass on a height grid** (CORE_REQUESTS `grass-heightfield`, done): `Grass::add_patch_on`, one storage buffer, bilinear in the blade pass; the ground carpet stays flat.
- **Ambient occlusion** reads its depth pyramid bilinearly (the stepped contact shadows were its whole-texel mip reads); the soft shadows' blocker search is bilinear; the depth of field ignores nearer taps.
- Wood stays inside its 2,638 B budget (exactly). No new dependency.
