## How to fold a helper's round into m1-foundation (2026-11-04)

- m1-foundation is checked out in the main checkout (`C:\dev\evani-dev`), which holds other people's uncommitted files, so nothing is committed or merged there. Take the lock (`mkdir <scratch>\evani-proc\fold.lock`; wait and retry while it exists). In your own worktree merge the latest m1-foundation into your branch, then run `cargo xtask check` and your tests. In a separate worktree (`git worktree add --detach <scratch>\evani-proc\wt-fold m1-foundation`, or `git checkout --detach m1-foundation` in the existing one) run `git merge --no-ff --no-commit <your branch>`, add the DECISIONS line `fold: <asset> round N, score X`, and commit. Move the branch with a compare-and-swap, `git update-ref refs/heads/m1-foundation <merge> <old m1-foundation>`. Then bring the main checkout's files up to date without committing: first check that none of the files the merge changes (`git diff --name-only <old> <merge>`) is among the main checkout's uncommitted ones (`git status --porcelain`; stop and ask if any is), then run `git read-tree -m -u <old> <merge>` in the main checkout (it refuses rather than overwrite a local edit). `git status` there then shows the same uncommitted files as before and nothing new. Rebuild the served Material library from the merge (`cargo xtask build material-view --ship --no-diff` in wt-fold; without `--no-diff` it then builds a per-module size report, about 80 more builds and hours, which Shorelines' round 2 fold left running on 2026-11-06), swap it into `.evani/serve/material-view`, capture your asset there once, remove the lock even on failure, and tell the orchestrator `folded <asset> round N, score X, commit <sha>`. Run the build in the foreground or wait for it before ending your turn: a background job still running at the end of a turn keeps the helper marked working, so Asset Studio holds its next round and the lock stays taken.

## Grass duplicates removed from the procedural library (2026-11-04)

- **Chris saw "Wild grass", "Dry grass" and "Grass clumps" (dark placeholder-looking previews) next to Short grass and Long grass, which already cover them.** Audit of the 15 Grass, plants and ground vegetation entries against Short grass (evani-grass lawn) and Long grass (evani-grass meadow), which carry height, height variation, density, lean, curl, stiffness, root, tip and dry colour, dryness, variation, clump, bare patches, wind and wetness: Wild grass (plain green blades, a meadow patch), Dry grass (straw-coloured, more bent blades: meadow with dryness up and the dry colour) and Grass clumps (tufts: meadow with clump up) are all reachable from Short or Long grass. They are **removed** (manifest, Cargo features, generator, tests, docs): the library is 357 assets, the category 12.
- **Kept, because each draws something Short and Long grass cannot:** Wildflowers (untouched, as asked), Flower beds (soil bed with flowers), Weeds (leaf rosettes with a seed stalk), Ferns (arching fronds with leaflets), Bushes and Shrubs (crowns, woody stems), Reeds (tall stiff blades with seed heads), Moss patches (flat ground blobs), Vines (climbing a post) and Ground cover plants (low leaf rosettes). The wheat plants (agriculture) and the muddy trampled ground kind of evani-grass are not in this category and stay.
- **Short grass and Long grass are untouched:** same params and presets, a picture and a parameter-panel readout before and after match. No reference to the three was left anywhere (no look, kit, example or `evani.toml` listed them). A game without the library is unchanged (the no-procedural build has no dependency on the crate).
- **Not mine, found on the way:** `cargo xtask check --quick`'s clippy step fails on m1-foundation itself (`proc_data::is_standin` is only used by the wasm build, so the native bin calls it dead now that no stand-in is left); `cargo xtask check` is clean.
- **Joined into m1-foundation (after the granite and faceted ball folds); gating proof like for like.** The no-procedural proc-field wasm (`GATE_ONLY=none`, rustc 1.99.1), built from m1-foundation 47fa645 and from this branch (f7a146f) in one folder with one target, is 1,515,607 B both times and differs only in the 7-character commit stamp (6 bytes). Re-checked on each newer m1-foundation it was joined onto (the granite fold 5e340a6, the faceted ball fold 2af754b): the none build is 1,515,607 B with and without this join's content (one folder, the same commit stamp) and byte for byte identical; cargo rebuilt nothing for it, as no file this join touches is in that build. The branch's first figure, 1,515,782 B, came from a build in another folder: the folder path is baked into the wasm 28 times, so wasm sizes from different folders never compare. Short grass and Long grass were captured headless before (the served copy) and after (this join) on a driven clock (the page's clock held while it loads and its materials prepare, then advanced exactly 150 frames), so the wind is at the same moment in both; two runs of one build give 0 changed pixels.
- **A target folder copied from another worktree is a trap.** Its cached `evani-xtask` keeps the folder it was compiled in (`EVANI_COMPILED_DIR`), so `cargo xtask build/check` there quietly builds and checks that other worktree; its cached evani-core keeps that worktree's commit stamp. Set `EVANI_ENGINE_ROOT=<this worktree>` and `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=<short hash>` (or start from an empty target) when reusing one.

- **Solid oak bytes (the oak block's live session, 2026-11-04).** Wood's byte budget rises by 1,020 B gzip (2,638 to 3,658; the test's count, `round4_growth`; round 1 of the session asked 760, round 3 measured 3,632). Round 9's oak scored 2 of 5 after five rounds: its rings were contours of one distance from a pith outside the piece, so every face showed even stripes and one big loop. Solid wood (variants 15 and 16) now has its own function (`rc_wood_solid`): a pith inside the piece, each year's ring its own width, rings wandering along the grain, an early-wood pore band widened to a pixel so end-grain rings stay visible, fibres as thin broken lines in the wood's volume at three scales, open pores, pin knots, hairline checks along the rays on the end grain and tone streaks, about 1 KB (round 3: the rays layer dropped, it did not show). Only games that list wood pay; the trim and the option of a `wood-solid` part (as `wood-layouts`) are open once the look is settled.

## Asset Studio: Photoreal and Realism are one style, kept as "photoreal" (2026-11-06)

- **Question (Chris).** The Asset Studio style picker said Photoreal; elsewhere the engine says Realism. Same art style or two?
- **Finding: the same style in Asset Studio, so merged.** The picker (tab `as1.js`) was the library's style strip (`kits/evani-kit-material-view/data/styles.json`: WK24 "Cinematic Realism", short name "Realism", `look: null`, `fidelity: "true"` = the engine's own physically based light, "natural colour") with a hand-added `photoreal` first. Both named one thing: every procedural library asset is built for WK24 first (`evani_procedural::REALISM`, `crates/evani-procedural/src/style.rs`), the realism pass's references were stored under `.../photoreal/` and tagged `look: photoreal` (generator "Evani Cloud picture (realism pass)", `apps/material-view/assets/proc-refs/`), and the references are neutral studio photographs. "Realism" there was never a second style id of its own (the id in the strip is WK24); the tab derived `realism` from its short name, so two options pointed at one style.
- **Not the same thing as the engine look.** The look `photoreal` ("Gritty photoreal", `catalog/looks.json`, `looks/evani-look-photoreal`: filmic tonemap + grade, saturation 0.88, haze) is the whole-world look and `realpbr` ("Realistic PBR", ACES, natural light) is a separate catalogue look. Neither is in the Asset Studio picker, neither changed, and WK24's own note keeps the look's daylight preset apart from per-material presets. No look, shader, parameter or guard file was touched.
- **Canonical id `photoreal`.** `realism`, `realistic`, `cinematicrealism`, `wk24` (and `photo-real`, which normalises to `photoreal`) are deprecated aliases: the tab's `STYLE_ALIAS` / `canonStyle` (v1.3.7) maps them, and nothing else (`realpbr` stays itself). One option shows in the picker (hint: "also called Realism"). Older saves load under Photoreal by themselves (the default): a column's style, its saved reference key, feed lines, a reference store saved as `refs.realism` (joins `refs.photoreal`; the kept entry wins, an older different picture goes to that asset's backups; the old key is left in place), and the `add_column` / `references` / column lookup arguments. Tags only: rounds, scores and notes are never rewritten. No column or store held the old tag at the time of the change.
- **Left alone on purpose.** The strip's own label "Realism" for WK24 in the material viewer, `"realism"` as the data key of the realism pass in `catalog/procedural/library.json`, and "realism pass" as a process name are not style ids.

## Evani.commons: asset versions shared on Evani.app (2026-11-06)

- **Goal (Chris).** "I want Evani.commons now full released with the upload feature that shares their version to Evani.app website for other Evani users to download as long as it is a better quality." Evani.commons is the Asset Studio tab as it ships inside Evani.App. Plan: `.vibedeck/plans/evani-commons-release.md`; the Evani.Dev side: `docs/EVANI_COMMONS.md`; the contract with Evani.App: its `docs/evani-commons.md`.
- **A version is code, not a baked mesh** (engine lightness): one asset x one style as a folder `evani-commons/1`: the round's diff against the engine commit it was built on plus the touched files' base copies (for a 3-way merge), params, the independent score and its reviewer, the reference and round JPEGs, MIT licence and author, a content hash over every file. The clouds' round 5: 115 KB of code, 44 KB of pictures.
- **Only library code travels, and only safe code.** Paths: the procedural library, its base, the material crates, the grass module, the proof game's dev scenes, `catalog/procedural/library.json`. A Cargo.toml may change only `[features]`; no Cargo.lock, build.rs, binaries or renames; added Rust may not use process, net, fs, env, os, ffi, unsafe, extern, link, include. Strangers' code is built on the adopter's PC and on the server; the procedural library needs none of these. The exporter, the importer and the server all check.
- **The server decides** (the owner's choice, relayed 2026-11-06): it renders every upload itself with hidden cameras and scores it with its own reviewer; the tab's "likely to pass" (independent score above the published server score, or the 3.0 floor) is a hint. Only the owner's click on Evani.App's Share card uploads.
- **Adopting is all or nothing.** `cargo xtask commons import` plans every file, merges a file the project changed 3-way, writes nothing on any conflict, undoes itself when the project check turns unclean, records the version in `catalog/procedural/commons.json` and never copies package pictures into the project.
- **No one PC in the tab.** The project folder, worktree folder (default `<project>/.evani/worktrees`), main branch, run-low path, reviewer account and the owner's safety text come from the tab's settings, then the install's `local.js` (empty in the shipped bundle `tools/evani-commons-tab/`; this PC's in `.vibedeck/asset-studio/local.js`), then generic defaults. A column keeps the worktree folder it started with. The guide uses `<project>`, `<worktrees>`, `<main>`, `<run-low>`, filled in by the tab.
- **New dependency (tools only, never in a game).** `jpeg-encoder =0.7.1` (xtask; the package's round and reference pictures as small JPEGs; pure Rust, no dependencies, no default features, `std`).

## Asset Studio: a reference shows the asset the way a game shows it (reference classes) (2026-11-06)
- **Problem (Chris).** "I am not sure these are the right images to get the outcome of a procedural engine that works for games, and maybe there are other assets like wind that you can not take a picture of": the sun and moon reference was two studio spheres on grey, the sky dome a glass dome on a table.
- **Cause.** One prompt wording for every asset (the tab's `refPrompt`, copied by Evani.App's commons seed: "Studio photo of X, whole object in frame, three-quarter view, neutral grey backdrop"), and nothing in the catalogue said how an asset is seen in a game.
- **Decision.** Three reference classes, `ref_class` in `catalog/procedural/library.json` (per category, per asset where it differs), their meaning in `catalog/procedural/ref_classes.json`: **object** (studio still, the old wording byte for byte; 287 assets), **scene** (a ground-level player-camera still with set eye height, field of view, horizon and time of day; 66: terrain, water, sky, roads, plus scree, rock walls, arches, grass fields, forest, canopies, crop rows), **behaviour** (a standard test scene as four frames 0.5 s apart plus a measurable spec; 4: wind gusts, water currents, skeletal rigs, face morphs). The tab's prompt, author and reviewer briefs and reference box follow the class; the reviewer judges scenes from the game camera and behaviour on the frames plus each measured value against its range. `tools/procedural/gen_ref_classes.mjs` writes the tab's `classes.js` and the guide's table (`--check` for drift). Guide: docs/ASSET_STUDIO_GUIDE.md "Reference classes".
- **Old references (Chris's default).** Studio-made references of scene and behaviour assets are kept and flagged "needs new reference"; nothing is deleted, no round or score changes. Sky columns with a flagged reference pause through the tab's Stop until their new reference is stored (then they carry on from their last finished round); other flagged columns (shorelines, canyons) carry on and their authors are told to aim at the class's target.

## View-model depth marking and a raw-mouse lock (2026-11-07, TopGun Tom request)

- **Closes the accepted gap "depth-reading post effects do not see it" (S5-E3), for games that opt in.** `ViewModel::mark_depth` (evani-render `view-model`, default false). When on and some enabled pass reads `depth`, a `view_model_mark_depth` step after the view-model pass (and after the 4x depth resolve, before the glass pass) writes depth 1.0 (nearest, reversed-Z) into the scene depth where the view model drew. Chosen over a depth-only redraw of the meshes (a second vertex stream, instance and light bindings) and over a stencil mask (a stencil format on the scene depth for every game): the view-model pass already has its own depth, cleared to 0, so any value above 0 is coverage; the pass keeps it (Store instead of Discard, plus `TEXTURE_BINDING`) and one full-screen triangle with compare Always and discard on 0 copies the coverage as 1.0. Cost: one triangle and a read of one depth texture, only while on.
- **Off costs nothing and changes nothing.** The pipeline, bind group and the readable depth usage are made only when the option is first on; off, the depth texture has the usage and the pass the store op it always had, no pass is added, no shader is compiled. The new code is inside the `view-model` feature (no new feature, no new dependency); a game without `view-model` carries none of it. The gate in `view_model.rs` tests (`marks_depth`, the reference against the WGSL's words, naga validation). wgpu links only on wasm32, so the pass itself is checked by wasm32 `cargo check` and clippy and by the CPU reference; there is no native GPU test.
- **Still not covered when on:** a view-model pixel is marked as a whole (no partial coverage on edges, as the view model has no MSAA); only the first split-screen view's viewport is drawn, so only its pixels are marked.
- **Raw mouse (`PointerLock::set_raw_mouse`, evani-core `pointer-lock`, default off).** `requestPointerLock({ unadjustedMovement: true })` through js-sys (the typed option is behind a web-sys unstable flag); a rejected promise takes a plain lock and sets `raw_denied()` instead of reporting a refusal. No new dependency.
- Ideas from UE 5.5 First Person Rendering and Unity URP's FPS sample; no code copied.

## Evani.commons auto-send and the trusted reviewer models (2026-11-07, Asset Studio 1.5.12)

- **The owner's rule** (Chris, 2026-11-07): "we only trust rankings like gradings from Anthropic and OpenAI models. Opus 5.5 or higher, Fable 5.1 or higher, Sol 6.1 or higher and Astra or higher. That's it." The one list is `TRUSTED_REVIEWERS` in `tools/evani-commons-tab/autosend.js`, described in docs/ASSET_STUDIO_GUIDE.md 2.4; Evani.App's server applies the same list. Any other model, an unknown model or version, and the author's own score never count for Evani.commons. Versions compare part by part (Opus 5.5, 5.6 and 6 count; Sol 6.0 doesn't). Reviewer models were already recorded with every score (`round.reviewer.model`, the feed's `model`).
- **Auto-send** (his card answers: send automatically, any improvement counts, on for everyone as a setting they can switch off, catch up once): a trusted score above the best version on Evani.app for that asset and look (nothing published counts as lower; the site's first-version floor still applies) runs the existing Pack round flow and then `evani.commons.autoShare`, a no-click share Evani.App adds on its existing `commons` ability (no new tab permission; agreed with this project's orchestrator and Evani.App's, 2026-11-07). Each round is sent once (`CM.sent`, keyed `<asset>@<style>/c<column>r<round>`); a failure is shown and never retried by itself; an Evani.App without `autoShare` says "needs your click". Uploads still go through the server's render, score and approval queue.
- **Why the Cone (column #19, Photoreal) showed "not rated", "nothing published yet" and "no independently scored round yet"**: column #19 never ran a round (0 rounds on the built-in tab's board; it was later switched to Mountains, also 0 rounds). The Cone's real scores (4.0 in the 2026-11-05 folds) come from the loop before Asset Studio and live in DECISIONS.md, not in any board round, and the tab's ratings count board rounds only. Nothing was ever published for it because sharing was a manual Pack + Share click and no one pressed it. The same is true of every scored asset: the custom Asset Studio tab has no commons bridge (sharing only exists in the built-in Evani.commons tab), and the scored columns were cleared from the board (2026-11-06 20:53, kept in `.evani/tmp/refclass/board-backup`) before the board moved to the built-in tab, so no package or share was ever made (`pkgs` and `subs` empty).

## Asset Studio 1.5.20: plateau rule, notes for the next round, run state in every prompt, reviewer retry and trusted fallback (2026-11-07)

Why: Mountains (column 19) sat at 3.0 for rounds 4 to 6 while its author polished details, though it knew the cause (the player view needs a foothill stand point the scene lacked); an orchestrator's note to a finished helper only arrived when the tab next started it; helpers stopped on an old "stop" in their chat; a reviewer that crashed waited for someone to restart it.
- Plateau (new `robust.js`): a column whose independent score has not risen for 2 rounds in a row is on a plateau. Every message the tab sends its author starts with a PLATEAU block (the flat rounds, the gap the reviewer keeps repeating, change approach on it: structure, framing or method, not detail polish; first step line "Different this round: ... because ..."), and its reviewer is told to put the single biggest blocker first ("Blocker: ...") and say whether the round addressed it; that line becomes the next gap. After 4 rounds without a gain the column stops ("plateau: no gain in 4 rounds (best X in round N, kept)"); the owner's Go counts afresh. Shown on the column, its badge, the run summary and the `columns` read (`plateau`).
- Notes inbox: action `column_note { col, text, from, to }` and a box on each column. Notes live in their own storage key `inbox` (read, add, write, read back: a board save can't drop one); delivery marks in the loop record (`LOOP.inboxDone`, written only by the loop's copy). Each pending note is pasted at the top of the next launch brief or message to that helper under "NOTES FOR THIS ROUND" and marked delivered only when that start or send went through. Evani.App refuses `agents.send` to a helper mid-turn (only queues it behind a background job), so live delivery stays the orchestrator's own message path: `column_note` answers which helper is working now.
- Run state: one wrapper (`robustWrap`, in `startOnce`, `sendTo` and the reviewer's request sends) puts COLUMN STATE (running, or stopped and why) at the top of every launch and message; both briefs say an older "stop" in chat doesn't apply unless the tab says the column is stopped. A helper that ends its turn on a yes/no question its column's state answers gets the tab's answer (at most 2 a round), not a reminder count or a takeover.
- Reviewer: 2 retries on its model (30 s, 90 s), then the next trusted model in its chain (trustOf, the one list in autosend.js), each with the same tries; an unavailable model moves at once; the column stops only after every trusted model failed. Before: a move after 2 failures and a stop after 3. Each retry and move is shown on the column with its reason. Authors keep their 3 tries.
- Start time limit: on 7 Nov the tab's loop was "let go" twice (13:41 to 13:47, 13:46 to 13:51), both while column 20's author start went unanswered ("its start never began"). `agents.start` had no limit, so one unanswered start held the whole reconcile pass until the supervisor's 3 min watchdog. Now `startTimed` waits at most `START_WAIT` (2 min, under the watchdog) and then raises a plain timed-out error, which the tab already treats as an uncertain start: the marker stays, `resolvePending` finds the helper in `agents.list()`, and the same requestId and key keep a late start from making a second helper. Other columns carry on meanwhile.
- Manifest: the new action `column_note` and the `plateau` field of the `columns` read; no ability or permission is widened. Built on the installed 1.5.19 (the sends fix: autosend.js, commons.js), which this version keeps as it is.
- Checked: the tab harness in headless, muted Chrome, the new group RB (plateau count and rules, notes stored, pasted and marked delivered, live helpers named, run state in launch prompts and messages, answers to state questions, reviewer retries and trusted fallback) and every earlier group; U4 and LP5 now expect the new reviewer rule. On the exact 1.5.20 install set (installed 1.5.19 plus these files): the full harness 817/818; its one miss (W "After Go: none says waiting for Go") passes 143/143 on a re-run and fails the same way on the installed 1.5.19, so it is an older timing race; new group SW (a late start frees the loop, one helper, no "let go") with every always-run group 104/104; H 100/100; RB 135/135. The installed 1.5.19 alone stops at U4 (that check now expects the new reviewer rule).

## Evani.commons: the package names the item's reference, not its preview (2026-11-08)

- Cause of the refused Mountains sends (r11, r12: "made against a different reference picture than the item's locked one"): the exporter wrote `reference.sha256` as the hash of the re-encoded `reference.jpg` preview (Mountains fa721c48…), while Evani.App's contract (its docs/evani-commons.md 2.3, protocol `checkCommonsFiles`) and server compare it with the item's reference file itself. The server already held the new two-view picture (1bc9ce43…, the column's own). Every PNG reference was refused this way.
- Fix: `reference.sha256` is the SHA-256 of the `--reference` file's own bytes; `source_sha256` stays the picture the round was scored against. `--locked-sha256 <hex>` (the item card's `reference_sha256`, which the tab passes to its packer from 1.5.25): when it isn't the scored picture's hash, the export finds that file in the history of `apps/material-view/assets/proc-refs/<asset>.jpg` (what the first 14 Official items were seeded from on 2026-11-06) and names it only when it is the same picture (mean difference on a 64 x 64 grid at most 4 of 255; the real JPEG copies measure under 1: Office 0.41, Pebbles 0.26, Shorelines 0.38, Oak 0.93, Rolling hills 0.38, Cube 0.41). Otherwise it refuses: naming the locked picture would claim a score the round wasn't given (Clouds: its column now scores against the new player-camera sky, the server still has the old studio cloud).
- **New dependency (tools only, never in a game).** `jpeg-decoder =0.3.2` (xtask; decodes the locked JPEG for that same-picture check; pure Rust, no dependencies without its default `rayon`).

## Building blocks: a landscape waits for the blocks it is made of (Asset Studio 1.5.26) (2026-11-08)

- **Context.** Chris (2026-11-08), "like a football tournament bracket": a landscape is built from blocks (trees need bark; landscapes need trees, grass, rock and sky), and every block must reach the goal score before the landscape that uses it. Later the same day: rock builds up by size (pebbles → boulders → mountain), bark → trees is its own branch, a block is a child only if it is a real visual ingredient of its parent (no grass in the sky), chains may merge where the mix is itself an ingredient (mud + grass → riverbank → rivers), every link carries a one-line why, and every landscape in the catalogue is worked back from its reference picture.
- **Decision.** The graph is catalogue data, `catalog/procedural/blocks.json` (Chris chose the catalogue over tab-only data): `needs.<parent>` = `[{ block, why }]`; a block is a library asset key, `material:<id>` (catalog/materials/materials.json, e.g. `material:bark.oak`) or `planned:<id>` (a merge or part with no procedural asset yet: shown as not started, never given a column, ready once its own blocks are done). 25 landscapes (all 15 terrain assets and the 10 water places), 80 blocks, 12 planned merges, each tree marked with its evidence (picture, framing or name); the whole set is a draft for Chris to review. No new procedural assets.
- **Checks.** `tools/procedural/gen_blocks.mjs` refuses unknown ids, a missing or multi-line why, duplicates, self-links, unused planned blocks and cycles (with the cycle's path in names) and writes the tab's copy `tools/evani-commons-tab/blockdata.js` and the guide's table (`--check` for drift); `node --test tools/procedural/gen_blocks.test.mjs`; `crates/evani-procedural-lib` `blocks_tests` (so `check --full` guards the catalogue).
- **The tab (1.5.26, blocks.js).** Picking a landscape opens its bracket (leaves left, landscape right; status and best trusted score per block in the column's style). Done = best trusted score (2.4's list) at the Goal at the top. Go on a column with no rounds whose blocks aren't done doesn't start: it waits ("waiting for blocks"), names the blocking blocks with their whys, adds a column per missing block, starts those whose own blocks are done through the normal Go (At once still applies) and starts by itself once its blocks are done. Columns with rounds are never gated; their missing blocks are added once as idle columns. New read `blocks`; the `columns` read gains `blocks_ready`, `blocked_by`, `waiting_for_blocks`, `block_for`.
- **No new dependencies.**

## Asset Studio 1.5.27: plateau-test loop strategies, switched per column; standard stays the default (2026-11-08)

- Why: columns stop at 3.0-3.5 with "plateau: no gain in 4 rounds". Diagnosis (docs/PLATEAU_AB.md): 78 of 100 consecutive reviews repeat the same half-star score; 36% of reviews say the reviewer's own measurements were blocked; each request shows "Earlier scores" and the guide tells the reviewer not to move without numbers; every round builds on the last round, not the best; Scree slopes measured steady gains (luminance SD 31.9 to 42.6 vs 42.9) through five rounds all scored 3.0; Rolling hills' reference is a studio tile for a scene asset.
- What: `plateau.js` (strategies standard, combined, lean, best3, blocker from five parts: best-of-3 variants from the best version, two averaged review passes with the history withheld, one measured blocker, the tab's own measurements in `metrics.js`, a new plan after 2 rounds without a 0.25 gain), a Loop picker per column, the actions `loop_trial` (1-5 rounds through the column's own author and reviewer, one trial column at a time, then "trial finished"), `noise_check` / `submit_rescore`, and the read `trial`. Trial rounds are never auto-sent (`trustedBest`) and never folded. Ideas only from the five researched sources; no code ported.
- Outcome so far: built and tested (harness 359/359); the live trials wait for Chris's Restart & update of the built-in Evani.commons tab. No strategy is rolled out: Chris decides after the trials.

## Typed building-block links: every link says how the child feeds its parent, and the engine assembles from it (Asset Studio 1.5.33) (2026-11-08)

- **Context.** The building-block graph (1.5.26) recorded only that a child feeds a parent. Chris (2026-11-08) asked that every link record how ("shown and used by the engine") and confirmed the defaults: snow on high, flat ground; moss in low, shady cracks; small objects scattered sparsely.
- **Decision.** `catalog/procedural/blocks.json` version 2: each link is `{ block, why, kind, params }` with three kinds. `layer` = a material blended into the parent's surface by a mask: `mask` (terms `{ by: slope | height | curvature | noise, min?, max?, scale? }`: slope in degrees, height a fraction of the parent's height span, curvature -1..1 with below 0 concave, noise 0..1), `blend` (0..1], `falloff` (0..1, a fraction of each term's range) and the engine `condition` layer that draws it. `scatter` = instanced copies: `density` per m², `scale` [min, max], `lod` and `impostor` metres (0 = none), optional `slope`, `height` bands and `avoid_water`. `base` = the parent's shape: `join` merge (into its own meshes, never a new draw), part (its own draw: sky, sea, a separate piece) or surface (the material or stone it wears; also the rock chain by size, a stone proven on pebbles). Masks use the four terms Chris named; moss's low light is stood in for by concave curvature (no light or occlusion term). A planned block is a grouping: its links apply to the parent inside the mask of the layer that brought it.
- **Defaults and migration.** Untyped links (version 1) get defaults (`defaultEdge` in `tools/procedural/gen_blocks.mjs`): snow `height > 0.6, slope < 35°`, blend 0.9, condition snow; moss `height < 0.4, curvature < -0.1`, blend 0.8, condition growth; pebbles and small stones 0.4 per m², other scatters sparse by size; materials = base surface; sky, fog, sea, scree, splashes, walls = base part; terrains, rock walls, ocean waves = base merge. `--migrate` writes them (backing the file up to `.evani/tmp/block-edges/backup/`); the stored catalogue must be typed (`--check` refuses an untyped link) while the tab still reads an older copy with the same defaults, shown as defaults. Hand-set after the migration: tidal mud as a mud layer on low ground, marsh grass as a noise layer, the plateau's plain as its own part.
- **Engine.** `evani_procedural::compose` assembles an asset from its links: layers become `Surface::condition` layers on the parent's surfaced, non-card parts (the existing per-surface layering; no new mesh, no shader change), scatters seeded placements over the parent's ground (`Assembly::place` into `ProcScene`), base links merge, place or dress. gen_blocks writes the graph as Rust data (`crates/evani-procedural-lib/src/blocks_table.rs`, feature `compose`, so no game downloads it unless it asks); a `Composition` resource makes `ProcModule` draw each placed asset with its layers and base joins. No JSON is parsed at run time.
- **Missing paths (listed in `Assembly::missing`, not invented).** A layer with no condition layer (a second catalogue material blended by a mask: turf's loam, marsh grass, the planned meadows); a catalogue material as a surface (its 32-byte block is not compiled in); per-link height, curvature and noise masks in the shader (the condition shader masks snow by slope only, via the global `material.cond.snow.angle`; the masks are evaluated on the CPU and carried); scatter LOD and impostor distances (no draw path reads them); a composed parent isn't remade when only a child's params change.
- **Checks.** gen_blocks refuses unknown kinds, missing or unknown params, out-of-range values, a scattered or merged material, and cycles, each with a plain error (`node --test tools/procedural/gen_blocks.test.mjs`); evani-procedural-lib `blocks_tests` has the same schema check in Rust and runs it on the catalogue; `compose_tests` proves Mountains with snow and moss assembles as one mesh with two material layers, only scatter links make instances, and the engine table matches the catalogue link for link. The tab (1.5.33, blocks.js) labels each link in the tree ("blend: slope > 35°", "scatter: 0.4/m²", "base"), checked at 1280, 700 and 2560 px (`tools/studio/commons-tab-test/blocks.mjs` group B8).
- **No new dependencies.**

- **Scenes become fly-around Scenes on Evani.app (Chris, 2026-11-08).** "Make it a rule that all Scenes become scenes in Evani.app website that you can free roam with like a flying thing"; "playgrounds are game examples, Scenes are things like the sun, moon and meadow". Every scene item gets a Scene (free-flying camera, no goals, keys/mouse + touch, under 10 MB), published only on Chris's click; first is the Sun and moon meadow (CLAUDE.md, docs/SCENES.md).

## Netcode sync layer: prediction, reconciliation, smoothing and snapshot interpolation in the engine (2026-11-10)

- **Why.** The owner: "this has been a problem before so we need to make sure that we cover this inside the Evani.dev engine 'The online game shows raw server updates with no smoothing or prediction of the player's car.'" Engine only for now; the kart racer is not changed. Root cause: evani-net handed kits the bare predicted state (`Client::predicted`, `LockstepClient::display`) and snapshot poses that hold when updates run late (`PoseHistory::sample`, no extrapolation, fixed delay); the one fix (`NetSmooth`, 2026-10-29) lived in the kart kit and docs/NET_BRIDGE_GUIDE.md described corrections only as replays. So each online kit had to invent smoothing.
- **What.** New evani-net feature `sync` (`src/sync.rs`, docs/NET_SYNC.md): `Predictor` (fixed-tick prediction of the local entity with sequence-numbered inputs in an `InputHistory`; each authoritative snapshot rewinds to the server state and replays inputs after the ack; the server stays authoritative), `ErrorSmoother` (a correction becomes a render offset decaying by `e^(-rate dt)`; cut over the snap threshold), `SnapshotBuffer` (remote entities by server time, drawn `net.interp_delay_ms` behind, the delay growing with RFC 3550-style measured jitter up to 500 ms, a render clock slewed at most 10 %, capped extrapolation, late snapshots eased in). Pose maths through a small `Offset` trait (`f32`, `[f32; N]`, `Angle`, pairs; a pair's first part sets the size).
- **Defaults (owner-confirmed brief: take them).** Render delay 100 ms adapting to jitter (`net.sync.jitter_scale` 2); extrapolation cap 200 ms; smoothing rate 12 /s (95 % gone in 250 ms); snap threshold 3 m (blend smoothly, jump only for large errors). New live parameters, registered only with `sync`: `net.sync.smooth_rate`, `net.sync.snap_threshold`, `net.sync.extrapolate_max_ms`, `net.sync.jitter_scale`; the least delay reuses the existing `net.interp_delay_ms` rather than adding a second delay parameter.
- **On/off.** A Cargo feature of evani-net beside `lockstep` and `port`, turned on from the app's `net` feature (`"evani-net/sync"`), the same way the kart racer turns on `lockstep`; evani.toml keeps `net = true` (no new evani.toml key). Without it nothing of the layer is compiled and no parameter is registered; a game without `net` builds no evani-net at all. Proof (match-3, `cargo xtask build match-3 --ship` from 7cc12b97 and from this branch): every shipped file the same size (830,447 bytes in all), the js identical, the wasm (698,646 bytes) differing only in the 7-character commit stamp it carries (`7cc12b9` / `1bdd8b7`, 6 bytes), index.html and build-facts.json only in the names and hashes that follow from it. The crate's tests turn it on through a dev-dependency on itself, so `cargo test -p evani-net` always covers it while normal builds are untouched.
- **No new dependencies.** Plain std; no wall clock (the game passes tick-derived times), no random numbers.
- **Prior art (ideas, not code).** Gabriel Gambetta, "Fast-Paced Multiplayer" (client prediction with sequence numbers, server reconciliation, entity interpolation); Glenn Fiedler, "Snapshot Interpolation" and "State Synchronization" (gafferongames.com: a buffer sized to send rate and jitter, visual error smoothing); RFC 3550 section 6.4.1 (the interarrival jitter estimator).
- **Stage.** Stage 3's multiplayer engine build (STAGES.md: Chris, 2026-10-24, "fully build the Stage 3 multi-player engine"); multiplayer stays listed in Stages 5 and 9. Out of scope: lag compensation, transport, matchmaking, peer-to-peer rollback, wiring it into Sugarpeak.

- New params, each with a default that leaves the picture as it was:
  - `sky.disc_skirt_flat`: the aureole's skirt lies along the horizon, this many times wider than tall (1 round), a flattened oval and not a column over a setting sun. `sky.disc_glow_sun`: how far the aureole keeps the low sun's own deep orange above the sun (0 the view line's paler colour). `sky.disc_broad`, `sky.disc_broad_width`: a faint broad third lobe, the haze's brightening of the whole sky on the sun's side.

- Changed without a param, for every scene with `sky.discs` on (this asset's recipe, the proof game's `sunmoon` scene and the Sun and moon meadow Scene; nothing else turns the part on): the moon is no longer 16 point samples but its lit strip's exact share of each pixel (six lines towards the light, a tent's cumulative weight from the terminator to the limb), so a thin crescent has no beads; the sun's white core is even out to `disc_core_size` of the radius and gone within an eighth of the radius either side (before, it faded evenly from the centre to the rim); the disc's outline is smoothed over two pixels or at least 0.15 of its radius (0.22 before). ## Smoothness harness: frame pacing and motion steadiness as an engine tool (2026-11-11)

- **Why.** APEX Velocity shipped online with its car juddering on half of all frames, and only a one-off harness written for that game found and proved it. Root cause (5 Whys, measured): no engine check measures how evenly things move on screen; nothing exposes where things are drawn each frame (`RenderWorld` is rebuilt and cleared every frame, the live API had no position command, telemetry is averaged over periods); and the engine's local host (`tools/evani-host`) delivers on a perfect beat, so uneven relay delivery never happens in a test browser.
- **What.** `cargo xtask smoothness <id> [--baseline <build>] [--candidate <build>] [--net none|lan|wan|bad]` (docs/SMOOTHNESS.md). A dev build is driven by synthetic CDP keys in headless, muted Chrome on the GPU (`tools/bench-runner/chrome.mjs`, its GPU lock and throwaway profile); per presented frame it records the frame time (`tools/live-check/frame-gaps.mjs` hook) and where the game's probe was drawn. Analysis (ported from APEX's `.evani/tmp/stutter/analyze.mjs` and `chart.mjs`): each frame's speed over the mean of its +-7 neighbours within 140 ms (steady = 1), frames outside 0.6..1.4 uneven; frame intervals against 60 or 120 Hz; the longest stall split into the game's own work and the browser holding the page. Output: `result.json` (`evani-smoothness/1`), `report.html` (steadiness chart, frame-time chart, table view; Before and After overlaid). Exit 1 over the limits, 2 when the run cannot be made.
- **Genre-agnostic.** The engine tracks a probe, never a kart: `camera_target`, `camera_eye`, a `mesh` (id and/or material, nearest the camera target) or a `sprite` (cell and/or layer). The game's `smoothness.json` beside its evani.toml names the probe, the metric (world or screen), the start and drive keys, its own limits and its networked setup. Kart racer: `apps/kart-racer/smoothness.json` (probe: the chase camera's target; the camera's own smoothing damps part of the kart's judder, so a mesh probe on the kart body is the stricter choice when its material is known).
- **Engine hook through the live API, behind a feature.** New live commands `motion.trace`, `motion.read`, `motion.stop` (LIVE_API.md 6.32; `crates/evani-live/src/motion.rs`): a `live.motion` frame system at the end of `Stage::Frame` copies the probe's position from that frame's `RenderWorld` into a preallocated buffer (default 36,000 frames). It lives in evani-live, the dev-only `live` module every `--ship` build drops, so no new engine feature flag and no parallel channel: the runner calls it through the in-page `window.evani.live.call`, which works without the bridge.
- **Networked mode.** The game's own headless referee (`net.referee_package`, built as bridges/chimpvibe/build.mjs does) runs in `tools/evani-host/server.mjs`, the engine's reference host (the local authoritative-host stand-in), behind `tools/smoothness/relay.mjs`: a protocol-agnostic TCP relay holding back what the host sends by base + exponential jitter + an occasional hiccup, in order, seeded. Profiles: `lan`, `wan` (APEX's model: 22 ms + jitter mean 6 + 70 ms one chunk in 90), `bad`. The net sync layer (docs/NET_SYNC.md) is what games use to draw well under this; the harness measures whether they do, so it does not link the layer itself.
- **Default limits (owner-confirmed: from the APEX fixed build with small headroom).** APEX's four fixed-build traces (`..\APEX\.evani\perf\stutter\after\trace-after-*.json`, read only) re-analysed with this harness reproduce APEX's numbers (uneven 0 to 0.038 %, ratio SD 0.010 to 0.024) and give the worst case: uneven 0.038 %, ratio deviation p99 0.042, SD 0.024, longest frame 116.6 ms, hitches 1. Defaults: `uneven_pct_max` 0.1, `ratio_dev_p99_max` 0.06, `ratio_sd_max` 0.04, `frame_max_ms` 150, `hitches_max` 2. A run with under 60 moving frames fails (nothing measured).
- **Sample (kart racer online, `--net wan`, 20 s at 1280 px).** Before: a scratch build with the kart racer's `NetSmooth` bypassed (raw lockstep state; never committed); After: the kart racer as it is. Uneven frames 0.894 % -> 0.278 %, ratio SD 0.096 -> 0.082, deviation p99 0.343 -> 0.318; both over the default limits, as is the kart racer as it is (a finding for the game, not fixed here: out of scope). On this shared PC, runs while other helpers render show 1 to 3 s stalls at random times in either build; the stall split shows them as the browser holding the page (2 to 3 ms of game work inside), so compare runs made under the same load. Report and screenshot: `.evani/shots/smoothness-harness/`.
- **Ship proof.** `cargo xtask build kart-racer --ship` from m1-foundation 75f01829 (a clean detached checkout) and from this branch, each with `EVANI_ENGINE_ROOT` set to its own checkout and `EVANI_GIT_COMMIT=proof0`: 11 files, 10 byte for byte the same by SHA-256 (the wasm 1,167.3 KB raw / 499.8 KB gzip, the js, index.html, ENGINE-LICENSE.txt, the models, both snippets); `build-facts.json` differs only in its `commit` stamp and the `uncommitted_engine_changes` flag beside it (1 byte in 1,447,422). A first try without `EVANI_ENGINE_ROOT` and a shared target folder built this branch twice (xtask finds the engine from its executable), so the root must be pinned for such a proof.
- **AI guide.** One line in the AGENTS.md engine block (tools/evani-guide/guide/AGENTS.md, item 9); to stay under the block's 8,192-byte cap the geocheck item now points to docs/GEOCHECK.md for kit adapters instead of naming them. `cargo xtask init-ai` takes about 6 minutes with one build job (it builds the live bridge) and prints nothing meanwhile.
- **No new dependencies.** Node built-ins only (node:test, http, net); Rust: none.
- **Stage.** A dev and test tool for Stage 3's online play (the multiplayer engine build and the net sync layer, STAGES.md: Chris 2026-10-24); no gate box is ticked by it. It is a tool agents choose to run, not an automatic gate.

## The 10 MB download cap is for games only: the library, Scenes, viewers and tools have none (2026-11-11)

- **Owner's words (Chris, 2026-11-11, relayed by the orchestrator):** "the Library is not limited to the 10 MB that is only for games Library has no limit", then "Please ensure it is known that the 10mb is only for Games that is it".
- **Rule:** The 10 MB download cap applies only to games (and playgrounds, which are game examples); the library, Scenes, viewers and tools have no size cap.
- **Why now:** the Material library (apps/material-view, served by `cargo xtask library build`) is a `[playground]`, so `build --ship` held it to the game cap; after column 68's fold it was 9.97 of 10.00 MB with 33,222 bytes left, and the next asset fold would have failed. The cap was never meant for it.
- **How:** one function decides, `evani_guide::playground::size_cap(app, evani.toml)`: `Some(PACKAGE_CAP_BYTES)` (10 MiB, unchanged) for a game or playground; `None` for a tool app (`kind = "tool"`, which already needs the appkind proof that it has no gameplay: the material library) or a Scene (`scene-<name>`, docs/SCENES.md). A missing or broken `kind` counts as a game, so nothing slips out of the cap by mistake. Its users: `build --ship`'s guard (prints `package: X MB (...; no size cap)` for an uncapped app and never refuses it; a game still prints `of 10.00 MB cap` and fails over it), `check`'s last-ship-build warning (games only), and `publish`'s preflight, size report and summary (`cap_bytes: null`, "not a game, so no size cap"). `library build`/`library check` never had the cap; Evani.App's own library limits (400 files, 16 MB a file, 64 MB in all) are unchanged. The model viewer has no `[playground]` and is never published, so it was never capped.
- **Unchanged for games:** `PACKAGE_CAP_BYTES`, its error, fix line and test (`package_cap_is_ten_mib_on_disk`), and Evani.App's 10 MB check on a game's upload.
- **Tests:** `playground::tests::only_games_have_the_size_cap` (a game and a playground get the cap, also with a bad `kind`; the real material-view manifest and a `scene-` id get none) and `publish_tests` (the same 10 MB + 1 byte folder is refused for a game and passes, saying "no size cap", for an uncapped app).
- **Written in:** AGENTS.md's engine block (source `tools/evani-guide/guide/AGENTS.md`, `app.md`), CLAUDE.md "Scenes on Evani.app", docs/PLAYGROUNDS.md, SCENES.md, PUBLISHING.md, EVANI_COMMONS.md section 8, README.
- **Bytes:** tools and docs only; no shipped file changes.

## Fold: distance fog (Asset Studio column 77) round 1, score 4.0 (the tab's independent scored review, 75 of 100 in categories; the library's distance fog before it: unscored) (2026-11-11)

- fold: distance fog round 1, score 4.0 (asset-studio/col77-distance-fog-19mlffo befdb9e1, m1-foundation 7a36052b merged in: the round as it was scored is 22c72941). The library's `sky-distance-fog` was five stacked see-through sheets (params area, depth, color). It is now the air's own fog, worked out for every pixel from how far away and how high the thing behind it is: one full-screen game pass after the opaque 3D (`procedural.distance_fog`, evani-procedural-lib `crate::fog`), hosted by the procedural module whenever the asset is compiled in, as the volumetric clouds' volume is. A game that lists the asset and places it once gets the fog; the placement's height is the fog's floor.
- What the fog does: clear air round the eye (the density rises smoothly from half `start` to one and a half), an exponential fog along the ground that loses 95% of a thing at `visibility`, with a long faint tail (far things never snap out), a ground layer `height` metres deep over a share that stays at every height (the mean along the view ray in closed form, so a far pillar's foot is more lost than its top), the sky in the fog's colour, a colour a little darker along the horizon and darker again looking down at the ground, a depth-aware softening of the edges of far things (never into nearer ones), and a fine grain in place of bands.
- Params. The asset's own (`procedural.sky.distance_fog.*`): visibility 55 m, start 8 m, height 6 m, color 0.643/0.665/0.727; the old area and depth are gone with the sheets (no look, kit, game or Scene set them; the catalogue's building blocks name the asset only as a part). The pass's (`procedural.distance_fog.*`): aloft 0.5, tail 0.09, reach 8, sky 1, horizon 0.13, rise 0.22, ground 0.1, dip 0.05, soft 0.003, grain 0.009. The generator's CPU mesh is only the fog bank's bounds (384 triangles), for tests and a host without the pass.
- Nothing shared changes another asset: `crate::fog` and its hosting line are compiled only with the feature `sky-distance-fog`, which now also turns on evani-render's `game-passes` (as the clouds' feature does). A game that does not list the asset is unchanged.
